items.title: The avatar path is held until the engines have a model path, and after W554 no open row held that obligation at all
items.why: Found W555 by checking my own previous round. W554 closed FU-357 by amending P3.16's third ACCEPT clause: the avatar path is HELD until the engines have a model path (P3.20), on the Owner's decision, rather than wired now - because the loop WITHHOLDS every emission today, so wiring it would turn a chat surface that answers into one that deliberately delivers nothing. The amendment is right and it is recorded. WHAT WAS WRONG IS THAT NOTHING CARRIED THE DEFERRED WORK FORWARD: FU-357 was closed, no open row mentioned the avatar path or avatar_interface.py, and the obligation existed only as prose inside the bar of an item that is itself about to be marked DONE. That is the precise failure FU-361 was filed against in W551 - 'an item marked done is where a deferred obligation goes to be forgotten' - committed one round later in my own work. THE MEASURED STATE, unchanged by the hold: agentic_core/avatars/frontend/avatar_interface.py is the only caller of execute_cycle for a USER rather than for the organism; agentic_core/avatars/__init__.py exports the orchestrator and not the interface; no route reaches either. So a module that would wire the avatar path exists and is reached by nothing. WHAT RELEASES THIS ROW: P3.20 giving the engines a path to a model, after which clearance gate 1 can receive a constitutional verdict and the loop can emit rather than withhold. WHAT THE WORK IS THEN: export the interface, give it a route, and drive BOTH outcomes - an emission that clears and one that is withheld - because a chat surface wired to a loop that can still withhold must show the withholding as a refusal with its reason and never as an empty answer. UNTIL THEN THE HOLD STANDS and this row is what makes it visible rather than remembered. RELEASE CONDITION MET ON ITS WORDS AND NOT IN SUBSTANCE — MEASURED W560, AND THIS NOW NEEDS THE OWNER. This row says it is released by "P3.20 giving the engines a path to a model, after which clearance gate 1 can receive a constitutional verdict and the loop can emit rather than withhold". W560 GAVE THEM THE PATH: all six engines now call the tier router and carry what served them. BUT THE CONSEQUENCE DID NOT FOLLOW. On this machine the router walks down to the deterministic floor, because no tier above it holds a resource - nothing is pulled and reachable, and the higher tiers are not runnable here for measured reasons (FU-271 default (a), the Owner decision of 2026-10-03). Wiring the avatar path today would therefore still turn a chat surface that answers into one that deliberately delivers nothing, which is the user-facing regression the Owner already declined once (FU-357, W554). THE QUESTION, which only the Owner can settle because only the Owner set the condition: the hold said "until the engines have a model path" and they now have one that ends at the floor. (a) HOLD, and correct this row's release condition to the substance rather than the wording - the avatar path waits until an engine can actually produce a constitutional verdict, which needs a model that answers, which needs FU-271 option (b) hardware or (c) an Owner-gated external accelerant. (b) WIRE IT NOW and let the honest refusal show on the chat surface, accepting that it delivers nothing until a model answers. DEFAULT IF UNDECIDED: (a) HOLD, for the same reason the Owner accepted in W554 - more honest and a user-facing regression is still a regression. items.title: The recirculation loop cannot be switched on from a running backend: auto_metabolic defaults off, the configure route does not expose it, and no page shows it
items.why: Found W555 by the FRESH-BACKEND PROBE P3.16's bar asks for, which is what a probe is for - the suite drives this loop by setting the attribute in process and could never have found it. MEASURED on a live uvicorn at :8010: POST /api/v1/heartbeat/configure accepts interval_seconds, auto_evolve, auto_economy, auto_align, auto_compliance and auto_ship, and NOT auto_metabolic; agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:174 sets self.auto_metabolic = False at construction; heartbeat.py:369 gates the whole six-stage recirculation leg on it; and a POST /beat with the body {auto_metabolic: true, metabolic_every: 1} returns 200 while the field is silently ignored - the actions list comes back as pulse, homeostasis, genome_scan, transformation_tick and the metabolic cycle never runs. GET /status DOES report last_metabolic and metabolic_basis, so a reader sees a loop that never ran and no way to make it run. WHY THIS IS NOT A BUG IN W533: the loop genuinely runs from the beat and its stage latencies are genuinely recorded - that is driven, and the default being OFF is deliberate and right (six stages with their engine calls is expensive, and a surprise default that costs a second per beat would be the worse mistake). WHAT IS MISSING IS THE SWITCH: a capability nobody can turn on from outside the process is the reach class this plan keeps finding, one step short of a module nothing imports. ALREADY SCOPED, which is why this row is small: docs/CLOSURE_PREP_TWELVE.md item D7 sets out the work - add auto_metabolic to ConfigureRequest and to the heartbeat's _AUTONOMY_KEYS so it survives a restart, report it from status(), and add a sixth AUTONOMY entry plus the withheld state to HeartbeatMonitor.tsx. It also records a hazard found while scoping: adding the key to _AUTONOMY_KEYS breaks two existing guards through the shared store, so that half needs its own measurement. AND ONE BAR FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: a leg must assert the switch GATES the run - that with auto_metabolic false the cycle does NOT happen - because a leg that only drives the enabled case cannot tell a switch from a decoration. || CORRECTED W600 — THIS ROW'S OWN HAZARD IS FALSE, and it is why the row sat open for forty-five rounds looking larger than it is. The sentence above says adding the key to _AUTONOMY_KEYS 'breaks two existing guards through the shared store'. items.title: P2.17's body states the round-cost measurement that IS the item, and every figure in it is now stale by a factor of two to four
items.why: Measured W555 while reporting the plan's state. P2.17's body carries its measurement as prose: 'median round 4.1 h over 32 commit-to-commit gaps; the full suite 46 min of it (~19%); the blind sweep ~10 min (~4%); the remaining ~77% is measuring live state, patching, writing guards and refuting' and '18 items carry a DONE marker across 18 DISTINCT rounds... 30 of the 48 rounds closed none at all'. LIVE TODAY, from the register's own generated block and from this session's runs: the median round is 1.6 h over 36 gaps (not 4.1 over 32); a full suite run is 10-17 min (14 runs this session, mean ~10.6 min when the tree is quiet), not 46; 38 items carry a DONE marker, not 18; and the suite's share of a round is therefore nearer 10-18% of a much shorter round. The direction of the error matters: the body argues that the lever is NOT working faster inside a round because verification is only ~19% of it, and both terms of that argument have moved - the round got shorter and the suite got much shorter, so the proportion the argument rests on was recomputed by the very work the item describes. WHY THIS IS INSIDE THE BAR RATHER THAN BESIDE IT: part (c) already reads 'the round-cost figures are computed from git and the register, never typed', and these are typed. So this row is not new scope - it is the measured instance that shows (c) is unmet in the item's own body, recorded so the closing round does not have to re-derive it. WHAT THE CLOSING ROUND SHOULD DO: render these figures from scripts/session_forecast.py or the register's generated block at render time, exactly as the pace block already does, so the paragraph cannot go stale again - and keep the ARGUMENT separate from the figures, because the argument (rounds that close no item, and a round that cannot close two) survives the recomputation while the percentages do not. MEASURED W558, AND THE SUITE PROFILE EXISTS FOR THE FIRST TIME: a full run was taken with --durations=30 folded into a re-run that was needed anyway, so it cost nothing. 30 of 554 tests hold 2,024 of the 4,529 worker-seconds available (754.77s wall x 6 workers) - FORTY-FIVE PER CENT OF ALL COMPUTE IN FIVE PER CENT OF THE TESTS. The slowest single test is test_w502 at 157.74s, which is a HARD FLOOR: no amount of parallelism finishes the suite faster than its longest test, so -n beyond 6 cannot help. The top five are test_w502 157.74s, test_w452 148.16s, test_cross_tenant_isolation_under_auth 115.19s, test_w462 112.13s and test_w479 110.48s = 644 worker-seconds between them. Four of the five drive real multi-stage lifecycles end to end, so they are expensive because they do the work rather than because they waste it - which means the honest lever is PLACEMENT (shard the heavy five across workers deliberately instead of letting xdist place them) and not optimisation. SIX FULL RUNS THIS SESSION: 10m26s, 11m31s, 17m29s, 12m13s, 12m06s, 10m56s, plus a 13m25s - a 67 per cent spread on a test count that barely moved, and the long tail of that spread is the FU-362 stall rather than work. AND THE LARGEST COST IS NOT THE RUN LENGTH AT ALL: a red costs a whole extra run, and of the reds this session FOUR were guards going stale on the plan advancing (FU-365) rather than real defects - a pinned slot id, a parsed table column, a page block a later item restructured, and two guards with no arm for a gate being discharged. items.title: A stage with no prompt template yields its START event and then nothing, so a reader sees a stage begin and never finish
items.why: Found W558 while ANSWERING FU-338's open question rather than fixing it, which is what that row asked for. FU-338 asked whether _provenance_summary's calls=0 can mean 'a writer failed to append' instead of 'no call was made'. MEASURED and the answer is NO, so it closed as refuted: agentic_core/api/intelligence.py:513 is the only path that skips provs.append (a stage whose prompt template is empty hits `continue`), and all four engines declare every template they need - _APIE_STAGES 9 of 9, _BDP_STAGES 8 of 8, _DDPIE_STAGES 9 of 9, _SPI_STAGES 8 of 8 - so the writer is always reached today. And even on that path the zero would be TRUE, because a skipped stage makes no call, so not counting it is correct. WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND INSTEAD: the `continue` at :513 comes AFTER `yield _ev(f'{stage_key}_start', stage_label, stage_desc)` at :509. So a stage whose template is missing announces that it has STARTED and then emits nothing - no result event, no failure, no reason - and the completion line reports it only as part of 'N of M stages ran', with no word about which one did not or why. A reader watching the stream sees a stage begin and silently never finish, which is the one thing a progress stream must not do: an absent ending is indistinguishable from a stream that was cut off. NOT LIVE TODAY, because no template is missing - this is a latent gap, recorded because the guard against it is cheap and the failure is silent. FIX: either emit a stage event carrying the skip and its reason before continuing, so the stream closes every stage it opens, or move the template check ABOVE the start event so a stage that cannot run is never announced. The second is smaller; the first tells a reader more.

items.title: OWNER DECISION: may the platform hold a behavioural model of an individual, to build the user-satisfaction signal the vision requires
items.why: W563 assessed the archived biomimetic layer and found the only user-satisfaction mechanism that exists anywhere in this repository or its archive. Its explicit half is a rating channel and is buildable now. ITS OTHER HALF IS THE QUESTION: it collects IMPLICIT feedback - a person's dwell time - and fits a per-user preference model to that person's own behaviour. It passes Ruling A.9.5 as it stands, because it forms no verdict on anyone's spiritual state and no verdict on a person at all; it is a preference, not a judgement. THAT IS PRECISELY WHY IT MUST BE ASKED BEFORE A REBUILD RATHER THAN AFTER: the one-question test is whether the SUBJECT IS A PERSON, and here it is - the model is of an individual, fitted from their behaviour, held by the platform. A ruling permitting it would be the first time this platform models a person at all, and that is a constitutional step, not an engineering choice. THE DECISION: (a) the explicit rating only - a person says what they think and nothing is inferred from how they behaved (the default, and what is built today); (b) explicit plus implicit signals used only in AGGREGATE, never attributed to an individual and never stored per person, so the platform learns about the product and not about anyone; (c) a per-individual model, which needs its own terms - what is collected, what it is used for, whether the person can see it, correct it and delete it, and whether it is ever used to decide anything about them. The vision names customer/user satisfaction as one of four continuous measures and the selection item refuses while any of the four is unmeasured, so (a) does unblock the measure. Nothing beyond (a) is written while this is open, and a guard leg greps the live tree for the behavioural signal rather than trusting the sentence.

No dwell time, no implicit signal, no per-individual preference model, and no aggregate behavioural signal either since option (b) was not taken. items.title: Every other word-and-phrase screen on the platform is unaudited by the method that just found a live miss in the distress gate
items.why: W564 drove ten direct phrasings through the clinical-care gate and found that the plainest one - 'end my life' - PASSED the screen, while 'kill myself' escalated correctly. The pattern was `(?:end|take)\s+(?:my\s+own\s+)?life` : 'my' and 'own' were one optional unit, so it matched 'end life' and 'end my own life' and not the phrasing in between. It is fixed and guarded. THE LESSON IS THE METHOD, AND IT HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED ANYWHERE ELSE: a word screen is not reviewable by eye - the defect was invisible in the regex and obvious the moment the gate was driven with the phrasings it exists to catch. UNAUDITED BY THAT METHOD: _RULING_PATTERNS and _PROOF_PATTERNS in the same module, and - much larger - the three-regex keyword filter that the whole-vision document records as the ONLY screen on 49 of 57 API modules ('GaaS gate on every output: true for 8 of 57'). THE FIX: for each screen, enumerate the phrasings it is FOR, drive them, and record which pass - then either widen the pattern or move the phrasing into the declared coverage limit, because a screen that misses a phrasing it was written for is a defect while a screen that misses one it never claimed is a stated limit. Do not merely add patterns: the deliverable is the DRIVEN LIST, so the next round can tell the two apart.

items.title: Nine write paths use a TOLERANT read as their write base, so the write persists the recoverable prefix and destroys the rest
items.why: DRIVEN AND PROVEN in W577 on a user's own document. read_json_reported recovers a store's first complete JSON value via raw_decode and DISCARDS everything after it; nine functions take that value and hand it straight to atomic_write_json, so the discarded remainder is overwritten and gone. Driven: a user_workspace store holding two concatenated records (267 bytes, the shape a non-atomic overwrite of a shorter document by a longer one leaves) went through PUT /profile and came back 226 bytes with history=[] and prefs={} - the user's recorded question permanently destroyed - and the response reported success with no indication of any loss. THE NINE: api/agent_hub.py update_handoff_status (inside store_lock, so it is the authoritative write), api/operational_excellence.py set_health_baseline (would drop every OTHER model's baseline), api/user_workspace.py put_workspace + put_profile + clear_profile, api/native_ai.py evaluate_model + promote_model + retire_model + reinstate_model (all four via lifecycle_state -> save_lifecycle, dropping retired models and evaluations). THIS IS NOT FU-298's CLASS and must not be closed by it: FU-298 is a reader that does not disclose a short figure, which is a truth defect; this is a WRITER that destroys data it could not read, which is a loss defect, and surfacing a reason does not fix it. The remedy is the opposite one - a write base must be read STRICTLY and the write REFUSED, which is the rule capital_fund.py already states in writing for exactly this reason ('a WRITER asks strictly and refuses, because writing back over a quarantined store is how the reset becomes permanent') and which the other five files do not follow. LATENT VS LIVE: every in-platform writer is atomic (W472), so the platform cannot currently produce the concatenated shape itself; it is reachable through any corruption of external origin (a truncated restore, a partial sync, a copy interrupted mid-write), and the correct engineering answer does not depend on which - a tolerantly-read value is never a safe write base.

The guard asserts the class three ways - a tolerant read and a write in one function, a write base whose reason was discarded at the ASSIGNMENT, and the retire route driven - because a blind proved the first two are blind to one call of indirection.

items.title: Every request model on the platform silently discards a field a caller sends, so an instruction and a dropped instruction look identical
items.why: MEASURED in W577 while preparing FU-313: 206 request/response models derive BaseModel across 60 files in agentic_core/api, and ZERO declare extra=forbid. Pydantic v2 ignores undeclared fields by default, so a caller can send a field, receive 200, and have it discarded with no indication - which is exactly FU-313's mechanism (committed_rounds and confidence sent to /transformation/orchestrate vanish because OrchestrateRequest declares neither) generalised to every route. The caller cannot distinguish a recorded instruction from a dropped one, and on a governance or commitment route that difference is the whole content of the request. THE REMEDY IS NOT A BLANKET FORBID and this row must not be read as asking for one: flipping 206 models would answer 422 to any caller sending an extra field, the frontend included, for no gain in truth on most of them. The work is to forbid on the models where an undeclared field means a LOST INSTRUCTION - commitments, budgets, governance inputs, anything a caller sends expecting it to be recorded - to leave the rest tolerant, and to SAY WHICH AND WHY, so the choice is auditable rather than a default nobody chose. FU-313 is the first instance and should declare its two fields regardless; this row is the class behind it.

The two instruments answer different questions - a scan asks whether the code says it, a render asks whether a person sees it - and a claim about what a PERSON SEES belongs to the second. THE WORK, as a scheduled migration rather than one round: convert the guards whose claim is about what is RENDERED (an empty state, a disclosure chip, a figure with its basis, a control's direction), leave the ones whose claim is about the SOURCE (a binding present, a gate not disabled, a literal absent), and record which of the 295 testids are exercised so the count stops reading as coverage. ALSO: nothing in the Python suite shells out to node, so a guard that EXECUTES the runner would add an environment assumption CI does not carry - the round runs npm test the way it runs tsc, and the W579 guard asserts only that the configuration is intact and says so in writing.

Widening a label screen to prose would mean writing a language model as a regex, so the honest alternative was taken: the limit is DECLARED (_COVERAGE_LIMIT) and carried on every pass as + + , and economy/governance.py's governed_cycle_sync now puts them on the governance record beside its - which until then was a bare word reading as a clearance. THE PRE-FLIGHT'S KEY SCREEN THEN SAID, CORRECTLY, that the keys reach 'only 1 backend module and none of them PRINTS it'. items.title: An item holding routes can only be closed by handing ALL of them to one destination, which is how a sink is made
items.why: MEASURED IN W581, when P2.18's three clauses were all delivered and the item still could not be marked done. followups.py done P2.18 --reroute REFUSES with: "7 route(s) still send new rows to P2.18: pass --hand-to <the open item that owns that area now>". And --hand-to takes exactly ONE item. So the mechanism's only way to close an item that holds routes is to move ALL of them to a single destination, which is the definition of a sink. THIS IS HOW P2.4 BECAME ONE. Its own charter records it: nine of eleven open rows arrived AFTER its bar was written, through routes handed in when P1.16, P2.6, P2.8, P2.9, P3.18 and P3.19 closed, and the Owner ruled on 2026-10-02 that HIGH rows must route BY AREA precisely because that short-circuit is why P2.4 never closed. P2.18 then inherited all seven of those routes by the same single-target mechanism, and is now in the same position one item later. THE SEVEN AREAS HAVE NO OPEN OWNER BETWEEN THEM: autonomous technical support, the geospheric regulators and the causal simulator, the perimeter and the governance gate, the cascade's delivery measurement, the economy's flows, the catalogue and product directories (the largest, spanning forty files), and the developer pages' export surfaces. Every original owner is CLOSED, which is exactly why the rows keep landing wherever the mechanism last pointed. SO THE DECISION IS NOT A ROUND'S TO MAKE: handing seven unrelated areas to one open item recreates the condition the Owner has already ruled against, and splitting them by area is a thing the CLI cannot currently express. THE WORK, and it is two separable pieces. (1) THE MECHANISM: let an item's routes be handed per-route rather than per-item, so done takes a mapping or defers to the by-area routing that route_row already performs for a new row - the rule exists, it is simply not reachable from done. (2) THE DECISION, which belongs to the Owner once the mechanism can express it: for each of the seven areas, the open item that owns it now, or a statement that the area has no owner and new rows in it are unscheduled rather than silently assigned. UNTIL THEN P2.18's CLAUSES ARE DELIVERED AND THE ITEM IS NOT MARKED DONE, which is the honest state rather than either pretending the item is open work or forcing a routing nobody chose. Note the plan's own order makes the trap plain: the next open item before P2.18 is P2.17, whose subject is the round's own cost, and handing it the catalogue scatter would be absurd on its face.

items.title: No engine performs a constitutional check, so clearance gate 1 can only ever abstain and the loop withholds every emission
items.why: TRACED IN FULL IN W582, because FU-366 holds the avatar path on a condition that cannot be met by what it names. THE CHAIN, measured end to end: every cognitive engine hardcodes constitutional_validation.passed = None with the basis "no constitutional check ran: this engine performs none" - a LITERAL in the source, not a refusal; mushawara_bridge_2.deliberate reads those verdicts and derives status NOT ASSESSED whenever any is None; clearance gate 1 in avatars/core/clearance_chain.py requires status == "APPROVED" and blocks; and the recirculation loop therefore WITHHOLDS every emission. The heartbeat's own W533 comment states the outcome plainly: "six measured stages and an empty mouth is the NORMAL state of this platform today." SO THE RELEASE CONDITION FU-366 CARRIES IS WRONG, AND MEASURABLY SO. It holds "until the engines have a model path, after which clearance gate 1 can receive a constitutional verdict". MEASURED: ollama is reachable and three local models are installed (llama2, llama3.2, llama3.2:1b) with llama3.2 as the effective default - so the engines HAVE a model path - and the loop still withholds, because passed=None is a literal that no model changes. The deliberation's own reason string asserted the false cause too ("the engines refuse for want of a model path") and W582 corrected it: they do not refuse for want of a model, they perform no check at all. A hold whose condition cannot be met by the thing it names is a permanent hold wearing a temporary label. THE WORK, which is what the hold should actually wait on: implement a constitutional check that produces a REAL verdict for an emission, so gate 1 can receive a pass or a failure instead of an absence. Where it belongs is the open question and is a design decision rather than a line: either each engine performs the check its own domain supports and returns passed True or False with a basis, or - more likely right - the CHAIN performs one check over the emission and the engines stop being asked for a verdict none of them computes, which would also make the three-state derivation in deliberate honest rather than permanently NOT ASSESSED. WHATEVER IS CHOSEN, TWO THINGS ARE NOT NEGOTIABLE: the check must be able to FAIL and be seen to fail, driven both ways, because a gate that can only abstain is the same defect in a new place; and a withheld emission must continue to show the withholding as a refusal with its reason and never as an empty answer. SCOPE NOTE: this does not require a model to answer, and it is not the avatar path. It is the one thing standing between a loop that measures six stages and a loop that can emit, and FU-366's hold-or-wire choice only becomes a real question once it exists.

items.title: A fitness mean published as a vital sign averages across three provenances and reports none of them
items.why: The genome records keep a three-state provenance for every fitness and the published MEAN discards it. MEASURED IN W584 BEFORE BUILDING, and my first reading was wrong in the opposite direction so both are recorded here. organism/genome.py:194 writes "fitness_score": fitness if fitness is not None else 0.5, which looks like a default masquerading as a measurement - but the very next line writes fitness_provenance and it is HONEST: "ai-declared (unverified)" when a FITNESS line was parsed, "default-unencoded (no FITNESS line parsed)" when it was not, and "inherited-mean-unevaluated (no selection step exists)" for a crossover child. Three provenances, each naming exactly what its number is worth. Patching that writer would have broken working code. THE DEFECT IS THE AGGREGATE. api/organism_status.py:192-199 appends every numeric fitness_score to one list and reports mean_fitness = sum/len, with no filter on provenance and no statement of what the mean is a mean OF. Measured in the live store: of 15 stored genomes 11 carry exactly 0.5, three carry 0.85 and one carries 0.6 - so the published figure is a blend of a few self-declared numbers and a majority of records whose own provenance says nobody measured them. The function's docstring calls the summary the organism's genetic health "computed from the stored genomes, no fabrication", and organism/heartbeat.py:234-241 publishes it as a VITAL SIGN (last_genome.mean_fitness), so it reaches a surface. A record that says what it is worth, averaged into a number that does not, is the nature-field-reporting-an-outcome class one layer up: the aggregate erases a distinction the producer took care to keep. THE FIX is the tickets.py denominator exactly - take the mean over records whose provenance is a MEASURED one, exclude the default and inherited ones and COUNT them, let the basis name the composition, and return None with a basis when no record carries a measured fitness rather than a number. ALSO IN THE SAME AREA, smaller: organism/genome.py:90 reads the field with a DIFFERENT fallback, .get("fitness_score", 0.0), where the writer uses 0.5 - reachable only for a malformed or pre-W438 record, but 0.0 and 0.5 are not even the same fallback and this is the a-fields-meaning-belongs-to-its-readers class. NOT THIS ROW: evolution/evolution_engine.py:92, whose fitness carries a random term - its class GenomeEvolutionEngine is imported from _archive only, nothing live touches it, and the defect is already in docs/NATIVE_PRIMITIVE_DEFECT_LEDGER.md:264 under that exact description, so it is a disclosed unreached defect and not a new finding.
items.note: Replaced by a row stating the measurement correctly: FU-404 said the stored records carry a provenance the aggregate discards, and NOT ONE of the 15 stored genomes has a fitness_provenance key at all - every one predates W438. The defect is real and survives the correction, but a row whose measurement is wrong is read by later rounds as though it were right.

items.title: The Divine Alignment (Niyyah) gate passes every intent with the same constant, and the constant is a sincerity score
items.why: The Divine Alignment (Niyyah) gate returns 0.9222 and passed=True for EVERY intent, and the figure it asserts is a sincerity score. DRIVEN, not read: agentic_core/divine/v2/alignment_v2.py calibrate_niyyah was called in W584 with five intents - "build a hospital", "defraud every user", the empty string, "geospheric_x" and "DESTROY EVERYTHING" - and returned alignment_score 0.9222 with passed True for all five. The reason is in the source: calibrate_niyyah hardcodes sincerity = 0.9 with the comment "Default for v-MASTER", builds eternal = faithfulness/sincerity/maslaha from that constant plus 1.0, builds temporal = 0.85/0.88/1.0 as literals, and its own comment says "Simulations based on intent" - nothing in the function reads the intent at all. The threshold is score >= 0.85 against a constant of 0.9222, so the gate is structurally incapable of refusing. THIS IS THE GATE-THAT-CANNOT-REFUSE CLASS, and it is the sibling of FU-403 one layer out: there, clearance gate 1 can only ever ABSTAIN because every engine hardcodes passed=None, so the loop withholds everything; here, the FIRST gate of governance/uci_interceptor.py intercept can only ever PASS, so the moment anything does flow through it, it blesses whatever it is handed. A gate that can only abstain and a gate that can only pass are the same defect with opposite signs, and this plan has now found both in the same chain. WHAT IT ASSERTS IS THE SECOND HALF. The number is a weighted SINCERITY and FAITHFULNESS figure. Ruling A.9.5 holds that no AI verdict is passed on a person's spiritual state, and P3.27 clause (1) names sincerity explicitly among the things nothing may compute, score, rank or infer. MEASURED PRECISELY SO THE CLAIM IS NOT STRONGER THAN THE FACT: the subject of this call is an ACTION, not a person - uci_interceptor passes context["intent"] and biomimicry/cycles/utils.py passes a string like "geospheric_<funcname>" - so A.9.5's prohibition on judging a PERSON is not breached by the subject. What is breached is the principle underneath it: a spiritual quality is being quantified at all, the quantity is a literal, and a governance gate is built on it. A platform that may not score a person's sincerity should not be scoring sincerity as such and calling the constant a measurement. REACH, measured rather than assumed: the interceptor is driven by the suite at several points and sits on the avatars to recirculation_orchestrator to uci_interceptor import chain, so it is live code on a live path - but what reaches a person through it today is bounded by FU-403, since the recirculation loop withholds every emission. So no user action is currently being blessed by this gate, and every user action would be the moment FU-403 is fixed. The second call site is worse in a different way: biomimicry/cycles/utils.py:58-64 checks the calibration and, on failure, logs and PROCEEDS, with a comment saying "In a strict environment, we would raise an error here" - so even if the score could fail, that leg would not stop anything. THE WORK: the gate must be able to refuse and be seen to refuse, driven both ways, or it must be removed rather than left as a constitutional ornament. If a niyyah check is to exist it needs an input it actually reads and a basis it can state; if it cannot have one, the honest form is a REFUSAL to assess - NOT_ASSESSABLE with a reason, exactly as the vbs/quality.py screen does - and never a 0.9222 that reads as a measured pass. Either way the sincerity arithmetic goes: a weighted mean of literals is not a reading of anyone's or anything's sincerity.

items.title: Two live classes are both named UnifiedConstitutionalInterceptorV16Omega, and only one is the wired engine
items.why: Two live classes are both named UnifiedConstitutionalInterceptorV16Omega, and only one of them is the wired constitutional engine. MEASURED IN W584 while fixing the niyyah gate, and it nearly sent the fix to the wrong file. agentic_core/gaas/v5/uci_v16_omega.py:62 and agentic_core/governance/uci_interceptor.py:20 declare classes with the identical name. They are not variants of one thing: the gaas/v5 one is exported from agentic_core/gaas/v5/__init__.py, is what the suite drives (it returns an InterceptionResult with .status, .output and .ueg_logged, and tests monkeypatch it on the g5 module at four separate points), and is the constitutional interceptor engine the platform describes as wired. The governance one returns a plain dict, raises PermissionError from its gates, and is imported by exactly one live module - agentic_core/avatars/core/recirculation_orchestrator.py:24. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING UNTIDY. A round reading a finding about "the interceptor" has no way to tell which file is meant, and the two have DIFFERENT GATES: the governance one carries the Divine Alignment (Niyyah) gate that FU-406 found could only ever pass, and the gaas/v5 one does not. A fix applied to the name rather than to the file would have landed in the wrong place and reported success, and a guard asserting a property of "the interceptor" can pass against one while the other breaches it. This is the naming-hazard class the Vision 8.0 assessment already flagged twice in other forms, and the grep-the-call-not-the-method-name class: a search for the class name returns both, and a reader resolves the ambiguity by guessing. THE WORK, and it is a judgement rather than a rename to be done blindly: establish which one is the constitutional interceptor for this platform and give the other a name that says what it actually is - the governance one is really the avatar recirculation path's own pre-flight, since that is its only live caller - or, if the two are meant to be one thing, say which survives and move the gates that matter into it through Change Control. NOT A ROUND'S DECISION TO MAKE SILENTLY: both are reached, one by the suite and one by an import chain, so a rename touches live paths and the choice of which name means what is an architectural statement rather than a tidy-up. What a round CAN do without deciding anything is make the ambiguity impossible to walk into: a guard that asserts there is exactly one class by that name in the live tree would have failed the moment the second appeared.

items.title: A VSB records no parent and no lineage, which is the precondition for every clause of turnover
items.why: A VSB records no parent and no lineage at all, which is the precondition for every clause of turnover. SPLIT OUT OF FU-312 IN W584, because FU-312 carried two subjects and only one of them was P3.27's. FU-312 read "Three dead genome stubs should be deleted, and a VSB records no lineage": the stubs are clause (6) of P3.27 and were deleted in W584, and the lineage half is P3.26 clause (1) word for word - "a LINEAGE field exists on an entity and is written by whatever creates it: a guard drives a creation and reads the parent back, and an entity with no parent says so rather than showing null as though it were an answer". An item closes on its own bar, and P3.27's bar says nothing about lineage, so closing FU-312 against it would have closed a row on a clause that never asked for it. MEASURED IN W584: agentic_core/api/vsb.py contains exactly one occurrence of the word lineage, a comment at line 454 about manifest versioning, and no parent_vsb, parent_id or lineage field exists on an entity anywhere in the establishment path. So an entity created by this platform records nothing about where it came from. WHY IT IS THE PRECONDITION rather than one clause among seven: P3.26 couples destruction with creation, and five of its clauses are about an entity's relationship to another entity - mitosis creating a subsidiary that inherits its parent's constitution verbatim and is funded from the parent's own share, apoptosis returning what a retired entity held to the reservoirs, the never-auto-retire set protecting the LAST entity in its realm and domain, meiosis producing a candidate that is not a birth. None of those can be driven, asserted or even stated without a parent field, because each one is a claim about a lineage. P3.26's own text says so: a VSB "records no parent and no lineage at all, which is the precondition for any of it". THE WORK: a lineage field on an entity, written by whatever creates it, never defaulted - and an entity with no parent must SAY it has none rather than carrying a null that reads as an answer, which is the three-state rule this plan applies everywhere else. The guard drives a creation and reads the parent back, and drives a parentless creation and reads the statement back.

The governance one returns a plain dict, raises PermissionError from its gates, and is imported by exactly one live module - agentic_core/avatars/core/recirculation_orchestrator.py:24. WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING UNTIDY. A round reading a finding about "the interceptor" has no way to tell which file is meant, and the two have DIFFERENT GATES: the governance one carries the Divine Alignment (Niyyah) gate that FU-406 found could only ever pass, and the gaas/v5 one does not. A fix applied to the name rather than to the file would have landed in the wrong place and reported success, and a guard asserting a property of "the interceptor" can pass against one while the other breaches it. This is the naming-hazard class the Vision 8.0 assessment already flagged twice in other forms, and the grep-the-call-not-the-method-name class: a search for the class name returns both, and a reader resolves the ambiguity by guessing. THE WORK, and it is a judgement rather than a rename to be done blindly: establish which one is the constitutional interceptor for this platform and give the other a name that says what it actually is - the governance one is really the avatar recirculation path's own pre-flight, since that is its only live caller - or, if the two are meant to be one thing, say which survives and move the gates that matter into it through Change Control. NOT A ROUND'S DECISION TO MAKE SILENTLY: both are reached, one by the suite and one by an import chain, so a rename touches live paths and the choice of which name means what is an architectural statement rather than a tidy-up. What a round CAN do without deciding anything is make the ambiguity impossible to walk into: a guard that asserts there is exactly one class by that name in the live tree would have failed the moment the second appeared.

items.title: A VSB records no parent and no lineage, which is the precondition for every clause of turnover
items.why: A VSB records no parent and no lineage at all, which is the precondition for every clause of turnover. SPLIT OUT OF FU-312 IN W584, because FU-312 carried two subjects and only one of them was P3.27's. FU-312 read "Three dead genome stubs should be deleted, and a VSB records no lineage": the stubs are clause (6) of P3.27 and were deleted in W584, and the lineage half is P3.26 clause (1) word for word - "a LINEAGE field exists on an entity and is written by whatever creates it: a guard drives a creation and reads the parent back, and an entity with no parent says so rather than showing null as though it were an answer". An item closes on its own bar, and P3.27's bar says nothing about lineage, so closing FU-312 against it would have closed a row on a clause that never asked for it. MEASURED IN W584: agentic_core/api/vsb.py contains exactly one occurrence of the word lineage, a comment at line 454 about manifest versioning, and no parent_vsb, parent_id or lineage field exists on an entity anywhere in the establishment path. So an entity created by this platform records nothing about where it came from. WHY IT IS THE PRECONDITION rather than one clause among seven: P3.26 couples destruction with creation, and five of its clauses are about an entity's relationship to another entity - mitosis creating a subsidiary that inherits its parent's constitution verbatim and is funded from the parent's own share, apoptosis returning what a retired entity held to the reservoirs, the never-auto-retire set protecting the LAST entity in its realm and domain, meiosis producing a candidate that is not a birth. None of those can be driven, asserted or even stated without a parent field, because each one is a claim about a lineage. P3.26's own text says so: a VSB "records no parent and no lineage at all, which is the precondition for any of it". THE WORK: a lineage field on an entity, written by whatever creates it, never defaulted - and an entity with no parent must SAY it has none rather than carrying a null that reads as an answer, which is the three-state rule this plan applies everywhere else. The guard drives a creation and reads the parent back, and drives a parentless creation and reads the statement back.

THREE STATES, not two: no parent stated gives generation 0 and a basis saying the entity IS a root rather than a null left to speak for itself; a resolved parent gives one deeper than its own, with a parent predating the field counted as 1 and SAYING so rather than guessing a chain that cannot be walked; an unresolvable id gives None, never 0, because 0 would assert the entity is a root. THE REFUSAL IS AT THE ROUTE and had to be: enrich_vsb_entity calls register inside except-Exception-pass so a refusal raised in the writer is swallowed, and three of the five creation paths return a StreamingResponse so a refusal inside the generator cannot be a 4xx - status 200 is already sent. Both were driven over HTTP and both return 409 naming the id. AND THE COVERAGE LEG EARNED ITS PLACE TWICE: it caught that genesis_establish called register positionally without the field (register's own unit behaviour was already correct, so only driving HTTP exposed it), then caught four further paths reaching enrich_vsb_entity without passing it, two of them in synthesis_studio.py which the original three-path estimate had missed entirely. Eleven blinds red, including one that proved the absent-means-ON default had no assertion behind it at all.

items.title: Trimming the 12-language list to the 5 with dictionaries also narrows voice dictation, which the clause does not discuss
items.why: Trimming the 12-language list to the 5 with dictionaries also narrows VOICE DICTATION, which the clause does not discuss. OWNER-RULED 2026-10-05, approved shape recorded here so a later round does not decide it quietly. P3.6's own deliverable says "12-language list trimmed to what has a dictionary", and its ACCEPT clause (3) is explicit that "a hard-coded list of twelve fails this whatever it contains". MEASURED: apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/userPrefs.ts:20 hardcodes exactly twelve entries (en-US, ar-SA, ur-PK, fr-FR, es-ES, de-DE, hi-IN, bn-BD, zh-CN, id-ID, tr-TR, ms-MY) and apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/i18n.tsx:326 holds FIVE dictionaries (en, ar, fr, es, ur). So the clause is precisely met in its premise: the list is hard-coded and seven of the twelve have no dictionary. THE CONSEQUENCE THE BAR DOES NOT DISCUSS, and the reason this is a row rather than a line in a round. prefs.language is not only the interface language. Settings sets it on the browser Web Speech API for voice dictation, applyDocumentDirection reads it to switch the document to right-to-left for Arabic and Urdu, and it is the natural input for an AI output language. Trimming the single list to five therefore removes a user's ability to DICTATE in Turkish, Hindi, Bengali, Mandarin, Indonesian, Malay or German - a capability that works today, because dictation is the browser's own and does not depend on this platform holding a dictionary. AND THE OVER-CLAIM THE CLAUSE WAS WRITTEN AGAINST IS ALREADY ABSENT, which is what makes the trim a net loss if it is done naively. W370 and W505 already made the Settings page state coverage from the REAL dictionaries per selection: choosing a language without one prints "The interface is not translated into this language yet - it stays in English", and the dictation line says only that the choice is sent to the browser and that whether the browser recognises it "is its own capability, which this platform cannot check". So nothing currently claims twelve translated languages. What remains wrong is only the hard-coded list itself. THE APPROVED SHAPE: trim the INTERFACE language list as the deliverable says, computed from the dictionaries present so it grows by itself when a dictionary is added, and keep a WIDER set for dictation as a separate control rather than deleting the capability. A person who wants the interface in English and dictation in Turkish must still be able to say so. DO NOT delete the per-selection coverage line or the dictation sentence: both are true and removing a true statement is also a defect. NOT THIS ROW: P3.6's other two clauses. Clause (1) spans roughly nine surfaces (the six domain hubs, whatever the item means by DomainTool - no such file exists - Settings, and the avatar), each new key needing an entry in all five dictionaries or it silently falls back to English; clause (2) is a build from zero, since agentic_core/ai/gateway.py contains no language handling at all and a repo-wide search for requested_language, language_honoured, output_language and not_in_requested returns nothing. P3.6 is larger than one round and this row is only its clause (3) plus the consequence.

ALL THREE dictation readers honour the new preference with a fallback chain of dictationLanguage then language then en-US, so a user who never opens the new control keeps exactly what they had - DomainTool, useAvatarSession and GenesisJourney, because a new field honoured in one reader leaves two surfaces silently on the old one. items.title: The avatar path is HELD until a constitutional check produces a real verdict (FU-403), not until the engines have a model path
items.why: The avatar path is HELD, and the release condition is now the one that can actually be met. OWNER-RULED 2026-10-05: option (a) HOLD, with this row's release condition corrected from its wording to its substance. The hold itself is unchanged and the reason the Owner accepted in W554 still stands - wiring a chat surface to a loop that withholds every emission would turn a surface that answers into one that deliberately delivers nothing, and a user-facing regression is still a regression. WHAT THE OLD CONDITION SAID, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. This row was released by "P3.20 giving the engines a path to a model, after which clearance gate 1 can receive a constitutional verdict and the loop can emit rather than withhold". W560 gave them the path: all six engines call the tier router and carry what served them. W555 then measured that the consequence did not follow, and read it as a MODEL problem - the router walks down to the deterministic floor because no tier above it holds a resource, so the row pointed at FU-271 option (b) hardware or option (c) an Owner-gated external accelerant. W582 TRACED THE CHAIN END TO END AND THAT READING IS FALSE. Every cognitive engine hardcodes constitutional_validation.passed = None with the basis "no constitutional check ran: this engine performs none" - a LITERAL in the source, not a refusal for want of a resource. mushawara_bridge_2.deliberate reads those verdicts and derives NOT ASSESSED whenever any is None; clearance gate 1 in avatars/core/clearance_chain.py requires status APPROVED and blocks; the recirculation loop therefore withholds every emission. MEASURED IN THE SAME ROUND: ollama is reachable and three local models are installed (llama2, llama3.2, llama3.2:1b) with llama3.2 as the effective default - so the engines HAVE a model that answers, and the loop still withholds, because passed=None is a literal no model changes. The deliberation's own reason string asserted the same false cause and W582 corrected it. SO THE RELEASE CONDITION IS FU-403, NOT A MODEL: the avatar path waits until an engine - or the chain itself - performs a constitutional check that produces a REAL verdict, so gate 1 can receive a pass or a failure instead of an absence. Nothing about hardware, nothing about an external accelerant, and FU-271's options are not on this path at all. A hold whose stated condition cannot be met by the thing it names is a permanent hold wearing a temporary label, which is what this was for twenty-six rounds. WHAT THE WORK IS WHEN FU-403 LANDS, unchanged and still true: export the interface (agentic_core/avatars/__init__.py exports the orchestrator and not the interface), give it a route (no route reaches either today), and drive BOTH outcomes - an emission that clears and one that is withheld - because a chat surface wired to a loop that can still withhold must show the withholding as a refusal with its reason and never as an empty answer. WHY THIS ROW EXISTS AT ALL: W554 closed FU-357 by amending P3.16's third ACCEPT clause to hold the path, and nothing carried the deferred work forward - no open row mentioned the avatar path or avatar_interface.py, and the obligation existed only as prose inside the bar of an item about to be marked DONE. That is the exact failure FU-361 was filed against in W551, committed one round later. This row is what makes the hold visible rather than remembered. NO LONGER OWNER-GATED: the Owner has ruled, so it waits on FU-403's work rather than on a decision, and it is slotted alongside FU-403 on the item that now owns the avatars/core area.

items.title: A measuring script moves the process data root and a test loads it in-process, so a later test can see a moved store
items.why: A measuring script mutates the whole process's data root, and a test loads it IN-PROCESS, so whatever runs after it in that worker can see a moved store. FOUND W588 while diagnosing the W586 CI failure, and the diagnosis is NOT complete - the residue is named here rather than dressed as a cause. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. scripts/readme_figures.py api_figures() creates tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="readme-figures-") and then does os.environ.setdefault for DATA_DIR, WORKSTATION_DATA_DIR, PROJECTS_DIR, WORKSTATION_UEG_PATH and AI_DISABLE_LOCAL before importing agentic_core.app_mvp. Its own comment says why: the app writes to its data dir on import, so measuring must not touch the live store, and CI sets no DATA_DIR. Because it uses setdefault, it is a NO-OP on a developer machine where DATA_DIR is already exported and it SETS the process-wide data root on CI where nothing is. integration_tests/test_mvp_spine.py's W499 guard loads that script through importlib and calls measured() IN-PROCESS, so on CI the first test to do so moves the data root for everything that follows in that xdist worker. THE SYMPTOM THIS EXPLAINS. W586's repo guard failed on CI, and only on CI, with "the declared file is not on disk" at /tmp/readme-figures-lwa5daym/vsb_repos/vsb-ba11956c07/BUSINESS_PLAN.md - a path under exactly that temp prefix. The local suite was green in every round. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED, and why this row exists rather than a claim. agentic_core.config.data_path resolves Path(settings.data_dir), and settings is built when config is first imported, so it does not re-read the environment per call - driven in W588, where moving DATA_DIR mid-process changed nothing. For the CI path to resolve under the temp prefix, settings must have been bound AFTER the script set the variables, which requires an import order I did not reproduce. So the mechanism is consistent with the evidence and is not proven, and restoring the variables afterwards would not undo it, because the binding is in settings and not in the environment. WHAT WAS DONE IN W588: the W586 guard stopped re-deriving the store root and now reads agentic_core.api.vsb._REPO_STORE, the constant the WRITER binds at import, so the read cannot disagree with the write however the environment moves. That removes one class of disagreement without claiming to be the cause. THE WORK THIS ROW CARRIES: make the measurement unable to move another test's store at all - run readme_figures as a SUBPROCESS from the guard that checks its figures, which is what a script that mutates process-wide state needs, or give it a pure function that computes the figures without importing the app into this process. Then re-read CI, because CI is the only place this reproduces. SUSPECT IT ALSO FOR W565, whose CI failure is a forecast figure arriving as None - a store that moved mid-worker would produce exactly that, and the git checkout depth is a second environment assumption already recorded for that shape.

items.close_note: The measurement runs in a CHILD PROCESS now, which is the only fix that satisfies the clause. api_figures() used to os.environ.setdefault the data root and import the app IN-PROCESS, and a test loads this module and calls it - so under CI, which sets no DATA_DIR, the whole xdist worker's data root moved to a throwaway directory and every test after it read a temp store. RESTORING THE ENVIRONMENT WOULD NOT HAVE FIXED IT: the import is the damage, because the app's module-level config freezes against whatever the paths were when it was first imported. Driven in a child started WITHOUT the isolation variables, exactly as CI runs it - asserted in-process it would have passed even with the old code, which is why this survived every local run. ROOT is passed explicitly and re-inserted by the child rather than inherited, because a stray .pth puts the repo root on sys.path for every local process and a child relying on that passes here and fails on CI. Two blinds red, the second after FORCING the failure branch: a failing child must REFUSE, never answer zero, or `--fix` would rewrite the README to claim the platform exposes 0 API operations and `--check` would then agree with it.

items.title: Nothing asserts the register on disk is serialised the way its own writer serialises it, so a format drift returns as an unreviewable whole-file diff
items.why: MEASURED IN W588: docs/FOLLOWUPS.json was stored at indent=1 while both of its writers emit indent=2 (agentic_core/plan_followups.py:105 and scripts/followups.py:681), so the register had been maintained by scripted edits that preserved an older formatting. The first CLI write of the round reformatted all 7,708 lines and the round's real register change - seven retired areas, four reslotted rows, three new rows - arrived inside a 15,479-line whole-file rewrite that no reader could review. W588 separated the reformat into its own commit (ad30cf89), so the format now matches its writer. What remains is that NOTHING asserts it: the next scripted edit that rewrites the register at a different indent re-creates the drift silently, and the round after it produces another unreviewable whole-file diff. A whole-file rewrite is the shape that hides a defect rather than showing one, which is why this is worth a guard rather than a habit: assert that the register on disk is byte-identical to its own writer's serialisation of itself, so a drift fails at the pre-flight instead of surfacing as a 15,000-line diff.

items.title: The forecast returns a DIFFERENT KEY SET when history cannot be walked, so an unmeasurable figure reads as a missing field
items.why: MEASURED IN W589 from CI run 37276077594, where the keys the forecast returned were exactly ['hours_available', 'projection', 'round_durations', 'suite_h'] and a guard failed with "the forecast no longer reports the round-boundary cost". The cause is an EARLY RETURN: forecast_session() in scripts/session_forecast.py builds three keys, and when round_durations() reports assessable=False it sets projection to {"unavailable": why} and returns there - so round_boundaries_cost, contingency and the two-window comparison are ABSENT from the result rather than present with a stated basis. A reader that indexes round_boundaries_cost gets a KeyError, and a reader that uses .get() cannot tell an unmeasurable history from a forecast that simply does not carry the field. W589 fixed the CI symptom by setting fetch-depth: 0 on the backend checkout, so CI now has the history to walk; the defect itself is untouched, and a shallow clone is legitimate elsewhere - a fresh clone, a contributor's checkout, and the P5.4 handover where the entity repository must live without this repo. The fix is the pattern this codebase already uses everywhere else: every return of this function carries the same key set, with each unmeasurable figure as None beside the basis that says WHY it could not be computed, so the shape does not depend on whether the measurement succeeded. A missing key and a measured zero and an unmeasured field are three different things, and an early return collapses them into one.

My first fix filled the missing keys INSIDE the early return, which duplicated the key set in two places, left second_window_W490_plus still conditional, and added a _why key the full path lacked - so the shapes disagreed in the other direction. Driving both paths and diffing the key sets is what showed it. EVERY KEY IS NOW DECLARED ONCE in the initialiser both paths share, so no return can omit one because no return builds the set. round_boundaries_cost is a shape-complete DICT rather than None, because three of its seven fields need no duration at all and nulling the whole dict would throw away measurements that were available; the three that divide by the median round are None with a basis saying why. And what_this_cannot_know - the list of what the arithmetic cannot know - was being dropped exactly when the arithmetic could not know anything; it is now one tuple with one writer. Three blinds red.

items.title: CI runs the suite SERIALLY because the runner installs pytest without xdist: 48.8 minutes measured against 29 locally
items.why: MEASURED IN W589 from CI run 37287845785: the backend job took 48.8 minutes while the same suite takes 29 minutes locally at -n 2, and the other three jobs took 6.5, 1.7 and 0.1 minutes. The cause is in the workflow: the dependency step installs `pytest` alone, with the comment that it is the dev/test-only dependency the runtime requirements omit, so pytest-xdist is absent and the suite runs SERIALLY on a runner slower than this machine. The consequence is not the cost of the minutes but the feedback delay: a round pushes, waits most of an hour for CI, and in practice stops waiting - which is one of the reasons CI went unread for thirteen rounds while it was red. The fix is to install pytest-xdist in that step and pass -n auto, which is what the round itself runs; the conftest already subdivides the data root per worker (`_per_worker` rewrites DATA_DIR, WORKSTATION_DATA_DIR, PROJECTS_DIR, LISTINGS_DIR, SYNTHESIS_OUTPUT_DIR, PROPOSALS_DIR and WORKSTATION_UEG_PATH on PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER), so parallel workers over one store - the documented corruption mode - does not apply. It must be MEASURED on CI rather than assumed: a two-core runner may gain nothing from -n auto, and the four-core count observed in the test_w559 failure is the figure to size it against. Not done in W589 because that round's job was to make CI run the same suite the round runs and to stop it being red; changing how it runs the suite at the same time would have made the result of the first change unreadable.

items.title: A beat skipped the cadence for both layers in the full suite and the cause was never recorded; not reproduced since
items.why: OBSERVED ONCE IN W589 AND NOT REPRODUCED, which is why this is open rather than closed. test_w585_p33 failed in the full suite and passed in isolation: it ages both cadence layers' history past their periods, asserts with cadence.due() that each is genuinely DUE, runs one real beat, and the beat's actions came back as ['pulse', 'homeostasis', 'genome_scan', 'compliance_rescreen', 'transformation_tick'] with no 'cadence_refresh'. So the step raised, because the whole step sat in `except Exception: pass` - and the exception was swallowed, so the run that failed left NO record of the cause anywhere. The two defects that reading the step then found were fixed in the same round (the swallowed reason, and a single try around the whole layer loop that discarded a layer's completed refresh when a later layer raised), plus a confirmed ValueError where _compose ran int() on a progress field it does not own. The re-run with all three in place is green and the failure did not recur, so it CANNOT be said which of these was the cause, or whether the cause was any of them: a green run after a change is not evidence when the red run was not reproduced first. What remains to be done is therefore not a fix but a reproduction: the beat now records could_not_run with the exception type, message and a basis stating that a layer which could not run is still due, so the next occurrence names its own cause in the suite output and the guard's assertion message carries it. Candidates worth testing deliberately if it recurs: a store_lock TimeoutError on the plan path (store_lock raises after its timeout rather than writing unserialised, and the plan is written by several tests in a worker), and a strict read failing on a plan an earlier test left in a shape business_plan._load rejects. Do not close this row on another green suite; close it on a reproduction with the recorded reason, or on a measured argument that the fixed defects were necessarily the cause.

items.title: MILESTONE M1 cannot be re-run from this repository: the only committed fidelity workflow carries no TIER, which is the measure M1 is scored on
items.why: MEASURED IN W590 while preparing the M1 re-run the Owner ruled on 2026-10-05. MILESTONE M1 is mandated before any P2-P4 item and its bar is a standing Tier-1 count of 0, yet the milestone CANNOT BE RE-RUN FROM THIS REPOSITORY. The only committed fidelity workflow is scripts/workflows/fidelity_audit_v3.js: twelve agents (six assessors, six refuters) whose FINDINGS schema carries section, verdict, vision_claim, observed, evidence, disclosed_to_user, severity and smallest_honest_fix, and whose VERDICTS schema carries index, refuted, corrected_verdict, reason and evidence. Neither carries a TIER. But scripts/render_fidelity_ledger.py computes the M1 measure from exactly that field - standing_tier() reads a verdict's corrected_tier and falls back to the finding's own tier - so a run of the committed script produces a ledger in which every standing tier is None and the Tier-1 count cannot be computed at all. The script's own header says as much: version=4 "adds the tier the refuter stands behind", and v4 was W474. The tiered instrument has therefore never been committed. W572's commit 93f51c95 ran M1 with SIXTY-SIX agents over the six regions and committed ten files - the ledger, the v5 archive, the prompt, the register, the test file, the renderer, blinds - and no workflow script among them. So the instrument that produced the current measurement of 20 exists only in that session's transcript, and the repository holds a strictly weaker instrument that cannot score the milestone it is named for. Two consequences, both load-bearing. First, the milestone is not reproducible by anyone but the session that last ran it, which is the opposite of what a milestone is for and is squarely the P5.4 problem - the work must live without this repo's current session, let alone without this conversation. Second, every lesson about an instrument applies here: an instrument a plan names must RESOLVE, and this one resolves to a file that cannot produce the number the plan scores. The fix is to author and COMMIT the tiered edition - the v3 regions and the adversarial-refuter discipline, plus tier on the assessor's finding and corrected_tier on the refuter's verdict, the tier definitions the ledger itself states (1 a truth defect on a reached surface, 2 an invisible shortfall, 3 a disclosed or unreached gap, DELIVERED carrying none), and the completeness reconciliation scripts/refutation_gate.py already provides - so that the next M1 is a re-run of a committed instrument rather than a reconstruction. || CORRECTED W600 — THE SCHEMA HALF IS ALREADY DONE AND THIS ROW'S BASIS IS TEN ROUNDS STALE. The text above says 'the only committed fidelity workflow is scripts/workflows/fidelity_audit_v3.js'. MEASURED: scripts/workflows/fidelity_audit_v7.js is COMMITTED and tracked - W590, commit 41470fb2, whose own subject is 'MILESTONE M1 becomes runnable from this repository' - and it was written in response to THIS ROW (its header cites FU-418). Its FINDINGS schema requires section, verdict, tier, why_this_tier, vision_claim, observed, evidence; its VERDICTS schema requires index, refuted, corrected_verdict, corrected_tier, reason. Those are exactly the fields render_fidelity_ledger.py:162 standing_tier() reads (corrected_tier, else the finding's tier), so the M1 measure IS computable from this repository. It also carries the tier definitions and the v6 lesson that a refuter reporting only a verdict hides a tier they moved. WHAT REMAINS IS ONLY THE RUN. The Owner opted into that billed twelve-agent workflow on 2026-10-06b, for that purpose only. SEQUENCING CONSTRAINT: v7's prompt tells its agents a backend booted from HEAD is LIVE, so M1 needs a running backend and the shared stores - it must NEVER run beside a pytest suite (two suites against shared stores produced about forty false failures once already). It gets its own round, started early so it runs while the round prepares. NOTE FOR THE NEXT READER: this is the third row in one stretch whose stated basis had decayed (R13's deletion split was false, FU-367's hazard was false, this one was stale). followups.py satisfied could not see any of them - it matches rows whose NAMED FILES a later commit changed, and this row's basis was falsified by a file it does not name.

items.title: Every floor-served deliverable prints the platform's own house-style directive as its "Subject:", in the report body and in every downloaded file
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R1.0), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §10 — "Every solution is specifically designed … delivered end-to-end"; §15.6 "honesty over polish (never fabricate)". §13 — every deliverable is a living artefact the user exports. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce with brief "A 20-bed clinic in rural Kenya needs reliable power for vaccine refrigeration. Design and rank the best solution." returned content whose Executive Summary opens "Subject: Lead with the decision and its cost…" — the enterprise realm directive from agentic_core/taxonomy.py REALM_REGISTER, prepended to the prompt by agentic_core/api/deliverables.py:111-116. Cause: agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:137 `_subject()` searches 17 labels (User, Problem, Challenge, Objective, Mission, Concept, Topic, …) and "Brief" is NOT among them, while `_CONTENT_LABELS` at line 149 DOES list "Brief" — the two lists disagree, exactly the disagreement the function's own comment at lines 134-136 records for "Mission" and fixed only there. With no match, `_subject` falls through to "the longest sentence" in the prompt, which for all four realms is the directive's second sentence. The identical fallback in `_content` (line 163: `return … if vals else prompt`) makes POST /api/v1/qep/tajweed/lesson {rule_name:"Idgham"} print "## Terms most frequent in your request" over "triggers pronunciation · transliteration common · educational assistant · assistant supporting · generate structured · pronunciation guide" — six terms the learner never typed, lifted from the platform's own prompt; POST /api/v1/qep/adaptation/execute does the same. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/deliverables/deliv-ad0fddc5/export (executed, HTTP 200) returns the false Subject line two lines below the true "> **Brief:** A 20-bed clinic in rural Kenya…", so the artefact contradicts itself on page one; the same string is in the stored record, in `versions[0].content`, and in the .pdf/.docx/.xlsx writers (agentic_core/api/deliverables.py:727, 758, 832). apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/Deliverables.tsx:320-323 renders `selected.content` verbatim. Reproduced on a second surface: /api/v1/qep/tajweed/lesson, /api/v1/qep/adaptation/execute. WHY TIER 1: The sentence a reader is shown is "Subject: Lead with the decision and its cost, keep evidence tight, and prefer concrete numbers, timelines and owners over explanation of fundamentals. (domain: energy)." — the first line under the Executive Summary of a report whose brief was a Kenyan clinic losing vaccines. That is not an omission and not an environment fact: it is an affirmative statement naming the subject of the document, and it is false. The floor-provenance line directly above it ("composed by the deterministic native structured engine … arranges the headings it was asked for") discloses HOW the text was made but says nothing that makes this sentence true, so the disclosure does not pull it down to tier 2 or 3. The same root also makes the floor label its own prompt scaffolding as the learner's words (see `observed`), which is the same class of untruth on a QEP surface. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The surface discloses that the floor composed the text; it nowhere discloses that the "Subject:" line is the platform's own instruction rather than the user's subject, or that the "terms most frequent in your request" are not from the request. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: NOT REFUTED — reproduced verbatim, and larger than filed. Tier 1 is right and the assessor's own tier reasoning holds: the line is an affirmative statement naming the document's subject, and it is false — it is the platform's house-style instruction to itself. The floor-provenance line above it ("composed by the deterministic native structured engine … arranges the headings it was asked for") discloses HOW the text was made and says nothing that makes the Subject sentence true, so no disclosure pulls it to tier 2; and it is an assertion, not an omission, so it cannot fall to tier 3. Three corrections, all making it worse, none changing the tier: (a) the false subject is not confined to the Executive Summary — it is re-printed as the stated subject of EVERY section ("Native structured frame for 'Background' over: Lead with the decision and its cost…", likewise Analysis, Findings, Recommendations); (b) the exporters are four not three — PDF at deliverables.py:728, DOCX at 759, PPTX at 795 and XLSX at 838 each write d["content"] verbatim immediately after writing the true "Brief:" line, so every downloaded format contradicts itself on page one; (c) the same root defect leaks the raw prompt into the body of other floor surfaces — POST /api/v1/religion/halal-review prints "Native structured frame for 'Manufacturing Considerations' over: Product: Gelatin gummy … Conduct a pre-assessment and provide: ## Cross-Contamination Risks ## Manufacturing Consid", truncated mid-word, as its subject. Verdict PARTIAL stands: the run does produce a real deliverable with correctly grounded term extraction (vaccine refrigeration, rural kenya), so it is not a STUB; the defect is a truth defect inside working output. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce with the Kenyan-clinic brief (executed, HTTP 200, id deliv-0049e8bf) returned content whose Executive Summary first line is "Subject: Lead with the decision and its cost, keep evidence tight, and prefer concrete numbers, timelines and owners over explanation of fundamentals. (domain: energy)." GET /api/v1/deliverables/deliv-0049e8bf/export (HTTP 200) prints that line two lines under the TRUE "> **Brief:** A 20-bed clinic in rural Kenya…". Root cause confirmed by reading agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:137-139 — the _subject label tuple is (User, Problem, Challenge, Objective, Mission, Concept, Topic, Research question, Question, Task / question, Task, Hypothesis, Target role, Current situation, Concern, Subject, Search query); "Brief" is absent, while _CONTENT_LABELS at line 149 DOES contain "Brief". With no match, line 141-143 returns the longest sentence, which is the realm directive from taxonomy.py:40 prepended at deliverables.py:108-111. Reproduced on two further surfaces: POST /api/v1/qep/tajweed/lesson {rule_name:"Idgham"} prints the heading "## Terms most frequent in your request" over "triggers pronunciation · transliteration common · educational assistant · assistant supporting · generate structured · pronunciation guide" (the learner typed only "Idgham"; those terms come from the route's own role line and its "Include:" scaffold, via _content falling through to the whole prompt at line 165); POST /api/v1/qep/adaptation/execute {pattern:"font_size"} prints "The list below is the request's most frequent terms" over "cross-domain adaptation · adjustments expected · pedagogical pattern · adaptation engine · adapted mechanism". THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Add "Brief" (and "Title") to the label tuple in `_subject` at agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:137 so the brief wins, and make the longest-sentence fallback refuse rather than guess — emit "Subject: (not stated in the request)" and drop the term list when `_content` had to fall back to the whole prompt, rather than labelling scaffolding as the reader's words.
