items.title: The Religion hub's "Generate Class Report" button serves floor-composed Qur'an curriculum with no provenance badge, no AI-assisted label and no teache
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R1.1), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict STUB at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §11 rule 4 — "Floor-served output is never presented as scholarship or translation … every AI-served surface renders serving provenance (the shared amber 'structured floor — not model analysis' badge)"; §11 rule 5 — "AI content is labelled AI-assisted with provenance — never authoritative; learners are directed to qualified teachers." OBSERVED: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/LearnTeachModule.tsx:24-32 posts a hardcoded {subject:"Quran & Islamic Studies", level:"Intermediate", duration_weeks:12} to /api/v1/education/curriculum — the generic Education tool, not a Religion route — and lines 97-101 render `report` inside a bare `<pre>`. No provenanceBadge, no floor_note, no disclaimer, no scholar/teacher line, and the response's `ai_provenance` object is never read. The route itself returns no `disclaimer`, no `floor_note` and no `sections_withheld` keys, because it is not one of the four Religion handlers that were given them. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/education/curriculum {subject:"Quran & Islamic Studies",level:"Intermediate",duration_weeks:12} executed, HTTP 200. Response keys: curriculum_id, subject, level, duration_weeks, framework, curriculum, ai_provenance, generated_at — no disclaimer, no floor_note. Body opens "_Acting as: master curriculum designer with expertise in bloom._" and fills "## Week-by-Week Plan" with the floor's generic three-bullet plan ("Route richer generation to a model resource…"). Compare POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir, which returns both `floor_note` and a `disclaimer` and whose hub tab renders both. WHY TIER 1: A learner or teacher on /religion?tab=qep clicks a button labelled "Generate Class Report" and is shown a block of text beginning "_Acting as: master curriculum designer with expertise in bloom._" followed by "## Learning Objectives", "## Prerequisites", "## Week-by-Week Plan" for Qur'an & Islamic Studies. Two things a reader is told are untrue: that this is a report about their class (the card immediately above it says "No class roster exists on this deployment", and the subject/level/duration are hardcoded in the component, not chosen), and — by the complete absence of any label — that this is curriculum rather than a heading frame. This is not "no model ran" being held against the environment: the route's own payload carries `served_by: native` and `qms_basis: "not assessable — floor-served"`, and the component drops both. Every sibling Religion tool on the same hub renders `floor_note` and `disclaimer`; this one renders neither, so it is not a disclosed shortfall (tier 3) but an unlabelled assertion on the one surface §11 binds hardest. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. Nothing on the panel says the floor served it, that it is AI-assisted, or that it is not reviewed curriculum; the button's own label asserts a class report that does not exist. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: NOT REFUTED — reproduced. Tier 1 stands, but on different ground, because one of the assessor's two pillars is wrong and the task's own rules bar the other. WRONG: "the complete absence of any label" — the rendered <pre> DOES open with "_[Workstation native structured engine — owned, no external dependency]_", which is in the response body. BARRED: the missing badge/disclaimer/teacher line is an omission, and the task states an omission is not an assertion, so the absence of §11's labels cannot by itself be tier 1. What survives, and is enough, are the assertions. (a) The floor publishes "_Acting as: master curriculum designer with expertise in bloom._" over Qur'an & Islamic Studies content — §11 rule 4's exact prohibition, floor output presented as expert work, and the one marker line present boasts ownership rather than correcting it. (b) The button says "Generate Class Report"; A.6 feature 6 (Educator Platform & Class Management) is "not built", the subject/level/duration are hardcoded in the component, no roster exists, and the card two lines above says so — so the label asserts a report about a class that cannot exist. (c) "## Week-by-Week Plan" is a heading asserting a 12-week plan follows, and what follows is the floor's internal engineering instruction to route generation to a model. These are affirmative claims, not blanks, which is why this is tier 1 rather than tier 2; and nothing on the panel states the shortfall, so it is not tier 3. Verdict STUB stands: the surface offers a not-built capability by silently routing to the generic Education tool. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/LearnTeachModule.tsx:24-32 posts hardcoded {subject:"Quran & Islamic Studies", level:"Intermediate", duration_weeks:12} to /api/v1/education/curriculum and lines 97-101 render `report` in a bare <pre> — no provenanceBadge import, no floor_note, no disclaimer, no scholar/teacher line; the declared response type is only {curriculum?, output?}, so ai_provenance is structurally unread. POST /api/v1/education/curriculum with that exact body executed, HTTP 200; keys = curriculum_id, subject, level, duration_weeks, framework, curriculum, ai_provenance, generated_at — no disclaimer and no floor_note, confirming it is not one of the four religion.py handlers that carry them (contrast POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir, executed, which returns both). The curriculum body opens "_Acting as: master curriculum designer with expertise in bloom._" and its "## Week-by-Week Plan" contains exactly three bullets: "Validate the structured outputs above against the stated objective. / Route richer generation to a model resource (local-first; external only if enabled). / Iterate via the orchestrator's cascade for the stated domain; record outcomes to memory/UEG." Reached at /religion?tab=qep (App.tsx:179 → ReligionHub.tsx:117). ai_provenance does carry served_by "native" and qms_basis "not assessable — floor-served", both dropped by the component. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): In LearnTeachModule.tsx render `provenanceBadge(data.ai_provenance.served_by, …)` plus a fixed line — "Floor-served heading frame for Qur'an study, not reviewed curriculum; study with a qualified teacher" — above the `<pre>`, and rename the button to what it does ("Generate a study-plan frame"). Longer term the Religion hub should call a Religion route that carries `floor_note`/`disclaimer` like its four siblings, rather than the generic Education route.

items.title: The interfaith route is the one Religion tool with no disclaimer, no floor note and no withheld sections — it returns a scholar persona over three fai
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R1.2), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict API_ONLY at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §11 rule 4 — floor-served output is never presented as scholarship, and every AI-served surface renders serving provenance; §11 rule 5 — AI content labelled AI-assisted, never authoritative. OBSERVED: agentic_core/api/religion.py:569-614 `interfaith_dialogue` calls `ai_text(prompt, "religion_interfaith")` and returns {analysis_id, topic, traditions, dialogue_purpose, analysis, ai_provenance, generated_at}. There is no `_model_available()` check, no `_withhold_sections` call, no `floor_note` and no `disclaimer` — the four sibling handlers in the same file (lines 95-126, 176-207, 321-357, 521-555) all have every one of those. The leaked prompt scaffolding ("Structure as: ## Overview ## Islam's Perspective…") is reproduced inside the body of each section, and "## Islam's Perspective on charity" is filled with a commercial-service template ("Offering: what is delivered and the scope boundary. Delivery model… SLAs & assurance"). No UI reaches it: there is no interfaith entry in apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/toolRegistry.ts and no reference anywhere in src except an unrelated KnowledgeHub description string. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/religion/interfaith {"topic":"charity"} executed, HTTP 200. Response keys printed: ['analysis_id','topic','traditions','dialogue_purpose','analysis','ai_provenance','generated_at'] — `disclaimer` and `floor_note` absent. Body verified to contain the scholar persona line and the four tradition headings with the service template under the Islam heading. WHY TIER 1: The reached form of an API-only surface is its response body, and that body opens "_Acting as: scholar of comparative religion and interfaith dialogue._" and then publishes "## Islam's Perspective on charity", "## Christianity's Perspective on charity", "## Judaism's Perspective on charity", "## Points of Convergence". Those headings assert that each tradition's position is stated below. Nothing was looked up, and — unlike the fatwa, hadith, tafsir and halal routes, each of which withholds its scholarly sections and says so — this payload contains no `disclaimer`, no `floor_note` and no `sections_withheld` key, so no sentence anywhere in it corrects the claim. An omission would be tier 2; a persona claim plus substantive headings with no label is an assertion, and §11 rule 4 names exactly this. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The payload carries `ai_provenance.served_by: "native"`, which a caller must interpret; no sentence in the response says no comparative analysis happened. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: NOT REFUTED — reproduced, and worse than filed. Tier 1 stands. An API-only surface's reached form is its response body, and that body makes two assertions nothing behind it supports: a persona claim ("_Acting as: scholar of comparative religion and interfaith dialogue._") and four substantive headings each asserting that a named tradition's position on charity is stated below. §11 rule 4 names exactly this. It cannot fall to tier 2 because a persona plus substantive headings is an assertion, not a blank field; it cannot fall to tier 3 because no sentence in the payload states the shortfall. One correction to the assessor's reasoning, which overstates: "no sentence anywhere in it corrects the claim" is not quite true — most sections do carry "The list below is the request's most frequent terms, not findings about them." But that line qualifies only the term list, says nothing about the floor or about scholarship, and — decisively — the "## Islam's Perspective on charity" section, the one filled with the SLA/delivery-model template, carries no honest line at all. Two further aggravations the assessor missed: the raw prompt scaffold is republished inside each section body, and the route is the only one of five in religion.py with no _model_available guard, so if a model were ever provisioned it would also be the only one that could not refuse a floor answer the way tafsir and halal-review do. Verdict API_ONLY confirmed independently. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/religion.py:570-614 read in full: interfaith_dialogue calls ai_text(prompt, "religion_interfaith") and returns {analysis_id, topic, traditions, dialogue_purpose, analysis, ai_provenance, generated_at}. No _model_available() check, no _withhold_sections call, no floor_note, no disclaimer — the four siblings in the same file (quran-tafsir, hadith, fatwa/dialogue, halal-review) each have all of them; I executed halal-review and quran-tafsir and both returned sections_withheld + floor_note + disclaimer. POST /api/v1/religion/interfaith {"topic":"charity"} executed, HTTP 200; keys printed ['analysis_id','topic','traditions','dialogue_purpose','analysis','ai_provenance','generated_at'] — disclaimer, floor_note and sections_withheld all absent. The body opens "_Acting as: scholar of comparative religion and interfaith dialogue._" then "## Overview", "## Islam's Perspective on charity", "## Christianity's Perspective on charity", "## Judaism's Perspective on charity", "## Points of Convergence". Under "## Islam's Perspective on charity" the floor prints a commercial-services template: "Offering: what is delivered and the scope boundary. / Delivery model: how it is provided (cadence, channel, roles). / Quality measure for charity. / SLAs & assurance: the commitments and how they're governed for the stated domain." The prompt's own scaffold ("Structure as: ## Overview ## Islam's Perspective on charity …") is reproduced verbatim inside every section body. Reachability: grep over apps/workstation-superapp/src returns 3 hits for "interfaith", all in one unrelated string — KnowledgeHub.tsx:99 'Cross-domain synthesis and interfaith dialogue.' No toolRegistry entry, no route. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Give `interfaith_dialogue` the same three lines its four siblings have: gate on `_model_available()`, pass the per-tradition perspective headings and Points of Convergence/Divergence to `_withhold_sections`, and return a `floor_note` plus a `disclaimer` saying nothing was researched and no tradition's position was looked up.

items.title: The shipped repo manifest reports 13 of 29 files and calls the generated Website, Web app and Phone app "(scaffold)" — and swears it counted every fil
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R2.0), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §13 — the canonical output is a Repository of the IDBO Entity shipped as a coherent, version-controlled whole that integrates a Website, a Web app and a Phone (mobile) app. OBSERVED: ship_vsb_repo (agentic_core/api/vsb.py:368) runs its generators in the order repo → website → webapp → mobile → board_pack. generate_vsb_repo writes manifest.json FIRST, while `_generated = {website: (root/'web'/'site.json').exists(), ...}` is still all False and only 13 files exist. The three surface generators then write 16 more files and their own manifests; nothing ever re-writes the repo manifest. So every entity shipped at establish time carries a permanently 16-file-short manifest that labels all three §13 surfaces as scaffolds, with stale=false. Re-POSTing /repo by hand afterwards fixes it (vsb-9313233561 then reported file_count 27 and "web/ (generated — index · about · solution)"), which is how I isolated the ordering. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/genesis/establish -> vsb-a42ca383af, initial_ship {shipped:true, coherent_whole:true, surfaces:[board_pack,mobile,repo,webapp,website], commit 9f69db933014}. GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-a42ca383af/repo -> file_count 13, total_bytes 10901, integrated_surfaces all "(scaffold)", ship_status {stale:false, shipped_at 2026-10-05T14:47:28Z}, manifest generated_at 14:47:23Z. `find C:/tmp/m1data2/data/vsb_repos/vsb-a42ca383af -type f -not -path ./.git/* -not -name manifest.json | wc -l` -> 29. `git log --oneline` in that root -> 4 commits (9f69db9 mobile, f281f28 webapp, 6d86547 website, 341aeb5 repo). Reader: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/VSBCockpit.tsx:238-239 and :1195 (`repoTree.map`). WHY TIER 1: GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-a42ca383af/repo returns `file_count: 13`, `total_bytes: 10901`, a 13-entry `tree`, `integrated_surfaces: {website: "web/index.html (scaffold)", webapp: "webapp/ (scaffold)", mobile: "mobile/ (scaffold)"}`, `ship_status.stale: false` — and a `count_basis` that states in words "every file on disk under the repository root except .git and this manifest". 29 files are on disk. The sixteen missing ones are the founder's entire §13 output: web/about.html, web/solution.html, web/styles.css, web/site.json, webapp/index.html, webapp/app.js, webapp/data.json, mobile/index.html, mobile/sw.js, mobile/icon.svg and the rest. This is not an omission — `count_basis` asserts the count is complete and `integrated_surfaces` asserts three directories are scaffolds that were generated five seconds later, so a reader is told something untrue rather than merely left uninformed. Not tier 2 because VSBCockpit.tsx:238 feeds exactly this `tree` into the repo browser a founder clicks, so the untrue list is the surface itself, not a hidden field. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the opposite. ship_status.stale is false and count_basis claims a complete disk count. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: CONFIRMED, tier 1 held, and the finding UNDERSTATES its own scope in two ways I corrected. (a) The assessor's mechanism is wrong: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:428-432 does count from disk (`for _p in sorted(root.rglob('*'))`), not from `written` — the defect is purely the ship ORDERING at vsb.py:2406-2407 (repo generator first, then website/webapp/mobile write 16 more files and nothing re-writes the repo manifest). (b) Far more consequential: the assessor said re-POSTing /repo afterwards fixes it and implied this is an establish-time-only artefact. It is not. I ran POST /{id}/repo/ship — §13's own canonical 'one deliberate act' route — on a cleanly gated entity and the manifest came back 13 files again, because the ship re-runs the repo generator first every single time. So EVERY path the system offers produces the short manifest; only a hand-crafted bare POST /repo after a ship repairs it. Tier 1 rather than 2: `count_basis` asserts in words 'every file on disk under the repository root except .git and this manifest', `integrated_surfaces` asserts three directories are scaffolds when generated apps are in them, `x-repo-missing: none` asserts nothing is absent, and the Cockpit's own button reads 'Download all 13 file(s) as a zip' on a 29-file repository — four affirmative statements, each untrue, none an omission. Tier 1 rather than 3 because the manifest tree is also the download ALLOW-LIST (vsb.py:_repo_resolved_path), so the founder's website and apps are not merely unlisted, they are unreachable by file and absent from the zip — the surface both misstates and withholds. This is the most consequential finding in R2. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/genesis/establish (no bodies) -> vsb-cdc8805381, initial_ship {shipped:true, coherent_whole:true, surfaces:[board_pack,mobile,repo,webapp,website], commit e434616ebc48}. GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-cdc8805381/repo -> file_count 13, total_bytes 10181, a 13-path tree, integrated_surfaces {website:'web/index.html (scaffold)', webapp:'webapp/ (scaffold)', mobile:'mobile/ (scaffold)'}, ship_status {stale:false}. Walked C:/tmp/m1data2/data/vsb_repos/vsb-cdc8805381 excluding .git and manifest.json -> 29 files, 72703 bytes (web/about.html, web/solution.html, web/site.json, web/styles.css, webapp/index.html, webapp/app.js, webapp/app.json, webapp/data.json, webapp/styles.css, mobile/index.html, mobile/app.js, mobile/app.json, mobile/data.json, mobile/styles.css, mobile/sw.js, mobile/icon.svg all absent from the manifest). GET /repo/file?path=web/about.html -> 404 "'web/about.html' is not a file this repo declares ... 13 file(s) are declared." GET /repo/zip -> 200, content-length 7361, x-repo-files 13, x-repo-declared 13, x-repo-missing: none. SECOND, HARDER REPRODUCTION on the explicit canonical act: vsb-5f26b5c0c4, gate approved, POST /repo/ship -> 200 {shipped:true, coherent_whole:true, surfaces_shipped: all five} and GET /repo STILL reports file_count 13, integrated_surfaces all '(scaffold)', zip content-length 8089 / x-repo-files 13. Renderer: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/VSBCockpit.tsx:1163 button text 'Download all {repoTree.length} file(s) as a zip' and :1195 repoTree.map. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): In ship_vsb_repo (agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2402), move "repo" to the END of the generator tuple (or re-run generate_vsb_repo after the loop), so the manifest the Cockpit reads is written against the finished disk and `_generated` is true when integrated_surfaces is computed.

items.title: An entity established with no concept, design or commercialisation ships a README saying every §4 section is composed
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R2.1), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict STUB at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §4.1-§4.10 — one continuous lifecycle in which each stage is actually composed, verified, tested and validated before the VSB is established and output. OBSERVED: _resolve_body_fields (agentic_core/api/genesis.py:971) computes `is_floor = bool(text.strip()) and ...`, so an EMPTY body field is recorded as pending=False, i.e. "not awaiting the owned model". _derived_stage (agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1660) then walks body_pending, finds no gap, and emits the "(every §4 section on this entity is composed)" clause. The function's own docstring was written to kill exactly this defect ("the entity said in one field that it had commercialised and in the next that it had not composed its concept") — it fixed the pending case and left the empty case, which now reads as the strongest possible claim. The journey path is honest by contrast: the same template printed "Stage: no stage reached · Status: held · no §4 lifecycle stage is reached: the first section (concept) still awaits the owned model" for vsb-9313233561. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/genesis/establish {problem, domain:agriculture, realm:physical, name:"TamrCool Cooperative"} (no concept/design/commercialisation) -> vsb-a42ca383af, body_pending {concept:false, design:false, commercialisation:false, operations:false}, stage "commercialisation". GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-a42ca383af -> genesis_blueprint {"concept":"","design":"","commercialisation":""}, stage_basis "...(every §4 section on this entity is composed)". C:/tmp/m1data2/data/vsb_repos/vsb-a42ca383af/README.md lines 5-7; BUSINESS_PLAN.md "## Concept" followed by a blank line. Renderers: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:117 (README), VSBCockpit.tsx:676-681 (badge + stage_basis), vsb.py:1362 (Board Pack operational layer). WHY TIER 1: The shipped README.md and the VSB Cockpit both print: "**Stage:** commercialisation" and "**Stage basis:** the furthest §4 section composed with no gap before it: commercialisation (every §4 section on this entity is composed)". In the same repository, IDENTITY.md shows `"concept": "", "design": "", "commercialisation": ""` and BUSINESS_PLAN.md has three empty headings. Zero §4 sections are composed; the sentence says all of them are. That is an affirmative false statement about the entity's own state, not a blank field, so it is not the "omission is not an assertion" case; and it is not tier 2 because nothing anywhere qualifies it — the two honest files in the same repo (OPERATIONS.md, EVIDENCE.md) say "Not provided at establishment" one directory over, which makes the README's claim read as deliberate. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the README states the inverse of the truth, and the Cockpit repeats it verbatim. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: CONFIRMED exactly as described, tier 1 held. The bug is one `bool(text.strip()) and` in genesis.py:969 that collapses 'this field is empty' into 'this field is not awaiting the owned model', and _derived_stage — a function written specifically to kill the inverse of this defect, per its own docstring — then reads that as composition. Tier 1 rather than 2: the reader is shown the sentence '(every §4 section on this entity is composed)' in the shipped README and on the Cockpit badge while IDENTITY.md one directory over shows three empty strings and BUSINESS_PLAN.md shows three empty headings. That is an affirmative false statement about the entity's own state, so the 'an omission is not an assertion' carve-out does not reach it. Tier 1 rather than 3 because nothing qualifies it — and the qualification exists in the same repository (OPERATIONS.md and EVIDENCE.md both print 'Not provided at establishment'), which is what makes the README's claim read as deliberate rather than as a gap. Verdict STUB is right: the stage field and its basis are a surface that pretends. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/genesis/establish {problem, domain:agriculture, realm:physical, name:'RefuteCool Cooperative'} with no concept/design/commercialisation -> vsb-cdc8805381, body_pending {concept:false, design:false, commercialisation:false, operations:false}. GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-cdc8805381 -> stage 'commercialisation', stage_basis 'the furthest §4 section composed with no gap before it: commercialisation (every §4 section on this entity is composed)', genesis_blueprint {'concept':'','design':'','commercialisation':''}. Shipped C:/tmp/m1data2/data/vsb_repos/vsb-cdc8805381/README.md line 5-7: '**Stage:** commercialisation · **Status:** registered - not operating' / '**Stage basis:** ... (every §4 section on this entity is composed)'. BUSINESS_PLAN.md: '## Concept' followed by a blank line, '## Design & Development' blank, '## Commercialisation' blank. Mechanism: agentic_core/api/genesis.py:969 `is_floor = bool(text.strip()) and (...)` -> an empty field yields pending=False; agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1659-1695 _derived_stage then finds no gap and emits the all-composed clause. Contrast in the same install: the journey-established vsb-5f26b5c0c4 (bodies genuinely pending) honestly reports body_pending all true and status 'held'. Renderer: VSBCockpit.tsx:676. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): In _resolve_body_fields (agentic_core/api/genesis.py:971) record an empty body field as pending too (`pending[field] = True` when `not text.strip()`), so _derived_stage sees the gap; and make the "every §4 section is composed" clause in agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1700 require non-empty text rather than merely `pend[k] is False`.

items.title: The VSB Spawn Studio tells the user "VSB is now operational" one line after the server saved its status as "body pending"
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R2.2), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict STUB at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §4.8/§4.10 — the established VSB self-operates and forever runs, defends, heals, learns, improves and grows; §15.6 honesty over polish, never fabricate. OBSERVED: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2369 `yield _event("complete", "VSB Operational", f"VSB {vsb_id} is now operational.", {...})`. The entity it refers to has ceo_specification = "content pending the owned model — this enterprise has not yet composed its own CEO specification", status "body pending", stage null, and the living roster reports autonomous_cycles false for every entity, so nothing tends it. The rest of this same stream is scrupulous (it says the six cognitive engines "return fixed markers rather than reading the challenge" and that the constitutional gate was "NOT evaluated"), which makes the final line the one unguarded claim. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/vsb/spawn {challenge:"Cold-chain loss for 40 date farms in Medina...",name:"SpawnTamr",scope:"commercialise"} -> last SSE frame `label "VSB Operational", content "VSB vsb-4620d8faab is now operational.", elapsed_seconds 0.81`. GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-4620d8faab -> status "body pending", status_basis "1 body section(s) still await the owned model: ceo_specification", stage null. Renderer: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/VSBSpawnStudio.tsx:317,320; route registered at App.tsx:189-190 (/vsb and /vsb-spawn). WHY TIER 1: The terminal SSE event is `{"stage":"complete","label":"VSB Operational","content":"VSB vsb-4620d8faab is now operational."}`, and VSBSpawnStudio.tsx:317/320 renders `{ev.label}` and `{ev.content}` straight into the page with a Sparkles icon in the accent colour. Six lines earlier in the same generator the server computed `_derived_status(vsb_entity)` -> ("body pending", "1 body section(s) still await the owned model: ceo_specification") and persisted it. The user is shown "operational"; the record says otherwise. That is a positive false claim on a page a person uses, not a disclosed gap — the honest string already exists in the same function and is simply not the one emitted. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the stream's own final word is "operational". THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: CONFIRMED by execution, tier 1 held. The honest string is computed, assigned to vsb_entity['status'] and written to disk SIX LINES ABOVE the event that contradicts it, in the same generator. Tier 1 rather than 2: 'VSB vsb-3f7557af27 is now operational.' is a positive assertion of an outcome the platform's own persisted record denies in the same request; it is not a blank field and not a hedged one. Tier 1 rather than 3 because the stream does not state this shortfall anywhere — and the contrast is damning, since the same stream candidly labels its own frames 'Six Cognitive Engines (fixed responses)', 'Cascade Complete (fixed markers)' and 'CEO Strategy Pending'. The one line that is not candid is the last thing the user reads. Verdict STUB: the terminal frame is a surface that pretends an operating enterprise exists 1.27 seconds after a form submit. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/vsb/spawn {challenge:'Cold-chain loss for 40 date farms in Medina...', name:'RefuteSpawn', scope:'commercialise'} -> 15 SSE frames, terminal frame verbatim: data: {"stage": "complete", "label": "VSB Operational", "content": "VSB vsb-3f7557af27 is now operational.", "data": {... "elapsed_seconds": 1.27}}. GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-3f7557af27 -> status 'body pending', status_basis '1 body section(s) still await the owned model: ceo_specification', stage null, stage_basis 'the body-pending map names no §4 lifecycle section (it holds ceo_specification), so the stage reached is NOT KNOWN'. GET /api/v1/economy/living-vsbs -> autonomous_cycles false, autonomous_cycles_note 'OFF — the heartbeat's Self-run lever is off'. Code: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2359-2364 computes and PERSISTS _derived_status(vsb_entity) -> ('body pending', ...), then vsb.py:2371 yields the 'VSB Operational' / 'is now operational.' event. Renderer: VSBSpawnStudio.tsx:317 {ev.label} and :320 {ev.content}, route /vsb and /vsb-spawn (App.tsx:189-190). THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Build the terminal event from the values computed immediately above it: `yield _event("complete", f"VSB {_st}", f"VSB {vsb_id}: {_st_basis}", {...})` at agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2369.

items.title: The Organism page's green "operational" count and readiness percentage are computed from two status words no writer produces any more
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R2.3), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §4.10 — Run · Defend · Heal · Learn · Improve · Grow, forever; §15.6 never fabricate a figure. OBSERVED: agentic_core/api/organism_status.py:123 fixes the predicate to ("operational","active"). The comment above it records the previous half of this same bug ("W438 — the only status the VSB writer persists is 'operational'; this counted 'active'") — then W496 replaced the literal statuses with derived ones ("operating", "body pending", "held", "registered - not operating") and this reader was not moved with them. The same `operational` value feeds `vsb_operational: operational > 0` (:487) and `commercialisation_readiness` (:476), so one stale vocabulary drives a boolean, a count and a percentage. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/organism/lifecycle -> `"vsb_operational": true, "vsb_entities": {"total": 6, "operational": 1, "by_status": {"active": 1, "body pending": 3, "held": 1, "registered - not operating": 1}}, "commercialisation_readiness": 0.0833, basis "0.5 x project commercialisation_rate (0.0) + 0.5 x VSB operational share (1/6)"`. The one "active" record is C:/tmp/m1data2/data/vsb_entities/vsb-0a6ca2ab.json with vsb_id null and name null. GET /api/v1/economy/living-vsbs -> every row operating_cycles 0, last_operated null. Renderer: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/organism/OrganismAnatomy.tsx:79,278,280. WHY TIER 1: OrganismAnatomy.tsx:278 renders `<Chip tone="ok">1 operational</Chip>` and :280 renders "Readiness 8%" with the basis "0.5 x VSB operational share (1/6)". No entity is operating: the living roster reports autonomous_cycles false, and the six stored entities hold statuses "body pending" x3, "held", "registered - not operating", and one malformed legacy record whose status literal is "active" and whose vsb_id and name are both null. The counter `operational = sum(n for s, n in by_status.items() if s in ("operational", "active"))` matches only the vocabulary W496 abolished, so it counts the broken record and can NEVER count the status _derived_status actually returns ("operating"). A reader is shown a green count of 1 and a quantified readiness figure derived from it; both are untrue, and the number is displayed, not merely stored — so tier 1 rather than tier 2. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the chip carries the 'ok' (green) tone and the basis line names a share that is itself wrong. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: CONFIRMED by execution, tier 1 held — and one factual correction that makes it WORSE, not better. The assessor called the counted record 'a malformed legacy record'. It is not legacy: it was written today at 14:50 by agentic_core/api/synthesis_studio.py:320, which is a live, routed establishment writer that stores `status: "active"` as a literal and never calls _derived_status. So the organism's green 'operational' chip is not counting a stale artefact, it is structurally counting exactly and only the entities born down the one path that bypasses the derivation — and it can never count the status the derivation actually returns ('operating'), because 'operating' is not in the predicate's tuple. Tier 1 rather than 2: OrganismAnatomy.tsx:278 renders a green chip reading '1 operational' and :280 a quantified 'Readiness 6%' whose own basis sentence names 'VSB operational share (1/8)'. No entity is operating — autonomous_cycles is false, so by the platform's own definition nothing tends any of them. A displayed count and a displayed percentage are both untrue, and a fabricated figure is named in the tier-1 definition. Tier 1 rather than 3 because nothing on the card qualifies the number; the basis line beside it repeats the wrong share rather than correcting it. Verdict PARTIAL is right (the lifecycle route is real and mostly honest; one counter's vocabulary is stale). THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/organism/lifecycle (live, twice) -> first: vsb_operational true, vsb_entities {total:6, operational:1, by_status:{active:1, 'body pending':3, held:1, 'registered - not operating':1}}, commercialisation_readiness 0.0833, basis '0.5 x project commercialisation_rate (0.0) + 0.5 x VSB operational share (1/6)'. After my three establishments: {total:8, operational:1, by_status:{active:1, 'body pending':4, held:1, 'registered - not operating':2}}, readiness 0.0625, basis '... (1/8)'. Counter: agentic_core/api/organism_status.py:123 `operational = sum(n for s, n in by_status.items() if s in ('operational','active'))`. Every return of _derived_status (agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1634,1638,1644,1647,1650) is one of 'held', 'body pending', 'registered - not operating', 'registered - operation unknown', 'operating' — 'operational' and 'active' are unreachable from it. The single counted record is C:/tmp/m1data2/data/vsb_entities/vsb-0a6ca2ab.json: status 'active', vsb_id null, name null, created_at 2026-10-05T14:50:24Z, keyed on entity_id. Its writer is LIVE: agentic_core/api/synthesis_studio.py:320 `"status": "active"` (also :409, and capital_fund.py:285). GET /api/v1/economy/living-vsbs -> autonomous_cycles false. Renderers: OrganismAnatomy.tsx:278 <Chip tone={life.vsb_operational ? 'ok' : 'dim'}>{life.vsb_entities.operational} operational</Chip>, :280 'Readiness {pct(...)}' plus the basis line at :281. THE VISION CLAIM: §5: "The Chief owns the living Business Plan … and the Chief delivers it via Strategy and a living Roadmap"; the AI CEO "receives the action plan" and the chat's own greeting promises "I answer from the record, and every answer says who served it." Reached at /ceo (LivingOrganisationHub default tab). WHY TIER 1: The answer a reader is shown contains the literal lines "## Living plan
- Validate the structured outputs above against the stated objective.
- Route richer generation to a model resource (local-first; external only if enabled).

"No model ran" is not the complaint: the floor serving is the environment, and the floor is labelled; the defect is that the floor's own boilerplate is served under headings naming the founder's records with no conflict chip. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partially — one of three fabricated sections is flagged; the other two are shown with no mark. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: Reproduced, and the defect is WIDER than the assessor stated — so tier 1 stands and the finding should not be softened. The detector is not merely single-key: it is gated on the count being 0 or None, so on any scope that HAS records it does not run at all. In my run two real board directives and three real objectives existed, grounding_conflicts came back EMPTY, and the answer still printed the floor's three generic bullets under '## Board directives' instead of either of the two recorded directives, and under '## Living plan' and '## Business plan for this scope' while those records hold three objectives and four empty fields. The page therefore shows a reader a grey chip reading 'grounded in 2 directives · 3 objectives' over text that recites none of them, with no amber chip anywhere — the one instrument built to catch exactly this (W574) is structurally unable to fire on a populated scope. Tier 1 rather than 2 because these are assertions about the content of the founder's own stored records, not blank fields: '## Business plan for this scope' followed by bullets is a claim about what that plan says. Tier 1 rather than 3 because nothing on the surface qualifies it — the floor IS labelled, which is honest provenance, but provenance does not disclose that the headings name records whose content is absent. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v138/ceo/chat {scope: workstation}. Final event: grounding {directives: 2, objectives: 3, plan_score: 0.3, debate_entries: 0}, grounding_conflicts []. items.title: The living Roadmap's "current phase" and "next milestone" are ordered by the order objectives were typed in, not by time, so it names a 2026 Q4 phase
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R3.1), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §5: the Chief "delivers it via Strategy and a living Roadmap: a time-phased view of the objectives (phases · per-phase progress · current phase · next milestone) that updates as the plan progresses". OBSERVED: Three objectives were added in the order Q4 2026, "next review" (written by the Chief-instruct fallback), Q1 2026. GET /api/v1/business-plan/roadmap then returned phase order ['Q4 2026', 'next review', 'Q1 2026'], current_phase 'Q4 2026', next_milestone the Q4 objective. `_roadmap` builds an `order` list by first appearance of the free-text `timeline` string and takes `current = next(p for p in phase_list if not p["complete"])` — the first incomplete phase in ENTRY order. Nothing parses the timeline, so a placeholder like "next review" also becomes a roadmap phase. The per-phase progress and overall progress arithmetic are correct and do update; the ordering is the defect. EVIDENCE: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/business_plan.py:171-213 (`order.append(tl)` at :183, `current = next((p for p in phase_list if not p["complete"]), None)` at :199); rendered at C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/BusinessPlan.tsx:204 ("overall {pct}% · current: {current_phase}") and :218 ("Next milestone: …"). WHY TIER 1: The surface shows the founder `"current_phase": "Q4 2026"` and `"next_milestone": {"phase": "Q4 2026", "title": "Commission the Birmingham filtration pilot"}` while the same response's phase list reads `["Q4 2026", "next review", "Q1 2026"]` with the Q1 2026 objective at 0% and status planned. "Next milestone" is a definite claim about which objective comes next in TIME — that is the word the vision and the field names use — and the claim is wrong. It is not tier 2, because the shortfall is not a missing field but a specific wrong answer; it is not tier 3, because the only note on the surface is "Living roadmap derived from the plan's objectives — it updates as objectives progress", which never says the phases are in entry order. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the note says the roadmap is derived from the objectives and updates; it does not say the phase order is the order they were entered. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: Reproduced exactly, and the defect is reachable without any contrived input: the 'next review' phase was written by the platform's OWN chief_instruct fallback (plan objective obj-cd78bf1a carries source 'chief_instruct_fallback', timeline 'next review'), so the platform itself injects a non-temporal placeholder into what it calls a time-phased roadmap. Tier 1 rather than 2 because 'current_phase' and 'next_milestone' are not blank fields — they are specific answers to a question about time, and the answers are wrong: the founder is shown 'current: Q4 2026' and 'Next milestone: Commission the Birmingham filtration pilot (Q4 2026)' while the same response carries an incomplete Q1 2026 phase at 0% sitting last. Tier 1 rather than 3 because the only note on the surface says the roadmap is derived from the objectives and updates as they progress; nothing says the phases are in the order the objectives were entered, and the highlighted card compounds it by visually marking the wrong phase as current. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Executed GET /api/v1/business-plan/roadmap?scope=workstation: phases in order [{'timeline':'Q4 2026',...},{'timeline':'next review',...},{'timeline':'Q1 2026','progress_pct':0,'complete':false,'objectives':[{'title':'Secure the Q1 water-quality permit','status':'planned'}]}], current_phase 'Q4 2026', next_milestone {'phase':'Q4 2026','title':'Commission the Birmingham filtration pilot','progress_pct':0}, note 'Living roadmap derived from the plan's objectives — it updates as objectives progress.' Code at C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/business_plan.py:176-199: `order.append(tl)` on first appearance of the raw `timeline` string (:183) and `current = next((p for p in phase_list if not p["complete"]), None)` (:199) — no parse of the timeline anywhere. Render at apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/BusinessPlan.tsx:204 ('overall {overall_progress_pct}% · current: {current_phase}'), :218 ('Next milestone: {title} ({phase})'), and :208 which highlights the phase card matching current_phase. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Either sort `order` by a parsed date and refuse to phase an unparseable timeline (park those under an explicit "Unscheduled" phase excluded from current/next), or — if free text must stay — rename the fields to `first_incomplete_phase`/`first_incomplete_objective` and state on the surface that phases are listed in the order objectives were added.

items.title: The org cascade's governance verdict says both "The delivery's content was NOT screened" and content_screened: true, and the Swarm tab shows the false
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R3.2), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §5: "Change Control (arms-length Agency) — governs all change at arm's length from operations"; §17.5: "mandatory GaaS gate on every output". OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/swarm/cascade returned governance = {status: allowed, scope: "…The delivery's content was NOT screened…", screened: "intent + domain + the delivered content of every tier", content_screened: true, content_chars: 38253, tiers_screened: [15 tiers], content_compliant: true}. W505 genuinely closed the gap W494 had labelled — the post gate now reads all 38,253 characters — but the fix overrode `screened` and `content_screened` and left `scope` at the shared `INTENT_GATE_SCOPE` constant whose whole purpose is to say content was not read. EVIDENCE: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/gaas/v5/__init__.py:24-26 (INTENT_GATE_SCOPE) and :33 (`intent_gate_result` seeds scope + content_screened: False); C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/swarm.py:1002-1008 (the override that omits `scope`); rendered at C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/organism/SwarmIntelligence.tsx:290-295 — `title={cascade.governance.scope}`, and the " · content not screened" suffix is correctly suppressed, so the chip and its own tooltip disagree. WHY TIER 1: One response object carries `"scope": "intent + domain only — this gate screened the request's intent label against the prohibited list and its own constant attestation sentence. The delivery's content was NOT screened, so this verdict is not a judgement on what was produced."` beside `"screened": "intent + domain + the delivered content of every tier"`, `"content_screened": true`, `"content_chars": 38253` and 15 named tiers. The `scope` sentence is false for this emitter — the content WAS screened — and it is the string the UI puts in the chip's tooltip, so a reader who hovers is told the opposite of what happened. It is an assertion, not an omission, so tier 1 rather than 2; and it is not a disclosed shortfall, because the two fields contradict each other and nothing tells the reader which to believe. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the contradiction is the disclosure failure; a hover tells the reader the content was not screened. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: Reproduced exactly by execution. One response object carries two statements about the same act that cannot both be true: `scope` says the delivery's content was NOT screened, while `content_screened: true`, `content_chars: 35123` and fifteen named tiers say it was. The `scope` sentence is the false one for this emitter, and it is precisely the string the UI hands to the chip's `title`, so the only extra information a reader can get by hovering the governance chip is the opposite of what happened. Tier 1 rather than 2 because this is an assertion, not an omission — a sentence stating that content was not screened, shown over a gate that read 35,123 characters. Tier 1 rather than 3 because a self-contradiction is not a disclosed shortfall: nothing in the response or on the page tells the reader which of the two fields to believe, and the suffix mechanism that would have warned them is (correctly, for this emitter) switched off, leaving the false sentence as the only narrative. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v1/swarm/cascade {mission, domain: engineering}. governance returned: status 'allowed'; scope 'intent + domain only — this gate screened the request's intent label against the prohibited list and its own constant attestation sentence. The delivery's content was NOT screened, so this verdict is not a judgement on what was produced.'; screened 'intent + domain + the delivered content of every tier'; content_screened true; content_chars 35123; tiers_screened 15 named tiers (Chief … Build-to-Order); content_compliant true. Code: agentic_core/gaas/v5/__init__.py:24-26 defines INTENT_GATE_SCOPE and :31-35 seeds scope + content_screened False; agentic_core/api/swarm.py:1002-1013 overrides screened/content_screened/content_chars/tiers_screened and never replaces `scope`. Render: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/organism/SwarmIntelligence.tsx:290-295 — `title={cascade.governance.scope}` on the chip, with the ' · content not screened' suffix correctly suppressed by `content_screened === false`. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Give `intent_gate_result` a `scope` argument (or add a `content_gate_result` sibling) so an emitter that screens the content replaces the sentence rather than appending a contradicting field, and make the SwarmIntelligence tooltip read `governance.content_screen_basis` when `content_screened` is true.

items.title: /api/v1/organism/cadence reports a stale beat as "what the most recent heartbeat managed", because last_cadence is only written on a beat that refresh
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R3.4), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §17.3: the Strategic layer refreshes "quarterly + market signal" and the Action Plan "weekly + KPI-triggered" as continuously-maintained layers — so whether the cadence is firing NOW is the fact this surface exists to answer. OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/organism/cadence returned last_beat.at = 2026-10-05T14:45:21Z with refreshed = the two boot refreshes, while /api/v1/heartbeat/status at the same moment showed 10 beats and last_beat 2026-10-05T14:53:22Z. The heartbeat assigns `self.last_cadence` only inside `if _refreshed or _cad_failed:`, so every beat on which nothing was due leaves the previous beat's record in place and the route republishes it as the latest. The cadence itself is real and heartbeat-driven, and its per-refresh provenance ("DERIVED from the plan's own stored state by this module - no model composed it") is exemplary — this is a reporting defect on top of working machinery. EVIDENCE: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:287-294 (`if _refreshed or _cad_failed:` guarding the assignment); C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/organism_status.py:699-723 (builds `last_beat` from `heartbeat.last_cadence` and the basis sentence). API_ONLY — no frontend file references /organism/cadence, so the reached form is this response body. WHY TIER 1: The response asserts `"last_beat": {"ran": true, "at": "2026-10-05T14:45:21Z", …}` under `"last_beat_basis": "`layers` is the plan's own record of when each layer last refreshed; `last_beat` is what the most recent heartbeat managed."` At the moment of the read, GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status reported `beats: 10, last_beat: "2026-10-05T14:53:22Z"` — eight minutes and roughly eight beats later. So the named timestamp is not the most recent heartbeat, and the sentence saying it is, is untrue. That is an assertion, not an omission, so not tier 2; and it is not tier 3 because the handler's own reading rule ("A layer that is DUE while last_beat.could_not_run is set means the cadence is not firing") instructs the reader to draw a conclusion from a field that can be arbitrarily old — a single failed beat would leave `could_not_run` standing as a report that the cadence is not firing long after it recovered. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the basis sentence states the opposite of the field's actual meaning. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: Reproduced with a wider gap than the assessor measured (26 beats rather than 8). Tier 1 rather than 2 because the defect is not a missing field but a sentence the handler itself publishes: last_beat_basis states that `last_beat` is what the most recent heartbeat managed, and the named timestamp is 26 minutes older than the most recent heartbeat. `ran: true` alongside a stale `at` is an assertion about which beat this was, not a blank. Tier 1 rather than 3 because the handler goes further and instructs the reader how to draw a conclusion from the field — 'A layer that is DUE while last_beat.could_not_run is set means the cadence is not firing' — which, on a field that can be arbitrarily old, converts one historical failed beat into a standing report that the cadence is broken long after it recovered. Nothing on the surface qualifies the age. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Executed GET /api/v1/organism/cadence: last_beat {ran: true, at '2026-10-05T14:45:21Z', refreshed: [strategic, action_plan], could_not_run: null, basis '2 layer(s) refreshed on this beat and 0 could not run…'} under last_beat_basis '`layers` is the plan's own record of when each layer last refreshed; `last_beat` is what the most recent heartbeat managed. A layer that is DUE while last_beat.could_not_run is set means the cadence is not firing…'. GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status read at the same moment: beats 28, last_beat '2026-10-05T15:11:24Z' — 26 minutes and roughly 26 beats later. Code: agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:288 guards the assignment with `if _refreshed or _cad_failed:`, so a beat on which nothing was due leaves the previous record standing; agentic_core/api/organism_status.py:699-723 builds last_beat from heartbeat.last_cadence and publishes the basis sentence. grep over apps/workstation-superapp/src for 'organism/cadence' returns nothing, so API_ONLY is correct and the response body is the reached form. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Set `last_cadence` on EVERY beat that completed the cadence step (including `{"refreshed": [], "could_not_run": None}` for "nothing was due"), or carry the beat counter and timestamp separately so the route can say "the last beat that acted on the cadence was X; the most recent beat was Y".

items.title: The §17.3 Strategic and Action-Plan cadence runs only for the workstation apex — no VSB's layers are ever refreshed
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R3.6), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §17.3: "Strategic (AI CEO; quarterly + market signal)" and "Action Plan (BTO; weekly + KPI-triggered)" are two of the four "continuously-maintained layers (with cadence)" of the Living Business System — and the VSB IDBO enterprise is what the vision says the layers belong to. OBSERVED: The heartbeat's cadence step calls `_cad.refresh("workstation", _layer)` with the scope hard-coded, so only the apex plan is ever refreshed. GET /api/v1/organism/cadence?scope=vsb-9a371566c3 confirms it by execution: both layers return `refresh_count: 0`, `ever_refreshed: false`, `last_refresh_at: null` and `due: true` with trigger "never_refreshed" — permanently due, with nothing that will ever fire them. For the apex the cadence is genuinely delivered: two refreshes on record, honest provenance, and a `due` computation that distinguishes "never" from "just now". EVIDENCE: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:275-285 (`_res = _cad.refresh("workstation", _layer)`); C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1780-1799 (the board pack's per-layer `refresh_basis`); executed GET /api/v1/organism/cadence?scope=vsb-9a371566c3 and POST /api/v1/vsb/vsb-9a371566c3/board-pack. WHY TIER 1: A founder who opens their entity's board pack is told, per layer, exactly this: "no §17.3 strategic refresh exists for this entity's plan, so this layer is whatever the CEO specification is - which is what the basis says" and "no §17.3 action-plan refresh exists for this entity's plan, so this layer is whatever the board roster is", and the strategic layer is marked `holds: "placeholder"`, `present: false`. The shortfall is large — it is every living enterprise the platform generates — but the surface states it in its own words at the point of reading, which the tier rules put at 3 however large it is. It is not tier 2 because nothing is left unsaid, and not tier 1 because no field asserts a refresh that did not happen (`refresh_id` is null, not a fabricated id). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Yes — stated per layer in the board pack and in the cadence response itself. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: The capability gap is reproduced, but I am ESCALATING the tier from 3 to 1 because the assessor's ground for tier 3 is falsified by execution. Their stated reason was that 'no field asserts a refresh that did not happen (refresh_id is null, not a fabricated id)'. It does: within one scoped document for vsb-70c8186f, `layers` says both §17.3 layers have NEVER been refreshed and `history_count` is 0, while `last_beat` says 'ran: true' and names those same two layers — strategic and action_plan — as '2 layer(s) refreshed on this beat', with a basis sentence calling it what the most recent heartbeat managed and no word anywhere that this field belongs to a different scope. A founder reading the surface built to answer 'is my entity's cadence firing?' is told it fired minutes ago on both layers. That is an assertion, not an omission, so not tier 2; and it is not a disclosed shortfall, because the honest statements the assessor relied on live on a different surface (the board pack) while this one contradicts them. The per-layer board-pack disclosure is genuinely exemplary and I verified it — but a disclosure elsewhere does not de-tier a false assertion here. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: The hard-coded scope is real: agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:278 `_res = _cad.refresh("workstation", _layer)`, the only call site. Executed GET /api/v1/organism/cadence?scope=vsb-70c8186f: strategic {last_refresh_at null, refresh_count 0, ever_refreshed false, due true, trigger 'never_refreshed'}, action_plan identical, history_count 0. BUT the same scoped response carries last_beat {"ran": true, "at": "2026-10-05T14:45:21Z", "refreshed": [{"layer": "strategic", …, "served_by": "deterministic-floor"}, {"layer": "action_plan", …}], "could_not_run": null, "basis": "2 layer(s) refreshed on this beat and 0 could not run…"} under last_beat_basis '`last_beat` is what the most recent heartbeat managed' — no scope qualifier anywhere. Source: agentic_core/api/organism_status.py:699-712 reads the process-global heartbeat.last_cadence into a response whose scope, layers and history are all scoped. The board pack's honest counterpart is real and I read it back from POST /api/v1/vsb/vsb-70c8186f/board-pack: strategic holds 'empty', present false, refresh_basis 'no §17.3 strategic refresh exists for this entity's plan…'; action_plan holds 'other' with the roster basis. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Have the beat iterate the living registry (one entity per beat, round-robin, as the §4 economy step already does) so each VSB's two layers refresh on their own clocks; until then, the entity's cockpit should carry the board pack's sentence so a founder does not have to assemble a pack to learn it.

items.title: A user-designed swarm cascade tells the user that the engine's own boilerplate is what their request was about
items.why:
MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R4.0), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: §6: the AI Agent Swarm cascade is "synthesised, modelled and simulated bespoke to each solution's needs" and is "Reconfigurable by users … in Synthesis Lab, Build-to-Order, and Forge"; §15.6 honesty over polish, never fabricate. OBSERVED: `orchestrator.swarm` sets `carry = res["output"]` and prepends it to the next stage as "Prior context:
" + carry[:1200]. The deterministic floor counts n-grams over the WHOLE prompt, so from stage 2 onward the most frequent terms are the floor's own banner ("_[Workstation native structured engine — owned, no external dependency]_") rather than the user's subject. Verified by execution on POST /api/v1/resources/swarm/run with three designed stages and a Birmingham halal-delivery context; also on POST /api/v1/native-ai/swarm. The workflow TREE does not have this defect — `_plan_tree` restates "Overall goal: …" in every node's task, so every tree node's terms were the goal's terms. EVIDENCE: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/ai/native/orchestrator.py:900-906 (prompt = … 'Prior context:
' + carry[:1200] …; carry = res["output"] at :908); C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:205 and :302-304 (the two headings that print the term list). Reached at C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/developers/NativeAI.tsx:72 (`Trace` renders `s.output` whole, for Quick swarm and for every saved-cascade Run) and in the Resource-Fabric composition trace. WHY TIER 1: The reader is shown, as stage 2 and stage 3 of a cascade they designed: "## Terms most frequent in your request … The list below is the request's most frequent terms, not findings about them. - external dependency - structured engine - owned external - engine owned - workstation" — for a request whose context I typed as "Launch a halal food delivery business in Birmingham serving 50 restaurants". Stage 1 got it right (halal food · business birmingham · serving restaurants). That is not an omission and not an environment fact: it is a positive sentence about the user's own input that is false, on the surface that renders it verbatim. It is above tier 2 because the shortfall is not merely undisclosed — the surface makes an affirmative, wrong claim about the reader's words. It is not below tier 1 on the argument that the terms are true of the stage's internal prompt, because nothing a reader can see distinguishes 'the request' from the engine's prior-context block, and the user's subject has silently vanished from the cascade by stage 2. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. Nothing on the stage card, and nothing in the response, says that stages after the first count the engine's own text instead of the request. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: Tier 1 upheld. The reader is shown an affirmative sentence about their own words — 'the request's most frequent terms' / 'Structured frame over the terms most frequent in the request' — immediately under a 'Subject:' line quoting the instruction they typed, and the list is the engine's own banner ('external dependency', 'structured engine', 'owned external', 'workstation'). That is not an omission and not the AI_DISABLE_LOCAL environment: the floor is entitled to say it counted terms, it is not entitled to say whose terms. It is above tier 2 because the surface makes a positive false claim rather than failing to disclose one; it is not below tier 1 on the defence that the terms are true of the internal prompt, because nothing a reader can see separates 'the request' from the prior-context block, and their subject has silently left the cascade by stage 2. I verified the reach myself rather than taking it on the code citation, and I found the same class in the tree's final output, which the finding wrongly excluded. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/native-ai/swarm with three stages (researcher/strategist/planner) on a Birmingham halal-delivery subject: stage 1 terms were the subject's (serving restaurants · birmingham serving · market birmingham · delivery market · food delivery); stage 2 and stage 3 printed 'Subject: Design the go-to-market strategy for that halal delivery business' and then 'Structured frame over the terms most frequent in the request (a term count, not an analysis): - external dependency - structured engine - owned external - engine owned - workstation'. Code confirmed: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/ai/native/orchestrator.py:900-908 (carry = res['output']; prompt prepends 'Prior context:
' + carry[:1200]) and C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:205, :302-304 (the two headings that print the term list). Reach verified in source: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/developers/NativeAI.tsx:70 renders s.output per stage (line-clamp-4) and :201 renders run.final (line-clamp-6) — I counted the rendered lines of a real run and the false sentence plus its first boilerplate bullet fall inside the six-line clamp, so a user does see it. ONE CLAIM OF THIS FINDING IS WRONG AND THE DEFECT IS WIDER THAN REPORTED: the assessor exempted the workflow tree, but POST /api/v1/native-ai/tree on 'Establish a solar microgrid cooperative' returned final = 'Subject: ## Terms most frequent in your request (domain: the stated domain). (domain: the stated domain).' — the tree's synthesis takes the engine's own HEADING as the user's subject. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): In `orchestrator.swarm`, pass the ORIGINAL context (and the stage instruction) as the term-bearing subject and carry the prior output under a separately-labelled block the floor excludes from its n-gram count — the tree already does this by restating the goal in every node; or, failing that, strip the floor banner from `carry` before it becomes the next prompt and label the list "terms most frequent in this stage's input".

items.title: The Qur'an Education Platform's roadmap advertises an emotion-adaptive interface, which the vision ratifies as REFUSED
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R5.0), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict PARTIAL at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: A.9.4: "Emotion inference is not adopted ... QEP's adaptive UI adapts to profile and stated preference (the W428 explicit profile), never to inferred affect. Reopening this needs an Owner ruling with a consent model attached." A.6 feature 12's status names the W428 explicit profile as "the right substrate". OBSERVED: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:33 declares `{ id: 'adaptive_ui', name: 'Adaptive UI', ... desc: 'Interface adjusts to age and emotion.' }`. The grid is reached at /religion -> "QEP Flagship" tab -> the "Roadmap - modules not yet built (honestly labelled)" section (ReligionHub.tsx:115-128), and each card renders a 7px "planned" badge plus that description verbatim (lines 69-72). A repo-wide grep for "emotion" across apps/workstation-superapp/src returns this card and nothing else except AdaptiveUIProvider.tsx:13/48, where `emotionalAdjustment` is derived purely from the stored `ui.tone` preference, and six domain hubs that render it as "{tone} TONE (saved pref.)" with the tooltip "a saved preference - no request from this hub carries it yet". So the live mechanism is correctly preference-based; only the QEP roadmap card promises inference. EVIDENCE: QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:33 (the literal), ReligionHub.tsx:115-128 (reach), QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:69-72 (render), AdaptiveUIProvider.tsx:48 `emotionalAdjustment: ui.tone === 'neutral' ? 'Neutral' : 'Encouraging'` (the real, compliant mechanism), ScienceHub.tsx:31 (the honest "saved pref." badge). WHY TIER 1: The reader is shown a card titled "Adaptive UI" whose whole description is the sentence "Interface adjusts to age and emotion.", under a section heading that vouches for its own honesty ("Roadmap - modules not yet built (honestly labelled)"). That is an affirmative statement about what the platform intends to do, and it is untrue: A.9.4 records emotion inference as NOT ADOPTED, re-openable only by an Owner ruling with a consent model attached, for a population that includes minors. Not tier 2, because nothing here is a hidden shortfall - the card does not understate a capability, it announces one the constitution forbids. Not tier 3, because the "planned" badge discloses that the feature is absent, which is the opposite of the problem: it endorses it as coming. This is also the one item in the appendix where a surface promising the capability is worse than a surface lacking it. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No - the opposite. The card is presented inside a section whose heading asserts the labels are honest, so a reader has no cue that this particular line describes something the platform has ruled out. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: Reproduced in full, and the detail panel makes it worse than the assessor said. QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:33 carries the literal `desc: 'Interface adjusts to age and emotion.'`; it is reached at /religion -> QEP Flagship tab, rendered by ReligionHub.tsx:120-126 under the heading 'Roadmap - modules not yet built (honestly labelled)', with a 7px 'planned' badge (QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:69-72). I additionally read launchFeature (lines 46-51) and the expanded panel (lines 96-112): clicking the card opens 'Adaptive UI Module / Not yet built - nothing was run' over the sentence 'This module is described in the platform plan but has no backend yet' - so the surface does not merely describe emotion inference, it asserts it is IN THE PLAN. The vision's A.9.4 (line 1325) states the opposite in terms: 'Not adopted ... Reopening this needs an Owner ruling with a consent model attached', and line 1131 repeats 'add emotional state - not adopted'. I confirmed the live mechanism is compliant: AdaptiveUIProvider.tsx:48 derives emotionalAdjustment purely from the stored ui.tone preference, fontScale is a real rendered effect, and six hubs label it '{tone} TONE (saved pref.)' with the tooltip 'no request from this hub carries it yet' - which is why the verdict is PARTIAL (the A.9.4-compliant adaptive UI IS live) and not MISSING. Tier 1 and not tier 2: nothing here understates a capability, so there is no hidden shortfall - the card and its panel make an affirmative, untrue statement about what the platform intends, for a population that includes minors. Tier 1 and not tier 3: the 'planned' badge discloses only that the feature is absent, which endorses it as coming rather than correcting it; a disclosure that the thing is on its way is not a disclosure that it has been refused. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:33 (literal), :46-51 (launchFeature sets 'not yet built'), :69-72 (planned badge + desc render), :96-112 ('described in the platform plan'); apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/ReligionHub.tsx:120-126 (reach); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/AdaptiveUIProvider.tsx:44-58 (preference-only mechanism); docs/WORKSTATION_IDBO_WHOLE_VISION.md:1325 (A.9.4), :1131; repo grep for 'emotion' in apps/workstation-superapp/src returns only this card, the provider, and the six 'saved pref.' badges. THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Change that one `desc` string to the A.9.4 posture, e.g. "Adapts to your stated profile and preferences (text size, guided mode, tone) - never to inferred emotion, which is not adopted." items.title: The QEP flagship's two unbuilt tabs answer a click with a release name and a hardware requirement that nothing in the system backs
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v7 (R5.2), measured 2026-10-05 against HEAD 6e63e762 on the native floor (AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1), standing verdict STUB at TIER 1 after independent refutation. THE VISION CLAIM: A.6 feature 9 status: "rendered as **planned**, and the buttons say so on click. Honest, and a placeholder." A.6 feature 4 status: "Competitions, leaderboards and badges do not exist." Principle 6: honesty over polish; never fabricate. OBSERVED: C:/Users/rehan/Workstation/apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/QEPReligionHub.tsx:234 (`toast('Global leaderboard launching with QEP Season 2')` on the "View Leaderboard" button of all three tournament cards), and :218/:219 (`toast('AR Mouth Model requires a WebXR-compatible device - coming in Phase 4')`, `toast('VR Mosque requires a WebXR headset - coming in Phase 4')`). Both tabs are top-level tabs of the flagship (lines 20-25: "Competitions" and "AR/VR Lab"), equal in prominence to "Memorization", which is the one that works. The surrounding prose is honest - "Immersive Lab - planned (Phase 4)", "no WebXR code exists yet, so nothing here claims readiness", three cards badged PLANNED with "0 Participants" - so the toasts are the only untrue text on the two tabs. EVIDENCE: QEPReligionHub.tsx:234, :218, :219 (the three toast literals); QEPReligionHub.tsx:20-25 (the two tabs); docs/FABLE_DELIVERY_PROMPT.md:723 "P4 is the Owner's hand" and :815 "P4 0/6" - a case-insensitive grep of that file for webxr|AR/VR|immersive|arvr|Season 2 returns nothing. WHY TIER 1: Three specific sentences are shown to a reader on click. "Global leaderboard launching with QEP Season 2" names a release; grep finds "Season 2" nowhere in agentic_core, nowhere in the frontend outside this one toast, and nowhere in the delivery plan. "AR Mouth Model requires a WebXR-compatible device - coming in Phase 4" and "VR Mosque requires a WebXR headset - coming in Phase 4" attribute the unavailability to the reader's hardware - so a user who IS on a WebXR headset is told something plainly false about why nothing happened - and name a phase that does not contain this work (the plan's own line is "P4 is the Owner's hand", the Owner-switch phase; grep for webxr/AR-VR in docs/FABLE_DELIVERY_PROMPT.md returns zero). Not tier 2: the absence of the capability IS disclosed (PLANNED badges, 0 participants, and prose saying "no WebXR code exists yet"), so what remains is not a hidden shortfall but three positive claims that are untrue. Not tier 3 for the same reason - the untrue parts are asserted, not omitted. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly. The absence is disclosed on the cards and in the prose; the release name and the device-is-the-blocker framing are not qualified anywhere. THE REFUTER, who was told to default to refuted and had to reproduce the gap: All three toast literals reproduced at QEPReligionHub.tsx:220, :221, :234, on two of the flagship's five top-level tabs (lines 19-25: 'Competitions', 'AR/VR Lab'). A case-insensitive repo grep for 'Season 2' returns only this toast and an _archive/ copy - nothing in agentic_core, nothing in the delivery plan; a grep for 'webxr' returns this component, the excluded long-form docs/QURAN_EDUCATION_PLATFORM_VISION.md (whose technology and roadmap parts A.10 bars from being read as a vision claim), and two _archive/ files. docs/FABLE_DELIVERY_PROMPT.md:723 reads 'P4 is the Owner's hand' and contains no WebXR/AR-VR work, so 'coming in Phase 4' names a phase that does not hold it. Tier 1 and not tier 2: the ABSENCE is disclosed well - the card prose says 'no WebXR code exists yet, so nothing here claims readiness' (line 215) and the tournament cards badge PLANNED - so what is left is not a hidden shortfall but three positive claims that are untrue. The strongest leg is 'Global leaderboard launching with QEP Season 2': it is an invented release commitment with no counter-statement anywhere on the Competitions tab. The AR/VR pair adds a false CAUSE - a reader on a WebXR headset is told their device is the blocker. Tier 1 and not tier 3: the untrue parts are asserted on click, not omitted, and a tier-3 reading would require the surface to state them as unbacked, which nothing does. THE REFUTER'S OWN EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/QEPReligionHub.tsx:234, :220, :221 (toasts), :19-25 (tabs), :205-222 (the honest ARVRLab prose), :226-236 (PLANNED cards); docs/FABLE_DELIVERY_PROMPT.md:723; repo-wide 'Season 2'/'webxr' greps (only this file, _archive/, and the A.10-excluded long-form QEP doc). THE SMALLEST HONEST FIX the assessor proposed (a proposal, not a decision): Replace the three toast strings with what is true: "No tournament or leaderboard backend exists - this is a preview" and "No WebXR code exists yet; this is not blocked by your device." Drop the phase reference, which the plan does not carry.
