items.title: Change Control terminally rejects a HIGH change on an 'organism health' figure that counts §11 lexicon flags over the platform's own floor text as compliance regressions — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5 (Recorded W464): a HIGH change approved by a review waits for Board ratification; Change Control governs change at arm's length; §15.6 never fabricate, label simulation; §11 'a screen may flag and escalate but never clear' (W483). OBSERVED: At 10:36 board/status reported organism_health 1.0. One org cascade (22 floor calls, §11 screen escalations ['ethical:human']) plus one VSB spawn (website/webapp/mobile/repo screens) drove /api/v1/organism/systems to {health 0.1, by_type: {compliance_escalation: 5}} and health-summary to mode EMERGENCY. cca-63f6f1590b (code_change, HIGH) submitted at 10:39:52 recorded health_gate.verdict 'fail' and immune_threat 'CRITICAL'; its review at 10:40:44 returned decision 'rejected', decision_source 'health_threshold_rule'. After the 5-minute window expired (health back to 1.0) an identical-tier change cca-1334f3af84 was rule-APPROVED and reached the Board queue — the verdict depended on nothing about either change. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:486-492 (`if _comp.get('overall') == 'fail' or _escalated: immune.record(f'compliance:{label}', … 'compliance_escalation')`); agentic_core/organism/immune.py:67 (`health = max(0.0, 1.0 - total/10.0)`), :69-76 threat tiers; agentic_core/compliance/ethical_engine.py:47-48 (_HARM_SEVERE regex), :92-97 (escalate=True on a match); UEG compliance.screen node for label 'cascade' with escalations ['ethical:human']; agentic_core/api/change_control.py:1445-1470 (review: no marker → health rule; 'rejection is terminal'); agentic_core/api/board.py:111-112 (_ORGANISM_HEALTH_SCOPE string); live records: GET /api/v1/cca/cca-63f6f1590b, GET /api/v1/organism/health-summary ("Organism critical — measured health 10%"), GET /api/v1/organism/systems; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/ChangeControlAgency.tsx:102,305-310,366-370. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the record says the rule decided it and names the 0.10 figure; nothing on the change record, the Board status basis or the organism summary says the figure is a count of lexicon flags on floor-composed text rather than failures or regressions.. WHY THIS TIER: The record a submitter is shown (ChangeControlAgency.tsx renders review_result verbatim and 'decided by: organism-health threshold rule (not the model)') says: "MEASURED composite_health 0.10 < 0.5 → rejected", and the Board/organism surfaces describe that figure as "the immune system's health: AI-call failures and compliance regressions only" and "Organism critical — measured health 10%. Emergency mode." What the figure actually counted in this session was five `compliance_escalation` immune events — the ethical lexicon matching a severe-harm verb (e.g. 'abuse') inside text the deterministic floor composed for the cascade and the entity's generated public faces. W483 defines an escalation as a flag for a human that 'never convicts'; recording it as an immune error at 10% of health each means ten flags in five minutes put the organism in EMERGENCY and every HIGH review is rule-REJECTED, which change_control.py says is terminal. The submitter is therefore told their change was rejected because the organism's health regressed, when no regression was found and nothing read the change. A reader could argue tier 2 (the mechanism is named on the record), but the record asserts a measured health that misdescribes what it measured and the rejection is a terminal governance outcome asserted on it — that lands on tier 1. The twin pre-validation on the same record reads 'fail' from the same figure. REFUTER: Reproduced the mechanism in an isolated process and confirmed the live records. One evidence correction: BoardOfDirectors.tsx only TYPES live.organism_health (line 30) and never renders it or the 'compliance regressions' basis, so that sentence is response-body only; the reached surfaces are the Change Control record ('MEASURED composite_health 0.10 < 0.5 → rejected', 'decided by: organism-health threshold rule'), OrganismDashboard ('10%', 'CRITICAL', 'N errors') and OrganismAnatomy ('Organism critical — measured health 10%'). Tier 1 rather than 2 because those are assertions, not silences: 'N errors' and 'measured health 10%' report failures that did not occur — every event in the window was a word-list flag the ethical engine itself labels 'not an assessment … escalated for a human', recorded by quality.py as an immune error at 10% of health each — and a HIGH change was terminally rejected on that figure while an identical-tier change was approved 12 minutes later on nothing about either change. Not the environment: the floor did not cause this; W483's routing of an escalation into immune.record did. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Stop recording an escalation (a flag) as an immune error — record it to the UEG and route to a human as W483 intended, and record only `overall == 'fail'`; or at minimum exclude floor-served screens. Make review_result name what the measured health counted (immune.by_type) so a rule rejection carries its own basis.

items.title: From the second stage on, every native cascade lists the platform's own banner words as "the request's most frequent terms", and the user's context arrives glued to a literal backslash-n — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R4)
items.why:
MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6: bespoke, reconfigurable agent-cascade trees where "each stage completes in-house-first and feeds the next"; §15.6 "never fabricate". OBSERVED: orchestrator.swarm() builds the next stage's prompt with an f-string whose braces contain the literal `'Prior context:\n'` (a backslash and an n, not a newline), so the carried stage-1 output — whose first line is the provenance marker — shares a line with the label. The engine's `_CARRIED_MARKER_RE` is line-anchored (`^…$`), so the marker survives stripping and its words become stage 2's "request terms". The same literal glues `\n\nTask:` and the user's own context onto the next word. Every caller of orchestrator.swarm is affected: /api/v1/native-ai/swarm (Primitive Console quick swarm), /api/v1/resources/swarm/run (saved cascades, including every VSB's registered delivery swarm), the composition run ("composition-run") and the fabric's native_swarm resource. The run is UEG-logged, so the durable record carries it too. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/ai/native/orchestrator.py:898 — `f"{('Prior context:\n' + carry[:1200] + '\n\n') if carry else ''}"`; agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:55-62 `_CARRIED_MARKER_RE = re.compile(r"^[ 	]*" + re.escape(_MARKER) + r"[ 	]*$", re.M)`. Local reproduction at HEAD with AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1 through orchestrator.swarm: the stage-2 prompt repr is `'Prior context:\n_[Workstation native structured engine — owned…'` and the stage-2 bullets are ['- external dependency', '- structured engine', '- owned external', '- engine owned', '- workstation', '- product']. items.title: The workflow tree's final synthesis names an upstream node's instruction as the request's subject and counts the floor's own "request named" phrase as a request term — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R4)
items.why:
MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6: autonomous workflow/pipeline/cascade trees that decompose a goal and synthesise the branches; §15.6 honesty over polish. OBSERVED: orchestrate_tree feeds each node's upstream outputs under "Inputs from upstream nodes:" and the final node's task is to synthesise them. With the floor serving, the engine's `_subject` falls through to the first carried sentence (the research node's instruction), and the floor's "(domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain)" accumulates once per hop (three copies in the synthesis subject line) and is then counted as a request term. The tree's meta blocks are honest (planner "deterministic_template"; qms/validation/decision/consensus all "not assessable — every node floor-served"), but the node text is not. business_plan.py also consumes orchestrate_tree for the founder's plan (code-read, not driven). EVIDENCE: Live POST http://127.0.0.1:8031/api/v1/native-ai/tree {"goal":"Launch a halal student micro-lending service","max_parallel":3,"timeout":20} → node `synthesise` (chief synthesiser, served_by native) output head: "## Understanding
Subject: Gather the key facts, prior art, and constraints relevant to the goal. (domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain).). (domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain).).).
Structured frame over the terms most frequent in the request (a term count, not an analysis):
- constraints relevant
- request named
- key facts"; the same response's `final` is that node's output. Meta in the same body: planner "deterministic_template", governance.qms_basis "not assessable — every node floor-served", validation.integrated null, decision.recommendation null, consensus.reached false. Code: agentic_core/ai/native/orchestrator.py:597-610 (dep_ctx / "Inputs from upstream nodes:" block), agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py `_subject` (line 165) and the WITHHELD literal at engine.py generate(); consumer agentic_core/api/business_plan.py:517 `tree = await orchestrator.orchestrate_tree(goal, context=context)`. Surface: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/developers/NativeAI.tsx:136 (n.output, line-clamp-3) and :210 (run.final, line-clamp-6). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the meta blocks say every node was floor-served and nothing is assessable; the node text itself is not qualified and states the wrong subject.. WHY THIS TIER: The synthesiser's output tells the reader "Subject: Gather the key facts, prior art, and constraints relevant to the goal." for a goal that was "Launch a halal student micro-lending service", and lists "request named" — a fragment of the floor's own WITHHELD-domain sentence — among the request's most frequent terms. Those are assertions about the user's request that are untrue, on the surface a person reaches (the tree's `final` is rendered on the Primitive Console), so tier 1 rather than tier 3; the tree's meta-level honesty ("every node floor-served") does not correct the node text a reader actually reads. REFUTER: Reproduced live. The synthesise node's Understanding line states 'Subject: Gather the key facts, prior art, and constraints relevant to the goal.' for the goal 'Launch a halal student micro-lending service' — the research node's instruction, not the goal — followed by three accumulated '(domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain)' copies, and 'request named' (a fragment of the floor's own sentence) is listed among the request's most frequent terms; the review node accumulates four copies. The tree's `final` is that node's output and is rendered at NativeAI.tsx:210; each node's output at :136. The meta blocks (planner deterministic_template; qms/validation/decision/consensus all 'not assessable — every node floor-served') are honest, but they qualify the verdicts, not the node text a reader reads. A false subject and a counted fragment of the platform's own prose are assertions on a reached surface → tier 1, not 3. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Treat the floor's own WITHHELD-domain sentence as carried framing in `_strip_carried` (so it is neither re-quoted nor counted), and have `_subject` prefer the labelled "Overall goal:" field over any sentence inside a carried block; add a test that runs orchestrate_tree under AI_DISABLE_LOCAL=1 and asserts the synthesis subject equals the goal and that "request named" is not a listed term.

items.title: A founder is told "Genome Encoded — DNA stored in the epigenetic registry" while the organism's Genome layer, its lab and the heartbeat report zero genomes for five living VSBs — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.2 layer 1: "Genome — VSB identity/capabilities/constraints/evolution (arms-length controlled)"; §7 lists genome among the organism systems a user composes. OBSERVED: VSB establishment and spawn write `genome_spec`/`epigenetic_traits` through `GenomicRegistry` (agentic_core/genetic_immune), while /api/v1/organism/genome, the Anatomy Genome lab and heartbeat `last_genome` read `organism/genome.py`'s trait-vector store. The vision's own realisation map concedes "the two are not yet one arms-length-controlled identity", but no user surface says so. EVIDENCE: GET http://127.0.0.1:8031/api/v1/organism/genome → {"total": 0, "population": {"mean_fitness_basis": "no genomes stored yet"}}; GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status → last_genome.total 0; GET /api/v1/vsb → total 5; GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-ecc17d7f72 → keys include genome_spec, epigenetic_traits, generation. agentic_core/api/genesis.py:1579 `yield _event("genome", "Genome Encoded", "DNA stored in the epigenetic registry (layer 1).")`; agentic_core/api/vsb.py:42-47 `from agentic_core.genetic_immune.genomic_registry import GenomicRegistry … _genome_registry = GenomicRegistry()`; agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2495 "Genome Encoded" event; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/organism/OrganismAnatomy.tsx:86 reads /api/v1/organism/genome and :398 renders "no genomes yet — encode one above". docs/WORKSTATION_IDBO_WHOLE_VISION.md §17.2 realisation map: "the two are not yet one arms-length-controlled identity (P2.7/P3)". DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. Neither the establishment event nor the Genome lab/heartbeat states that VSB genomes live in a different registry.. WHY THIS TIER: Nothing shown is false in isolation — the VSB's genome IS written to the GenomicRegistry, and the organism store IS empty — but the two surfaces describe one layer and neither says there are two stores. The Anatomy tab's "no genomes yet — encode one above" and the heartbeat's "no genomes stored yet" are read against five establishment streams that said the DNA was stored in layer 1. The shortfall (two un-unified genome identities) is invisible at every surface, so tier 2, not tier 3; it is not tier 1 because no figure is fabricated. REFUTER: The assessor's facts hold (two genome stores; Anatomy and heartbeat read organism/genome's trait-vector files and show 0 while VSBs carry genome_spec) but the tier is too kind, and the count is stale (7 living VSBs, not 5). On the Genesis establishment path the only registry call is `store_epigenetic_pattern(layer=1)`, which assigns into `self.epigenetic_layers['layer_1']` — a process-memory dict. `_save` persists only `self.blocks` and `_load` restores only blocks; no file in agentic_core outside the registry reads `epigenetic_layers`; the VSB genome route (vsb.py:2205) reads the entity record, not the registry. So the four Genesis-born live entities are absent from meta/genome_ledger.json, while the three spawn-born ones are present because vsb.py:2491 also calls commit_mutation. The founder is shown 'Genome Encoded — DNA stored in the epigenetic registry (layer 1)' (GenesisJourney.tsx:1054/1128 render s.content), a registry whose own docstring says 'Persistent trait memory … Long-term (30-90 days)'. That sentence certifies a storage outcome the platform did not produce — the DNA lives on the entity file, not in any registry that persists or that any surface reads — so it is an untrue assertion on a reached surface, tier 1, not an undisclosed omission (tier 2). The spawn path's 'encoded in epigenetic registry' IS backed by a committed block, so the escalation is specific to Genesis. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Have /organism/genome (and the lab's empty-state line) report the GenomicRegistry count beside its own — e.g. "0 trait-vector genomes in this store; 5 entity genomes recorded in the genomic registry (a separate identity, not yet unified)" — and make the establishment event name the registry it wrote to; a guard asserts the organism genome surface mentions the registry count whenever VSBs exist.

VISION CLAIM: §8/§17.2 cardiovascular: dynamic resource allocation governed by the organism's state; §15.6 honesty. items.title: Every floor-served domain tool and the avatar tell the reader their request "named no domain", on a page that IS the domain — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R5)
items.why:
MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §3A offering 1: domain-specific AI-mediated tools, the user works WITH AI mediation INSIDE their domain; Principle 6 honesty over polish (never fabricate; label simulation). OBSERVED: Executed law/analyse, care/care-plan, care/risk-assess, care/safeguarding, religion/quran-tafsir, religion/fatwa-research, employment/cv, employment/career-path, employment/application, education/lesson-plan, education/feedback and avatar/chat: all carry "domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain" in the body text. Only Science (whose request models have a `domain` field) prints a domain ("domain: botany", "domain: medicine"). Cause: agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:292 `domain = _field(prompt, "Domain") or "WITHHELD — the request named no domain"` (W631/FU-556 replaced a placeholder with WITHHELD), and none of the five routers' prompts (agentic_core/api/law.py, care.py, religion.py, employment.py, education.py) nor the avatar's grounding writes a `Domain:` label, although each knows its domain. Role truncation: engine.py:147 `_role` caps the persona at 60 chars and takes the first "You are/As a" match, so the Care prompt "You are a clinical risk assessment specialist supporting a qualified clinician" prints as "...supporting a qualified cl." and Education's "You are an experienced ..." prints as "Acting as: experienced.". DomainTool.tsx renders the body verbatim in a

EVIDENCE: curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8031/api/v1/law/analyse -d '{"document_text":"The tenant shall pay rent..."}' → analysis contains "Subject: (domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain)" x5 and "Iterate via the orchestrator's cascade for WITHHELD — the request named no domain". care/risk-assess → "_Acting as: clinical risk assessment specialist supporting a qualified cl._". education/feedback → "_Acting as: experienced._". avatar/chat context=vsb → "_Acting as: VSB._". agentic_core/ai/native/engine.py:292 and :145-148. apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/DomainTool.tsx lines 283-285 (
{displayText}
) and withDisclosures (lines 83-91). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The floor_note correctly says no analysis was performed, but nothing says the domain IS known and simply was not labelled; the false sentence stands uncorrected on screen and in every export.. WHY THIS TIER: The sentence shown to a reader (and copied, downloaded and saved into My Work) is: "(domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain)" repeated under every heading, plus "Iterate via the orchestrator's cascade for WITHHELD — the request named no domain" and "Each phase grounded in WITHHELD — the request named no domain". A user who posted to /api/v1/law/analyse from the Law hub, or to /care/care-plan from the Care hub, DID name a domain; the statement is untrue as the reader understands it, and reads as if they omitted a field. It lands on tier 1 rather than 2 because it is an assertion, not a silent gap; it sits at the bottom of tier 1 because it misleads about a label, not an outcome — the floor_note beside it correctly says no analysis happened. The same floor also prints truncated persona lines a reader cannot parse: "_Acting as: experienced._" (Education marking), "_Acting as: VSB._" (avatar in vsb context), "...supporting a qualified cl._" (Care risk). One narrowing: when the avatar is called with a vsb_id the grounding block supplies '(domain: enterprise, stage: None)', so the avatar leg holds only for ungrounded replies (which is what the ConversationPanel sends unless a VSB is chosen). items.title: The six domain tools drop the gateway's profile verdict, so a user whose saved profile was ignored by the floor is never told — MILESTONE M2 ledger v13 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v13 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §9: "dynamically and intelligently personalised to each user's instructions, requests, history, preferences, needs and abilities" — the W428 explicit user profile; Principle 6 label simulation. OBSERVED: PUT /api/v1/user/profile with a KS1-teacher profile, then POST /api/v1/education/feedback: the response keys are [feedback_id, subject, level, tone, feedback, ai_provenance, generated_at, disclaimer] and ai_provenance holds posture/served_by/is_external/language_*/floor_note/quality_assurance only — no profile_applied, profile_state or profile_basis. agentic_core/ai/gateway.py:427-432 computes `profile_applied: bool(_preamble) and not self._is_floor(served_by)` and `profile_state: "not_usable_by_floor"` with a basis sentence, but agentic_core/api/_ai_provenance.py:108-116 builds the provenance dict from a fixed key set and never copies the three profile keys (the file does not contain the word profile outside a W619 comment). DomainTool.tsx has no profile rendering; ConversationPanel.tsx lines 142-146 render `profile-not-usable` for the avatar only. EVIDENCE: PUT then POST shown above; agentic_core/api/_ai_provenance.py:108-116 (provenance = {posture, served_by, is_external, language_requested, language_delivered, language_basis}); agentic_core/ai/gateway.py:427-432; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/Settings.tsx:239 ("Used to shape what the platform generates for you"); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/avatar/ConversationPanel.tsx:142-146. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. Settings asserts the profile shapes generation; the domain tool output shows neither an applied nor a not-applied statement. Only the avatar discloses it.. WHY THIS TIER: Settings tells the user the profile is "Used to shape what the platform generates for you" and GET /user/profile says `applied_to: generation prompts on this platform`. On the floor the profile does NOT shape any domain-tool output (the gateway itself reports `profile_state: not_usable_by_floor`), and the domain tool's response and page carry no profile field at all — the shortfall is real and the surface does not say so. It is tier 2 rather than 1 because nothing on the tool page ASSERTS the profile was applied (an omission, not an assertion), and rather than 3 because the avatar discloses exactly this per reply ("profile: not usable by the floor") while the 24 domain tools stay silent, so a reader who read Settings is left believing their profile shaped a tailored CV or care plan. REFUTER: Reproduced with a real profile (the assessor's claim is confirmed only after writing the correct schema fields; a first PUT with wrong field names produced an empty preamble, so I redid it). With a 307-character preamble the domain-tool response carries no profile_applied/profile_state/profile_basis while the avatar, served by the same gateway, returns profile_state 'not_usable_by_floor'. Tier 2 not 1: nothing on the tool page asserts the profile was applied — the omission is on the tool surface, and Settings' 'Used to shape what the platform generates for you' is a general description of what the preamble does (it does reach the prompt), not a per-output claim. Tier 2 not 3 because the shortfall is not stated anywhere a tool user looks, while the avatar states it per reply. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In _ai_provenance.ai_text copy `profile_applied`, `profile_state` and `profile_basis` from the gateway result into the provenance dict (three lines), and in DomainTool.tsx render the same amber line the avatar already renders when `profile_state === 'not_usable_by_floor'`; add a guard that writes a profile, calls one domain tool, and asserts the response carries profile_state.

items.title: The immune system counts a compliance 'review' flag as an error, reports the organism under sustained threat, and the heartbeat self-quarantines on it — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: the organism 'defends itself' — homeostasis loops immune↔nervous↔metabolic; the immune layer monitors live compliance and errors. §15.6: honesty over polish, never fabricate. OBSERVED: At 10:39:55Z the heartbeat's respond_to_threat read threat CRITICAL and engaged immune_quarantine through CCA cca-9d322a4881 (impact MEDIUM, auto_approved_immune_defence, implemented the same second; stood down 10:44:58Z when the window purged). The events behind it: UEG compliance.screen rows at 1791542355–1791542367 (vsb_website/vsb_webapp/vsb_mobile/vsb_repo, two ships) plus 1791542274 (genesis) — all overall='review', escalations=['ethical:human'], zero 'fail'. immune.status computes health = 1 − total/10 with no weighting by error_type, so ten review flags in five minutes read as health 0.0 / CRITICAL. /organism/status at 10:44 still showed health 0.5 ELEVATED with hot_endpoint_tied all 'compliance:*'; POST /organism/homeostasis answered organism_mode EMERGENCY; /plan/state answered organism_health 0.0, threat CRITICAL. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:489-493 (immune.record(f'compliance:{label}', 'compliance_escalation') when _escalated); agentic_core/organism/immune.py:66-77 (health from raw count, threat ladder) and :100-105 (playbook text 'owner review — the organism is under sustained threat'); agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:988-1037 (engage at ≥HIGH); GET /api/v1/cca/cca-9d322a4881 (full audit trail quoted above); GET /api/v1/gaas/ueg/events (64 compliance.screen events, listed); apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/organism/OrganismAnatomy.tsx:304-311 renders health%, threat chip, 'errors in window' and the playbook lines verbatim. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The immune card prints '{n} errors in window' and the playbook sentence; neither says the events are review flags awaiting a human rather than failures. The CCA record's description says 'quarantine failing endpoints' — no endpoint had failed.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader of the Anatomy page's immune card and of /api/v1/plan/state was shown 'organism_health 0.0', 'threat CRITICAL', 'N errors in window' and the playbook line 'owner review — the organism is under sustained threat', and the heartbeat then filed and auto-implemented 'Critical threat — quarantine failing endpoints'. None of that was true: every event in the window was a §11 lexicon ESCALATION (verdict 'review', flag 'ethical:human') on routine shipped faces, which quality.py itself describes as 'a flag for a human, not a finding of harm'. A surface asserting an outcome (an error, a threat) the platform did not observe is a truth defect, not an omission (tier 2) or a disclosed gap (tier 3). REFUTER: Reproduced from stored records and code, not from the assessor's text. UEG holds 75 compliance.screen events this run and ZERO carry overall='fail'; 13 carry escalations ['ethical:human'] (vsb_website/webapp/mobile/repo x3 each, genesis, cascade, deliverable). quality.py:487-493 records every escalation with immune.record(..., 'compliance_escalation'); immune.py:66-77 computes health = 1 - total/10 with no weighting by error_type and ladders CRITICAL below 0.2. CCA cca-9d322a4881 (fetched) was submitted by organism.heartbeat at 10:39:55Z with description 'Critical threat — quarantine failing endpoints', auto-approved and implemented the same second, reverted 10:44:58Z. OrganismAnatomy.tsx:304-311 renders health%, the threat chip, '{n} errors in window' and the playbook lines; by_type (which would show 'compliance_escalation') is rendered nowhere in the frontend. /plan/state's basis says 'compliance regressions only' — an escalation is not a regression either. Tier 1 rather than 2: the card and the CCA record ASSERT outcomes ('errors', 'failing endpoints', 'under sustained threat') the platform never observed; nothing on any reached surface says the events were human-review flags on routine shipped faces. Not tier 3 because no surface discloses it. (Now purged: immune reads NOMINAL/1.0 at 10:54Z, so the defect is windowed, not permanent — it recurs on every batch of shipped faces.) SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In immune.status(), weight by error_type: count ai_failure/timeout/http_5xx toward health and report compliance_escalation separately as 'review flags' (never toward the threat ladder), and have respond_to_threat refuse to engage on a threat composed only of escalations; the Anatomy card then prints 'errors' and 'review flags' as two numbers.

items.title: The §17.5 KPI release gate is satisfied by the platform's own placeholder '(KPI to be set by the Board)' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v13 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v13 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.5 invariant 10: KPI gate before customer delivery; R5 ruling: release blocks on unmeasurable objectives and the platform must not invent KPIs. OBSERVED: board.py's chief/instruct fallback (the path taken whenever the floor serves, i.e. this whole environment) writes an objective line '<instruction> | (KPI to be set by the Board) | | AI CEO' into the scoped living plan; ChiefInstruction.scope may be any vsb_id. kpi_release_gate tests `str(kpi).strip()` non-empty. Live: the 'workstation' plan holds one objective with kpi '(KPI to be set by the Board)' (source chief_instruct_fallback, 10:37:39Z) and kpi_release_gate('workstation') returns ok:true, reason 'kpi_set', detail 'all 1 objective(s) carry a KPI'. The two living VSBs are still blocked only because their three seeded objectives carry ''. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/board.py:686 (scope: str = 'workstation' … e.g. a vsb_id), :791-796 (the fallback line with the placeholder); agentic_core/api/business_plan.py:211-213 and :228-229 (presence test); GET /api/v1/business-plan?vsb_id=workstation (objective obj-cd98c9e9, kpi '(KPI to be set by the Board)'); python read of the live store C:/tmp/m1_audit/data via kpi_release_gate('workstation') → {ok: true, reason: 'kpi_set'}; agentic_core/api/marketplace.py:381-386 and :464-469 (the gate's only consumers). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the gate reports 'kpi_set'; the placeholder is visible only to a reader who opens the objective.. WHY THIS TIER: The gate's own detail sentence, 'all 1 objective(s) carry a KPI', is served for a plan whose only objective's KPI is a placeholder the Chief-instruct fallback wrote; nothing on the surface says the KPI is a placeholder, so the shortfall is invisible rather than disclosed (tier 3). It is not tier 1 because the gate truthfully reports presence — it is the presence test itself that lets the platform's own text through. REFUTER: Reproduced. board.py:791-796 writes '<instruction> | (KPI to be set by the Board) | | AI CEO' through parse_objective_lines with source chief_instruct_fallback whenever the model path yields no objectives (every call on the floor); ChiefInstruction.scope (board.py:686) may be any vsb_id. business_plan.py:228-245 tests only str(kpi).strip() and returns ok:true 'kpi_set' / 'all N objective(s) carry a KPI'. Live: GET /api/v1/business-plan?vsb_id=workstation → one objective obj-cd98c9e9 with kpi '(KPI to be set by the Board)', source chief_instruct_fallback. The gate's only consumers are marketplace.py:381 and :464, which raise 409 on failure and proceed SILENTLY on ok — so at the point of release nothing tells a user the KPI they released on is the platform's own placeholder. Tier 2 not 1: the ok-branch sentence is never rendered (no route exposes it), and the Business Plan page shows the placeholder text in the KPI column, so no reached surface asserts a false fact; the shortfall is that the R5 release block is bypassed by the platform's own text with no disclosure at the release surface. Not tier 3 because the marketplace listing path says nothing about it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Have the fallback write kpi '' (as _seed_plan_from_journey does) and let the gate's message name the directive-sourced objective; or make kpi_release_gate treat the literal placeholder (or source == chief_instruct_fallback with no edit) as unset.

items.title: The Heartbeat page says 'All five are OFF by default' above seven switches and 'Your choices are saved and survive a restart' for two that do not — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8 'ever self-managing' with Owner-set autonomy; §15.6 honesty over polish. OBSERVED: HeartbeatMonitor renders the AUTONOMY array (7 entries) with the counter '{n} of 7 on', then the paragraph 'All five are OFF by default and take effect on the NEXT beat. … Your choices are saved and survive a restart.' whenever autonomy_persisted !== false. The backend persists only the five W420 flags + interval; auto_metabolic and circadian_to_atp are runtime-only by design (FU-367, Owner ruling 2026-10-07). EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/organism/HeartbeatMonitor.tsx:47-72 (seven AUTONOMY rows), :139-146 (the 'All five' and 'saved and survive a restart' copy); agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:1266-1276 (auto_metabolic/circadian_to_atp set but 'DELIBERATELY NOT PERSISTED'), :1322-1328 (status bases saying a restart returns them to off); GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status shows auto_metabolic_basis and circadian_to_atp_basis. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly — each of the two rows' captions says 'Runtime only: a restart turns it off', so the page contradicts itself rather than hiding it.. WHY THIS TIER: A reached page states, as a fact about the switch a user just turned on, that it is saved and survives a restart; for Self-reflect (auto_metabolic) and Circadian energy (circadian_to_atp) that is untrue — configure() leaves them out of _AUTONOMY_KEYS and status says 'a restart returns it to off'. A false sentence about what the platform did with the user's choice is a truth defect even though each row's own caption contradicts it. Low consequence, so ranked below the two findings above. REFUTER: Reproduced from source. HeartbeatMonitor.tsx:45-72 declares SEVEN AUTONOMY rows; :139-146 renders the counter '{n} of 7 on' and then the paragraph 'All five are OFF by default and take effect on the NEXT beat … Your choices are saved and survive a restart.' whenever autonomy_persisted !== false — and the live status returns autonomy_persisted:true, so that sentence is what a user reads. heartbeat.py:1194 _AUTONOMY_KEYS holds only the five W420 flags; configure() (:1255-1281) sets auto_metabolic and circadian_to_atp but the comment says DELIBERATELY NOT PERSISTED and status (:1322-1328) says 'a restart returns it to off'. The two rows' own captions (:67,:71) say 'Runtime only: a restart turns it off'. Tier 1 rather than 3: the page makes a positive, generic assertion about what the platform did with the user's choice that is false for two of the seven switches, plus a false count ('All five'); a caption contradicting the headline sentence leaves the reader with two incompatible statements, which is not a disclosed shortfall. Low consequence (a lever reverts on restart), so it ranks below [0]. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Derive the count from AUTONOMY.length and split the sentence: 'Five of these are saved and survive a restart; Self-reflect and Circadian energy are runtime-only.'

items.title: The BTO catalogue describes the Realms as "Learner · Developer · Enterprise · Scholar" and lists five Domains — a drifted §17.1 vocabulary the taxonomy module was created to eliminate — MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v13 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD fc81a933 on :8031, twelve agents. STRUCK IN ERROR by the renderer and restored in the same round: the refuter marked it refuted while writing that the defect is real and tier 1 stands (only the verdict word was corrected). VISION CLAIM: §17.1: Realms are Enterprise · Learning · Developing · Scholarship; Domains are Religion · Science · Education · Law · Employment/Career · Care. taxonomy.ts header: "every routed surface now imports from here instead of re-declaring its own variant". OBSERVED: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/BTOCatalog.tsx:23-24 hard-code `desc: 'Religion · Science · Law · Care · Education'` and `desc: 'Learner · Developer · Enterprise · Scholar'`; line 402 renders `title={c.desc}` on the selectable component button, so the text is shown on hover (and read by assistive tech). The file does not import lib/taxonomy.ts. POST /api/v1/bto/configure with components [realms, domains] returns `available: [Enterprise, Learning, Developing, Scholarship]` and the six canonical domains with routes — so the page's own hover text contradicts its own blueprint. EVIDENCE: BTOCatalog.tsx lines 15-27 (BTO_COMPONENTS) and 392-402; curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8031/api/v1/bto/configure -d '{"entity_name":"T","components":["realms","domains"]}' → realms.available = ["Enterprise","Learning","Developing","Scholarship"], domains.available has six incl. Employment. grep -l taxonomy apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/*.tsx does not list BTOCatalog.tsx. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No; the hover text is presented as the component's description.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader hovering the Realms component on /bto is told the realms are Learner, Developer, Enterprise and Scholar, and that the Domains component covers "Religion · Science · Law · Care · Education" (no Employment). Both are untrue against the canon (Enterprise · Learning · Developing · Scholarship; six domains) and against the page's own result, which comes back with the canonical lists. It is an assertion on a reached surface, so tier 1 rather than 2; it is ranked at the bottom of the tier-1 findings because it is a tooltip label, not a figure or an outcome, and the blueprint the user then receives shows the correct names. REFUTER: The defect is real and reproduced, but DOC_OVERCLAIM is the wrong verdict: that word means a vision or canon document claims more than the system does, and here no document over-claims — a working UI surface (the BTO component picker) asserts drifted realm and domain names in its tooltip while its own blueprint returns the canonical ones. That is a surface working with an undisclosed shortfall: PARTIAL. Tier 1 stands: 'Learner · Developer · Enterprise · Scholar' and a five-domain list are assertions shown to a reader (title attribute on hover, read by assistive tech) and are untrue against §17.1 and against the response the same click produces; it is at the bottom of tier 1 because it is a tooltip label, not a figure or outcome, and the blueprint the user then receives is correct. Not tier 2 because it is an assertion, not an omission. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Derive the two desc strings from REALM_LABELS and DOMAIN_LABELS in lib/taxonomy.ts (`Object.values(...).join(' · ')`) and extend the existing taxonomy-drift guard to BTOCatalog.tsx.

items.title: The resource optimiser returns an allocation nothing reads, from a degenerate objective with two typed demands
items.why: FOUND 2026-10-09 while reconsidering an external brief against the resource-management code. agentic_core/optimization/aro.py AutonomousResourceOptimisation.optimize() runs scipy's differential evolution and returns an 'allocation' of four weights (simulation, reasoning, ontology, fabric). MEASURED: git grep current_allocation finds only aro.py - nothing consumes the allocation, so nothing is allocated. The objective is linear in the weights (score = sum of weight x demand, with a penalty for not summing to 1), so the optimum is always everything on the largest demand; and two of the four demands are constants in the file (ontology 0.3, fabric 0.4) under the comment 'Simulated demand'. It is exposed as the CEO tool optimize_qep_resources (agentic_core/api/v138/ceo.py:77). MEASURE FIRST whether the tool's result reaches a reader in CEOChat; if it does this is a truth defect on a reached surface and is re-tiered. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: remove the tool and the module (nothing depends on the result), or have it state that it computes a split nothing applies, from the two demands it was given, and drop the typed ones.

items.title: The Religion tools stamp '§11 COMPLIANCE FAIL — this output did not pass the constitutional screen' on a question that merely NAMES a prohibited thing, and write it into every export — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11: compliance engines (Halal/Sharia …) are integrated into every workflow, not bolted on; floor-served output is never presented as more than it is; honesty over polish (§15.6). OBSERVED: Every domain-tool response is passed through assure_delivery, which runs the keyword screen over the OUTPUT. On the floor the output is an echo of the user's own words, so a fiqh question that asks about riba, or a halal review of a product declaring pork gelatin, is failed by the Sharia word list. I executed both: POST /api/v1/religion/fatwa-research with 'Is it permissible to take an interest-bearing mortgage, and what is the ruling on riba and gambling?' returned ai_provenance.quality_assurance.compliance_overall = 'fail'; POST /api/v1/religion/halal-review with ingredients ['pork gelatin','sugar'] returned 'fail' (the same tool on 'dates' returned 'review'). DomainTool.tsx then renders a red banner '§11 compliance FAIL — this output did not pass the constitutional screen' and withDisclosures() prepends '[§11 COMPLIANCE: FAIL — this output did not pass the constitutional screen]' to the copied, saved and downloaded text. The failing reason (a matched keyword) is not shown on the tool — only the overall. The same event is filed as an immune failure: a deliverable I produced minutes later carried immune.by_type {'compliance_fail': 1}, hot_endpoint 'compliance:tool:religion_halal', health 0.9, 'health and threat are computed from 1 failure(s)' — i.e. a user asking the halal tool about a haram ingredient lowered the organism health figure published on an unrelated deliverable. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/religion/fatwa-research (riba question) -> compliance_overall 'fail'; POST /api/v1/religion/halal-review (pork gelatin) -> 'fail', (dates) -> 'review'; POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce -> quality_assurance.biomimetic.immune {health 0.9, errors_in_window 1, by_type {compliance_fail:1}, hot_endpoint 'compliance:tool:religion_halal'}. Read: agentic_core/api/_ai_provenance.py:140-156 (screen runs on `output`, label tool:{agent}); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/DomainTool.tsx:87-93 and 354-357 (banner + export prefix). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The tool shows only the overall FAIL; the matched-keyword reason and the 'a keyword screen, not a certification' wording exist only on /compliance.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown the sentence '§11 compliance FAIL — this output did not pass the constitutional screen' in red, and the same sentence heads the exported file. What actually happened is that a word list matched a term the user asked ABOUT, in the Religion domain's own research tool, whose purpose is to ask about exactly those terms. That is a negative certification of something the platform could not assess (a study question is not a haram offering), so it is tier 1 rather than tier 2: it is not a silent shortfall, it is an asserted verdict. It is not tier 3 because nothing on the tool says the FAIL is a keyword match on the user's own question. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/religion/fatwa-research with the riba/mortgage question returned ai_provenance.quality_assurance.compliance_overall 'fail'; POST /api/v1/religion/halal-review (pork gelatin, sugar) returned 'fail' while the tool's own ingredient_screen correctly returned verdict null. _ai_provenance.py:140-156 runs assure_delivery over `output` (an echo of the user's words on the floor). DomainTool.tsx:91-93 prepends '[§11 COMPLIANCE: FAIL — this output did not pass the constitutional screen]' to exported text and :354-357 renders the red banner; no matched-keyword reason and no 'keyword screen, not a certification' wording is on the tool. The immune side-effect is real: a genesis journey I ran afterwards carried immune {health 0.3, threat_level HIGH, by_type {compliance_fail: 7}} with a playbook recommending throttling. Tier 1 rather than 2 is borderline and I hold it: the sentence is literally true of the word list, but it is shown as a §11 FAIL verdict from 'the constitutional screen' (the constitutional row is in fact not_checked; the hit is the sharia vocabulary) on a study question nothing assessed, heads the exported file, and feeds a HIGH threat figure on unrelated records. Not tier 3: nothing on the tool says the FAIL is a keyword match on the user's own question. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: On Offering-1 tools, render the verdict's own reason beside it ('the word list matched "riba" in the text — a keyword screen, not a finding about this output'), and do not file a research/halal-review subject's keyword match as an immune failure. Better: for the Religion tools, screen as 'review' when the matched term is the declared SUBJECT of the request.

items.title: The QEP adaptation engine reports 'blueprint_generated' and tells the user 'the request named no domain' after discarding the pattern and the two domains they entered — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10: every solution is specifically designed; §11.4: every AI-served surface renders serving provenance and floor output is never presented as more than it is. A.6 feature 12 status: 'an adaptation registry surface exists'. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/qep/adaptation/execute with {pattern:'spaced repetition with mastery gates', source_domain:'religion', target_domain:'care'} returned status 'blueprint_generated' and a blueprint whose three sections each read: "Native structured frame for 'Adapted Mechanism' over: (domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain). … - (no salient terms extracted)". The subject is empty: the floor received the route's wrapper prompt and extracted nothing of what the user typed. The entry is nevertheless appended to the persisted adaptation registry (my two probes are now rows ADP-f7cda08c and ADP-f326e4ca) with status blueprint_generated. QEPIntelligence.tsx renders the blueprint in a <pre> with the chip 'blueprint_generated' and the note 'a blueprint was generated and recorded'. The same mechanism empties the management-system generator: POST /api/v1/mgmt/qms/generate for organisation 'R1 Audit Madrasah' returned standard 'ISO 9001:2015' with sections reading 'Structured service frame for: .' and '(no salient terms extracted)' — the organisation name appears nowhere in its own QMS. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/qep/adaptation/execute (twice), GET /api/v1/qep/adaptation/registry, POST /api/v1/mgmt/qms/generate. Read: agentic_core/api/qep_intelligence.py:370-414 (prompt wraps pattern/domains in prose; status set to blueprint_generated whenever the gateway returns text); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/qep/QEPIntelligence.tsx:196-212. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the floor badge and 'outline-grade' chip are shown, and the status note says nothing was installed. That the engine read none of the request is not disclosed — the text asserts the opposite cause.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown 'domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain' and '(no salient terms extracted)' directly beneath a form in which they typed a pattern and selected two domains, under a chip saying a blueprint was generated. The sentence is untrue about their request, and 'blueprint generated and recorded' describes three empty headings. The floor badge is present (so 'no model ran' is disclosed and is not the defect); what lands this on tier 1 rather than 3 is that the surface misreports what the user asked and records an empty frame as a generated blueprint. REFUTER: Reproduced. POST /api/v1/qep/adaptation/execute with pattern 'spaced repetition with mastery gates', religion -> care returned status 'blueprint_generated', a new persisted row ADP-82a68832, and three sections each reading "over: (domain: WITHHELD — the request named no domain) ... (no salient terms extracted)". qep_intelligence.py:370-414 sets blueprint_generated whenever the gateway returns any text; QEPIntelligence.tsx:200-212 renders the chip, the <pre> and the status_note 'a blueprint was generated and recorded'. The floor badge ('outline-grade') is shown, so 'no model ran' is disclosed and is not the defect. Tier 1 rather than 3 because the text tells the user their request named no domain directly under a form where they chose two, and records three empty headings as a generated blueprint. The QMS half I only partly reproduced: POST /api/v1/mgmt/qms/generate returned a floor-noted response but I did not read its sections, so that sub-claim rests on the assessor. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Pass pattern / source / target to the floor as labelled fields (or as the subject), and when the composed frame extracts no terms return status 'not_generated' with that reason and do NOT append a registry row.

items.title: The QEP roadmap tells learners 'A record of completion is issued instead' — nothing in the system can issue one — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.12.2 (ruled): QEP issues no certificate; 'A record of completion is issued instead, stating plainly that it is not a credential. Built W594: the issuing path returns completion_record_id with status RECORDED and is_credential: false.' OBSERVED: The Certifications card in QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx (rendered on the Religion hub's QEP Flagship tab) reads: 'Not offered, by ruling: QEP issues no certificate in its own name (Appendix A.12.2). A record of completion is issued instead, and it states that it is not a credential.' The only code that produces a completion_record_id is qep_flagship.certifications(), which requires user.progress[course_id].completed — and nothing in agentic_core writes that field (grep for a writer returns only the reader at qep_flagship.py:381-382; the user record is created with 'progress': {}). No HTTP route exposes it: the OpenAPI document has no path containing certif/complet for QEP; the method is reachable only as a tool name inside the AI CEO's ToolRegistry. No course or curriculum exists to complete (A.6 feature 5). So the refusal half of the card is true and DELIVERED; the 'is issued instead' half describes a path that cannot run. EVIDENCE: Read: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:48; agentic_core/reactor/religion/qep_flagship.py:363-418; agentic_core/api/v138/ceo.py:36-70,132-134. WHY THIS TIER: The sentence a learner reads is 'A record of completion is issued instead, and it states that it is not a credential.' QEPFlagshipFeatures.tsx:48 prints 'A record of completion is issued instead, and it states that it is not a credential.' qep_flagship.certifications() (363-420) only records when user.progress[course_id].completed is set; the only occurrences of 'progress' in that file are the initialiser `"progress": {}` (line 62) and the reader (381-382) — no writer. /openapi.json has no path containing certif/complet/scholar for QEP (only quests, economy transfers and AI completion matched). items.title: The federated compliance screen's own basis says 'NOTHING here assessed this subject, so the overall is review' on responses whose overall is FAIL, and it fails a museum exhibition for mentioning gambling — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11: continuously monitored live compliance to legal, regulatory and best-practice standards; solutions ethically evaluated for human and environmental well-being, safety, quality and value. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/compliance/check on 'An interest-bearing payday loan product with 400% APR marketed to students' returns overall 'fail', compliant false, and a basis ending '— NOTHING here assessed this subject, so the overall is 'review' and no part of it may be reported as compliant'. The same contradiction appears on 'A museum exhibition on the history of gambling laws in Britain' (overall fail, compliant false, sharia row reason '…HARAM_ELEMENT_GAMBLING. (engine-backed)' while assessed_by is [] and the basis says nothing assessed it) and on 'Sell counterfeit medicines…'. The basis string is built unconditionally from `can` being empty (compliance.py:240-242) without reading `overall`. On the /compliance page the basis is not rendered, but the page prints its own version: a red FAIL header followed by 'NOTHING here assessed this subject. A keyword screen can refuse a subject; it cannot clear one.' What the screen does well, verified: negated terms ('pork-free', 'riba-free') downgrade to review with the reason stated; a subject calling itself halal is review, never pass; regulatory/EHS/ethical with no match read 'not_assessed', never clear; every row carries coverage. What it is: six word lists. All four ethical dimensions returned not_assessed on every subject I sent, and no row ever had coverage 'engine'. §11's 'ethically evaluated' and 'live compliance to legal, regulatory, international standards' are therefore not delivered — and the page says so in its header and per row. EVIDENCE: Executed: GET /api/v1/compliance/frameworks; POST /api/v1/compliance/check x7 (payday loan, tutoring service, pork-free sausage, gambling museum, qard hasan, counterfeit medicines, riba-free mortgage). Read: agentic_core/api/compliance.py:205-243; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/governance/ComplianceChecker.tsx (whole file); apps/workstation-superapp/src/lib/api.ts:202-254. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The word-list nature is disclosed thoroughly (header, framework cards, per-row reasons). The basis/overall contradiction and the meaning of 'engine-backed' on a row no engine is credited with are not.. WHY THIS TIER: The response body — which is also sealed into every deliverable's quality record as compliance.basis — states 'the overall is review' beside overall: 'fail'. That is one sentence asserting a verdict the same object contradicts, so it is tier 1 rather than tier 3; and a history exhibition is told compliant: false with a row labelled '(engine-backed)' while assessed_by is empty. The large capability gap (word lists, not engines) is NOT what tiers this: that part is stated on the page and would be tier 3 on its own. REFUTER: Reproduced. POST /api/v1/compliance/check on the gambling-museum subject returned overall 'fail', compliant false, assessed_by [], sharia row reason ending '(engine-backed)' with coverage 'vocabulary', and basis ending "NOTHING here assessed this subject, so the overall is 'review' and no part of it may be reported as compliant". The payday-loan subject gave the same fail / 'overall is review' contradiction. compliance.py:236-242 builds that clause from `can` being empty without reading `overall`. The word-list nature is disclosed per row ('a keyword screen, not a certification'), so the capability gap alone would be tier 3. Tier 1 because the response body (the reached form of this route, and what is sealed into quality records) states a verdict the same object contradicts, and labels a row 'engine-backed' while crediting no engine. I did not read ComplianceChecker.tsx, so the claim about what the page prints is the assessor's. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Compute the basis tail from `overall` ('a row refused this subject on a word match; nothing here assessed it' when overall is fail), and drop or define '(engine-backed)' so it agrees with assessed_by.

items.title: The Genesis stage rail says 'N candidate(s) were modelled and ranked' on a run whose own quality record withholds both 'modelled' and 'ranked' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10 as amended (ruling 2026-10-05b R3): modelled · simulated · ranked · optimised are each WITHHELD on a tie or on identical candidates, with the reason, rather than attested. OBSERVED: I ran POST /api/v1/genesis/journey (religion × learning, establish false). The backend behaved exactly as the amendment says: candidates_distinct 1 of 3, candidates_are_alternatives false, selection_basis 'TIE at 0.795 … resolved by list order, NOT by evidence', and bar_measured records modelled 'not attested: one text modelled 3 times is not 3 candidates modelled', simulated 'nothing was simulated apart', ranked and optimised 'not attested'; summary '0 measured · 1 attested · 2 screen-only · 13 not measured (of 16)'. The page renders the comparison note in place of ranked cards and prints the honesty line. But railState() in GenesisJourney.tsx lights the Model·Simulate·Rank tile as done/'ran' whenever the candidates array is non-empty, with the tooltip '3 candidate(s) were modelled and ranked. This stage carries no §10 verification entry…', and the card's footer appends '— the winner is carried into Design' to a selection the same sentence says was made by list order. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/genesis/journey; GET /api/v1/genesis/status. Read: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/synthesis/GenesisJourney.tsx:98-129, 612-640 (rail title), 800-919 (stage 5 card); agentic_core/api/genesis.py:204-275. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The correct account is on the stage-5 card and in the §10 chip tooltip; the rail tile contradicts it.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader hovering the lit stage tile is shown '3 candidate(s) were modelled and ranked', and the record on the same page says neither happened. It is an asserted outcome the platform declined to attest, so tier 1 rather than 2. It is low severity, not tier 3, because the correcting text is elsewhere on the page rather than on the tile that makes the claim. REFUTER: Reproduced. My POST /api/v1/genesis/journey (religion x learning, establish false) returned 3 candidates, candidates_distinct 1, candidates_are_alternatives false, selection_basis 'TIE at 0.774 ... resolved by list order, NOT by evidence', and bar_measured modelled/simulated/optimised 'not attested'. GenesisJourney.tsx:114-119 lights the Model·Simulate·Rank tile 'ran' whenever the candidates array is non-empty with why = 'N candidate(s) were modelled and ranked...', and line 896 appends '— the winner is carried into Design.' Important qualifier the finding understates: the sentence is a `title` tooltip on the small state chip (line 635), not visible text; the visible chip says only 'ran'. It is still an asserted outcome the run's own record declines to attest, so tier 1 rather than 2; lowest severity in the set because the correct account is on the stage-5 card. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Have railState read candidates_are_alternatives / tie.detected and say 'N candidate texts were produced; they were identical, so nothing was modelled apart or ranked'.

items.title: The vision's §10 says modelled, simulated, ranked and optimised are 'measured, with an instrument' — the system records them only as caller-ATTESTED, and reports 'categorised' as met although §10 says it has no instrument — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §10 amendment: 'Sixteen criteria are named above and instruments exist for four. Measured, with an instrument: modelled · simulated · ranked · optimised … Named, with NO instrument anywhere: best-in-class · innovative · effective · efficient · commercially viable · tested · validated · categorised. These are not reported as met.' OBSERVED: vbs/quality._measure_bar has exactly four criteria a gate can measure, and they are different ones: 'specifically designed' and 'verified' (from coverage/stub — both recorded not assessable on floor output) and 'compliant' and 'safe' (from the §11 rows — recorded source 'screen', never met, while the screens are word lists). modelled/simulated/ranked/optimised can only arrive through genesis._bar_attestations as `source: caller, measured: False, attested: True` — the code's own docstring: 'an attestation is a claim about a run, not a measurement'. Conversely 'categorised' IS reported met: my journey returned categorised {met: true, source: caller, 'realm learning × domain religion, both chosen by the caller'}, and tested/validated are attestable the same way when all stages verify. On every run I executed the measured count was 0 of 16 (deliverable: '0 measured · 0 attested · 2 screen-only · 14 not measured'; journey: '0 measured · 1 attested · 2 screen-only · 13 not measured'). The surfaces are honest about this — Deliverables.tsx and GenesisJourney.tsx print the summary chip and separate MEASURED from ATTESTED in the tooltip — so the product under-claims relative to the canon; it is the canon sentence that is wrong, in both directions. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/deliverables/produce (bar_measured), GET /api/v1/deliverables, GET /api/v1/deliverables/types, POST /api/v1/genesis/journey. Read: agentic_core/vbs/quality.py:153-286; agentic_core/api/genesis.py:204-275; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/Deliverables.tsx:195-362; docs/WORKSTATION_IDBO_WHOLE_VISION.md §10. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: At the surface, yes (measured / attested / not measured are stated apart). In the vision text, no.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader of the canon is told four criteria are 'measured, with an instrument' and that 'categorised' is 'not reported as met'; the system measures none of those four and does report categorised met. Nothing in the canon says so, which makes it an invisible shortfall (tier 2) rather than a disclosed one. It is not tier 1 because the reached product surface states the truth ('attested … a claim about a run, not a measurement'); the untruth is in the document, not shown to a user of the app. REFUTER: Reproduced. Vision §10 lines 498-502 say 'Measured, with an instrument: modelled · simulated · ranked · optimised' and that categorised is 'not reported as met'. genesis._bar_attestations puts those four in `ev` (attested) or `wh` (withheld) and attests 'categorised' when the caller chose realm and domain; quality.py:255-263 records them source 'caller', measured False, attested True, with the docstring that an attestation is not a measurement; only gate-sourced criteria count as measured (266-286). My journey's record showed modelled/simulated/optimised 'not attested', source none. One refinement: compliant/safe CAN be gate-measured when a §11 row fails (quality.py:231-235), so 'never met' is right but 'never measured' is not quite. Tier 2 rather than 1 because the untruth is in the canon document, not on an app surface, and the product record separates measured from attested; not tier 3 because the canon does not disclose it. I did not read Deliverables.tsx. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Amend §10 to say: gate-measurable = specifically designed · verified (not on floor output) and compliant · safe (screen-only today); attested by the journey, never measured = modelled · simulated · ranked · optimised · categorised · tested · validated; and state that with no model serving the measured count is 0 of 16.

items.title: Floor-served tafsir, fiqh and halal results open with 'Acting as: Islamic scholar and Quranic exegete' — a scholar persona line that travels into every export — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §11.4: floor-served output is never presented as scholarship or translation. §11.5: AI content is labelled AI-assisted — never authoritative. OBSERVED: With every scholarly section correctly withheld, the body that remains and is rendered in the result <pre> is, for POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir: '_[Workstation native structured engine — owned, no external dependency]_ / _Acting as: Islamic scholar and Quranic exegete._'. For fatwa-research: '_Acting as: Islamic studies scholar with expertise in classical jurisprudence (fiqh)._'; for halal-review: '_Acting as: halal certification consultant with expertise in Islamic dietary law…_'; for interfaith: '_Acting as: scholar of comparative religion…_'. This is the prompt's role instruction echoed by the deterministic floor as a statement about itself. It is surrounded by strong true statements (amber floor_note 'the floor composes headings, not scholarship', the withheld-sections list, the disclaimer 'NOT a scholarly tafsir and NOT a ruling'), and withDisclosures() carries the body — persona line included — into copy, save and download. The halal body additionally keeps generic filler under real headings ('Steps to Achieve Certification — Validate the structured outputs above against the stated objective', 'Likelihood × impact to be scored'). The tafsir button still reads 'Generate tafsir' for a run that by design generates none. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir (1:1-3; 2:1-60 capped to 2:1-10 with range_note; 1:9 -> 422; 2:275), POST /api/v1/religion/fatwa-research, POST /api/v1/religion/hadith-study, POST /api/v1/religion/halal-review, POST /api/v1/religion/interfaith, GET /api/v1/religion/schools. Read: apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/domains/ReligionHub.tsx:128-285; apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/DomainTool.tsx:87-101, 290-373. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The floor and the withholding are disclosed; that the persona line is an artefact is not.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown 'Acting as: Islamic scholar and Quranic exegete' as the first line of the result — on the surface where the constitution says the floor must never be presented as scholarship. I place it at tier 2 rather than 1 because the same card states, in three places, that this is not scholarship and that those sections are withheld, so a reader is not left believing a scholar spoke; and above tier 3 because nothing on the surface says that line is an echoed instruction, and it is the only non-disclaimer text in the body and in the exported file. REFUTER: Reproduced. POST /api/v1/religion/quran-tafsir (1:1-3) returned tafsir body consisting only of '_[Workstation native structured engine — owned, no external dependency]_' and '_Acting as: Islamic scholar and Quranic exegete._', with seven sections withheld and a floor_note. fatwa-research opened with 'Acting as: Islamic studies scholar with expertise in classical jurisprudence (fiqh)'; halal-review with 'Acting as: halal certification consultant...' plus generic filler ('Validate the structured outputs above against the stated objective', 'Likelihood × impact to be scored'). DomainTool.tsx withDisclosures carries the body into exports. Tier 2 rather than 1: the line is immediately preceded by the native-engine stamp and surrounded by the floor note, the withheld list and the disclaimer, so a reader is not told a scholar spoke; rather than 3: nothing says the line is an echoed prompt instruction and it is the only non-disclaimer text in the tafsir body. I did not call hadith-study or interfaith or read ReligionHub.tsx. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Strip the 'Acting as:' echo from floor output for the five Religion tools (or render it as 'the request asked for the role of …; the floor does not take it'), and relabel the button 'Retrieve ayah + study frame'.

items.title: QEP learner records are keyed by a caller-supplied uid with no identity check, and the studio hard-codes every user to the uid 'local' while calling the record 'yours' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R1)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R1), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: A.5.8: encryption, role-based access control; per-tenant isolation (§17.5 invariant 1); 'Learner data — especially children's — is the strictest case this platform holds.' A.6 feature 1: learner / teacher / parent / admin roles. OBSERVED: QEPStudio.tsx sets `const UID = 'local'` and uses it for hifz schedule, review, progress and gamification. The hifz and gamification routes in religious_domain/api.py take uid from the body or path and carry no Depends(get_current_user) (grep for Depends/current_user/owner_id in the file returns nothing, whereas qep_intelligence.py in the same prefix does bind the caller). I read and wrote an arbitrary learner's record unauthenticated: scheduled 112:1-4 and recorded a review for 'r1audit_w639', read its full progress_matrix back by path, and awarded it 10 XP — after which GET /api/v1/qep/leaderboard ranks 'r1audit_w639' #1 with caller_asserted_xp 10. In this single-user, AUTH-off environment the page's wording is true; I could not execute an AUTH-on deployment, so the multi-user consequence is reasoned from the source: every signed-in user of one deployment would share one hifz record and one XP total under 'local', the leaderboard would show a single row named 'local', and any caller could read or alter any learner's memorisation history by guessing a uid. The surfaces say 'Your real learning path is your hifz schedule' (LearnTeachModule) and 'Your memorisation review counts are real, from your own records' (roadmap card). The award route does disclose its own weakness honestly: award_source 'caller_asserted', 'the platform did not observe it'. Teacher and parent roles do not exist. EVIDENCE: Executed: POST /api/v1/qep/hifz/schedule, POST /api/v1/qep/hifz/review, GET /api/v1/qep/hifz/progress/{uid}, GET /api/v1/qep/gamification/{uid}, POST /api/v1/qep/gamification/award, GET /api/v1/qep/leaderboard — all with an invented uid and no credentials. Read: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/QEPStudio.tsx:20,49-115; agentic_core/religious_domain/api.py:544-702; apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/LearnTeachModule.tsx:83-89. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. Only the caller-asserted nature of manual XP awards is disclosed.. WHY THIS TIER: What the reader is shown is 'your own records'. Nothing on the surface says the record is a shared fixed id that any caller can read or write. That is a shortfall the surface does not state (tier 2). I do not put it at tier 1 because in the environment I could execute — single-user — the sentence is true; the untruth appears only with more than one user, which I reasoned from source and did not run. REFUTER: Reproduced. QEPStudio.tsx:20 is `const UID = 'local'` and it is used for hifz schedule/review/progress and gamification (lines 51-52, 90, 111). grep for Depends/current_user/owner_id in agentic_core/religious_domain/api.py returns nothing. GET /api/v1/qep/hifz/progress/{uid} with an invented uid answered unauthenticated, and GET /api/v1/qep/leaderboard shows the assessor's invented uid 'r1audit_w639' ranked #1 with caller_asserted_xp 10 — the write persisted. Limits: AUTH is off in this environment, so I could not show whether a global middleware would at least require a session in AUTH-on mode; the per-uid binding is absent regardless. Tier 2: the surface says the record is 'yours' and nothing discloses that it is a shared fixed id any caller can read or write; not tier 1 because in the executable single-user environment the wording is true and the multi-user consequence is reasoned from source; not tier 3 because it is undisclosed. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Derive the learner id from the authenticated caller on the hifz/gamification routes (as qep_intelligence already does), refuse a uid that is not the caller's, and have the studio stop sending a literal.

items.title: A founder who records their own concept is still told, on the entity record and in the shipped repository, that the concept 'still awaits the owned model' - and a floor-born VSB can never leave 'body pending' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §4.8 Establish the VSB IDBO Enterprise; §13 'a body the floor served is shipped as the founder's own words plus an honest content-pending state'; §15.6 honesty over polish. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/vsb/{id}/concept returned 200 with concept_source 'founder' and the blueprint concept replaced. Immediately afterwards GET /api/v1/vsb/{id} still returned body_pending.concept=true, status_basis '4 body section(s) still await the owned model: commercialisation, concept, design, operations' and stage_basis 'no §4 lifecycle stage is reached: the first section (concept) still awaits the owned model'; genome_spec.concept still read 'content pending the owned model - this enterprise has not yet composed its own concept'. After a re-ship (POST /repo/ship, 200) the SAME repository carried the founder's concept under '## Concept' in BUSINESS_PLAN.md while README.md printed the stale stage basis and genome.json/IDENTITY.md printed the pending marker. The same happens through the UI's own route: POST /api/v1/business-plan/set with a concept dropped 'concept' from the PLAN's body_pending, while the ENTITY kept all four. Cause: the entity's body_pending map is written only at birth (genesis.py 1390/1513/1604/1734, vsb.py 2556); no handler in vsb.py or business_plan.py ever clears it or calls _rederive on a concept change. There is no route at all to supply design, operations or commercialisation after birth, so _derived_status can never return anything past 'body pending' for an entity born on the floor - even with Self-run on. The concept change also did not mark the shipped body stale (GET /repo/ship -> stale: false), so the cockpit's 'Shipped body is current' line would stand over a body that predates the edit. EVIDENCE: vsb-1a0e91006d: POST /concept -> 200 {concept_source:'founder'}; GET /vsb/{id} -> status_basis and stage_basis unchanged, status_derived_at unchanged (20:36:07Z, the earlier gate decision); C:/tmp/m1_audit/data/vsb_repos/vsb-1a0e91006d/README.md line 7 vs BUSINESS_PLAN.md '## Concept'; agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1376-1390 (record_vsb_concept saves blueprint + concept_source only), :1796 and :1839 (the only readers), grep shows no writer of body_pending after birth. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The surface asserts the opposite of what happened.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown the sentence 'the first section (concept) still awaits the owned model' on the entity record and in the shipped README after the founder has written that section, beside a business plan in the same repo that contains it. That is an untrue statement on the reached form (response body, stored record, shipped file), not an omission and not a disclosed gap, so it is tier 1 rather than 2. The /concept route itself is API-only (no frontend caller), but /business-plan/set is the Business Plan page's edit route and produces the same contradiction. REFUTER: Reproduced from live state and code. GET /api/v1/vsb/{id} on vsb-1a0e91006d returns concept_source 'founder' and a founder-written genesis_blueprint.concept, while the same body still says body_pending.concept=true, status_basis '4 body section(s) still await the owned model: commercialisation, concept, design, operations' and stage_basis '...the first section (concept) still awaits the owned model'. The shipped repo on disk has the founder's concept under '## Concept' in BUSINESS_PLAN.md while README.md line 7 prints the stale stage basis and genome.json/IDENTITY.md print the pending marker for concept. record_vsb_concept (vsb.py ~1376-1390) saves only blueprint + concept_source; grep finds no writer of the entity's body_pending after birth (genesis.py 1390/1513/1604/1734, vsb.py 2556). Tier 1 rather than 2: the record and a shipped file assert a section is still awaited that the same repo contains - an untrue statement, not a missing label. Not re-driven by me: the POST /concept and POST /business-plan/set calls themselves (I read their effects), and the 'stale: false after concept edit' sub-claim (ship state now reads differently because of a later cycle). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Make every writer of a body section (record_vsb_concept, business-plan set/generate for a VSB scope) clear the matching body_pending key, update genome_spec, call _rederive and mark_repo_stale; and either add founder routes for design/operations/commercialisation or change the basis to say no path yet composes them.
