items.title: The one-call journey tells a founder they have an 'established living enterprise' in the same response whose nested record says 'it is not yet a living, operating enterprise' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §4.8 instantiate a living VSB IDBO that delivers and commercialises the solution; §15.2 the deliverable is a living VSB IDBO enterprise; §15.6 never fabricate. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/genesis/journey with establish=true (the page's 'Launch Journey -> Establish VSB' path) returned top-level deliverable: "The user's own VSB IDBO - Concept -> Commercialisation -> established living enterprise - frames only: every stage was served by the deterministic floor..." and enterprise_established: true. The nested established_vsb.deliverable in the same body reads 'VSB IDBO entity registered and persisted - body pending; it is not yet a living, operating enterprise', with status 'body pending', all four body sections pending, initial_ship.shipped false and autonomous_cycles false. GenesisJourney.tsx line 948 renders result.deliverable verbatim directly under the heading 'Enterprise Registered - body pending' (line 943), so the two statements sit together on the page. The same over-word recurs on reached text around it: the progress map ticks 'Establish' with hint 'Your living VSB IDBO entity', line 1105 prints 'Living Enterprise IDBO registered', the establish stream labels 'Registered as a Living Entity' / 'Living Economy Initialised', the roster row carries status 'living', the generated web app footer says 'Living VSB IDBO web app', and the seeded plan's executive summary opens '<name> is a living VSB IDBO established to solve: ...'. What actually exists at that moment: a registry record with the founder's problem statement, a slug name, four pending markers, a seven-director board template, a fixed swarm template, four generic objectives, a virtual-WST waterfall and one zero-revenue birth cycle; no repo, no website, nothing running. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/genesis.py:893-897 (the literal, conditioned only on established_vsb existing) vs :276-282 (_deliverable_line, derived from status, used only for the nested field); response saved from the run on vsb-1a0e91006d; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/synthesis/GenesisJourney.tsx:567, 943-948, 1105. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly and contradictorily: the heading and the nested status say 'registered - body pending', the sentence beneath says 'established living enterprise'.. WHY THIS TIER: The sentence a reader is shown is '-> established living enterprise', and the platform's own derived record for the same entity says it is not one. It is an assertion of an outcome the platform did not produce, not a blank and not a stated shortfall, which is tier 1. It does not drop to tier 3 because the 'frames only' suffix qualifies the stages, not the enterprise claim. REFUTER: Reproduced by code read plus a live journey call on the non-establish branch. genesis.py:893-897 emits the fixed literal '...Concept → Commercialisation → established living enterprise' whenever established_vsb exists without error, with no reference to the entity's derived status, while _deliverable_line (276-282) composes the nested 'registered and persisted — body pending; it is not yet a living, operating enterprise' from status. GenesisJourney.tsx:943-948 prints result.deliverable directly under the heading 'Enterprise Registered — body pending', and :1105 prints 'Living Enterprise IDBO registered'. My own POST /genesis/journey (establish=false) returned the sibling branch of the same expression ('A journey record ... NO enterprise was established — frames only ...'), confirming the construction; I did not create another entity to see the establish=true string live, so that half rests on the code and the assessor's run. The live roster does show status 'living' for every body-pending entity. Tier 1 rather than 3: the 'frames only' suffix qualifies the stages, not the 'established living enterprise' claim, which the platform's own nested record denies. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Build the top-level deliverable from _deliverable_line(established_vsb) instead of the literal, and make enterprise_established false (or add a separate enterprise_registered) while the status is not 'operating'; reword the 'living' labels on the progress map, stream, roster status and generated footers to follow the derived status.

items.title: The §11 veto guards only one of four establish doors: an online casino with interest-bearing loans is vetoed by the journey, yet is established by Spawn and by direct establish, then named, built and shipped with compliance 'fail' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §4 'One continuous, intelligent, autonomous workflow' with each stage verified; §13 output 'quality-gated (§10), compliance-screened (§11)'; §15.6 'Ethics architecturally binding'. OBSERVED: There is not one gated lifecycle. (a) POST /genesis/journey with the casino problem and establish=true -> status 'blocked_by_screen', all three candidates vetoed, established_vsb.error, nothing registered: correct. (b) POST /api/v1/vsb/spawn (the route VSBSpawnStudio.tsx line 181 calls, and the cockpit's empty state sends users to) with the same text -> a VSB 'Launch Online Casino' registered on the living roster with board, waqf_ltd_hybrid economy and seeded plan; the stream says 'Constitutional gate NOT evaluated - no genome/legal model is configured ... nothing was checked'; the roster shows compliance never_screened: true and economy_held false. I then named it (200), generated its website (200) and POST /repo/ship returned shipped: true, coherent_whole: true, surfaces_refused: {} with compliance_overall 'fail' on four surfaces and sharia_halal: fail 'haram term present' in the shipped compliance/QUALITY.md. (c) POST /genesis/establish called directly with the casino problem and concept -> 200, entity registered, intent gate 'allowed', first_screen overall 'fail', first cycle held (compliance_fail_hold) - the economy is held but the entity exists and nothing in vsb.py refuses a ship or surface on a compliance fail (the only refusals are pending name and Mode-3 review gates). Review gates themselves work but are all OFF by default and use a separate 8-stage vocabulary (intake...launch) from the journey's stages; any pending gate blocks every mover rather than its own stage. EVIDENCE: Runs: journey -> blocked_by_screen; vsb-7da10787dc (spawn) named 'Lucky Stakes Casino', POST /website 200, POST /repo/ship 200 with 'compliance is fail - written, not verified'; vsb-c8e4dbbfe9 (direct establish) birth_vitals.first_screen.overall 'fail'. agentic_core/api/vsb.py:2634-2710 (ship aggregates compliance, never refuses on it), :2328+ (spawn calls no §11 screen before registering). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: The individual facts are disclosed; the absence of the veto on these doors is not.. WHY THIS TIER: Each surface states its own facts truthfully - the spawn stream says nothing was checked and the ship says compliance is fail - so no single sentence is untrue, which keeps it off tier 1. But the shortfall itself is invisible: nothing tells the founder or the Owner that the veto the Genesis page demonstrates is absent on the Spawn page, and 'shipped: true · coherent_whole: true · surfaces_refused: {}' reads as a completed, accepted delivery of a body the platform's own screen failed. A partial enforcement the surface does not name is tier 2, not a disclosed tier-3 gap. REFUTER: Reproduced from stored state and code; I did not re-run the spawn or the direct establish. The live roster carries 'Lucky Stakes Casino' (vsb-7da10787dc) and 'Launch Online Casino' (vsb-c8e4dbbfe9), both status 'living'. GET /vsb/vsb-7da10787dc/repo/ship returns shipped: true, coherent_whole: true, surfaces_refused: {} with compliance_overall 'fail' on website/webapp/mobile/repo and commit message 'ship: QMS not assessable · compliance fail'. The spawn handler region (vsb.py ~2328-2570) contains only the GaaS 'Constitutional gate NOT evaluated' path and no §11 screen call before registration. VSBSpawnStudio.tsx:203-216 lists the pipeline (Six Cognitive Engines → MJM → GaaS → CEO Strategy → Genome) and discloses that the engines return fixed markers, but nowhere says the §11 veto the Genesis journey applies is not on this door. Tier 2 rather than 1: each statement shown is true (coherent_whole_basis itself reads 'compliance is fail - written, not verified'). Tier 2 rather than 3: the missing enforcement is not named at the surface, and a failed-screen body is reported 'shipped: true' with nothing refused. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Run the same §11 screen-and-veto (_refuse_vetoed_candidate's rule) at the top of spawn and genesis/establish before anything is registered, and make ship and the three public-surface generators refuse (409, naming the failed framework) while the latest screen is 'fail' - or, at minimum, state on the Spawn page and in the ship response that no veto applies there.

items.title: The same establish call records two opposite facts about the founder's product choice: the journey says 'chosen by the caller', the entity, genome and shipped IDENTITY.md say 'the default - no product was chosen' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §3 4 Realms x 6 Domains x 4 Products as the founder's selection; §13 the repo carries the entity's genome/identity. OBSERVED: POST /genesis/journey with product 'reactor' explicitly in the body and establish=true returned product_source 'chosen by the caller' at the top level. The entity it established (GET /vsb/{id}), its genome_spec, genome.json and IDENTITY.md in the shipped repo all record product_source 'the default - no product was chosen'. The journey->establish seam builds an EstablishRequest in code, so 'product' is never in that request's model_fields_set and the provenance is lost. EVIDENCE: r2 run on vsb-1a0e91006d; agentic_core/api/genesis.py:836 vs :1324 and :1349 (each reads model_fields_set of its own request object). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The stored record and a shipped file assert 'no product was chosen' about a call in which the caller chose one - an untrue statement of provenance on the reached form, so tier 1; it is low severity because the chosen value equals the default and the page already says product is 'recorded only'. REFUTER: Reproduced. My own POST /genesis/journey with product 'reactor' in the body returned product_source 'chosen by the caller'. The entity that the assessor's identical call established records product_source 'the default - no product was chosen' on GET /vsb/{id}, in genome_spec, and in the shipped genome.json:15 and IDENTITY.md:14. Cause confirmed at genesis.py:806-816: the journey builds EstablishRequest(problem, domain, realm, name, concept, ...) WITHOUT passing product at all, so the establish side's model_fields_set never contains it. The finding understates this: by that code a NON-default product chosen on the journey would not reach the entity either - it would be stored as 'reactor' and labelled default. I read that from the code and did not execute it. Tier 1 rather than 2: the stored record and a shipped file positively assert 'no product was chosen' about a call in which one was. Low severity in the observed case because the value coincides with the default. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Pass the journey's own product_source through to the internal establish call instead of re-deriving it from the inner request.

items.title: After the Owner edits the plan's concept, the Business Plan page still prints 'The concept field holds the platform's own pending-body text, which is not the Owner's words and was composed by nobody' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15.9 the Chief-owned Business Plan opens with Executive Summary · Concept · Vision - the founder's idea. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/business-plan/set with a new concept and vision for the VSB scope returned 200 and recorded owner_edits for both fields. The plan's provenance was not touched except body_pending: field_sources still says concept/vision 'establish_template', templated_fields still lists both, and opening_written_by still reads '...The concept field holds the platform's own pending-body text, which is not the Owner's words and was composed by nobody... a model or the Chief has composed nothing here.' PlanOpening.tsx line 141 renders that paragraph whenever templated_fields is non-empty, so (reasoning from source - I did not drive a browser) the page shows it above a Concept field that the per-field chip on the same card correctly marks 'owner-edited'. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/business-plan?scope=vsb-1a0e91006d after the set: owner_edits {concept, vision}, provenance.templated_fields ['executive_summary','vision','mission','strategy','concept'], opening_written_by unchanged; agentic_core/api/business_plan.py:399-437 (set_plan updates only provenance.body_pending); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/PlanOpening.tsx:141-145. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No - the stale sentence is itself the disclosure, and it is now untrue.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader is shown a sentence saying the concept is nobody's words directly above the Owner's own concept. That is a false statement on a reached page (tier 1), not a missing label (which would be tier 2); the per-field chip being right does not cancel the paragraph being wrong. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /api/v1/business-plan?scope=vsb-1a0e91006d returns concept 'A low-cost LoRa hive sensor kit ... sold through a beekeeper cooperative to UK delis.' with owner_edits for concept and vision, while provenance.field_sources still marks concept/vision 'establish_template', templated_fields still lists both, and opening_written_by still reads 'The concept field holds the platform's own pending-body text, which is not the Owner's words and was composed by nobody.' set_plan (business_plan.py:399-437) updates only provenance.body_pending. PlanOpening.tsx:75 and :141 render that paragraph whenever templated_fields is non-empty, with no owner_edits filter (the per-field chip at :157 does filter). PlanOpening is mounted on BusinessPlan.tsx and VSBCockpit.tsx. Rendering is reasoned from source, not a browser. Tier 1 rather than 2: the paragraph is a positive false statement about a field shown directly beneath it; the correct per-field chip does not retract it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: In set_plan (and the model-compose path) remove edited fields from templated_fields, set field_sources[f]='owner_supplied', and recompute opening_written_by from the fields that are still templated.

items.title: An entity's record says 'only the birth cycle ran' while the living roster counts two cycles run and booked for it — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §4.10 Run · Defend · Heal · Learn · Improve · Grow - forever; the established VSB self-operates. OBSERVED: GET /api/v1/vsb/vsb-1a0e91006d -> living.autonomous_operation: 'registered on the living roster - autonomous economy cycles are OFF (the heartbeat's Self-run lever is off), so only the birth cycle ran; enable Self-run...'. At the same time GET /api/v1/economy/living-vsbs shows that entity with operating_cycles 2, ledger_cycles 2, last_operated 20:38:28Z, and GET /repo/ship reports stale: true with stale_reason 'autonomous operating cycle 2'. The sentence about the past is composed from the present position of the lever, not from the cycle count. Caveat: I did not run the second cycle; other audit regions were using the same backend (roster rows 'R3 Audit...', 'R6 Audit Probe Cycles') and one of them most likely beat the heart with Self-run on for a moment. That explains how the cycle happened; it does not make the sentence true. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/economy/living_vsbs.py:64-75 (living_statement builds the phrase from the lever alone); roster row and ship state as quoted. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is told 'only the birth cycle ran' and the books show two. A sentence asserting a history that the platform's own counters contradict is tier 1; it is ranked low because it needs the lever to have been on and then off again. REFUTER: Reproduced. GET /vsb/vsb-1a0e91006d returns living.autonomous_operation '...autonomous economy cycles are OFF (the heartbeat's Self-run lever is off), so only the birth cycle ran...' while GET /economy/living-vsbs shows the same entity with operating_cycles 2, ledger_cycles 2, last_operated 20:38:28Z. Other entities born the same way show 1, so 2 is one cycle beyond birth. living_statement (living_vsbs.py:58-75) composes the past-tense clause from the lever's present position only. Tier 1 rather than 2: the response body asserts a history its own counters contradict. Held at tier 1 with low severity and two caveats: it needed the lever on then off (another audit region most likely did that on the shared backend), and the only frontend reference to this field I found is GenesisJourney.tsx:216 at establish time, so the reached form of the stale sentence is the API body and stored record rather than a page I can show rendering it later. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: State the lever position and the counted cycles separately ('Self-run is off; N cycle(s) have run, the last at T') instead of inferring the history from the lever.

items.title: The floor's 'Subject' line silently cuts the founder's request at 150 characters, dropping the actual ask, and calls the first five word-pairs 'the request's most frequent terms' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §4.2 Understand & Map - understand the person, the real underlying problem, constraints, goals and success criteria. OBSERVED: My request ended '...I want an affordable hive-monitoring sensor kit and a cooperative that sells their saffron honey directly to UK buyers.' Every stage prints 'Subject: Smallholder beekeepers in rural Kashmir lose about 40 percent of their hives each winter to varroa mites and cold; I want an affordable hive (domain: enterprise).' and 'Structured architecture frame for: ...I want an affordable hive.' - ending in a full stop as though that were the request. The sensor kit, the cooperative, the saffron honey and the UK market - the whole proposed solution - appear in no stage. The term list is labelled 'the request's most frequent terms' but every term occurs once; the list is the first five adjacent word pairs, and '40' is dropped so one term reads 'about percent'. Nothing marks the cut (no ellipsis, no 'truncated'). EVIDENCE: phase_1_conceptualisation.concept, phase_2_design_development and phase_3_commercialisation in the journey response; the same strings in the cascade tier outputs from POST /repo/cascade. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No - the truncation is unmarked.. WHY THIS TIER: The surface is honest that this is a term frame, so the frame itself is tier 3. But it presents 'I want an affordable hive.' as the Subject with no sign that two thirds of the ask was cut, and a reader cannot tell the engine never saw the rest - a partial reading the surface does not disclose, which is tier 2. I did not put it at tier 1 because the retained words are the founder's own, in order; nothing is invented. REFUTER: Reproduced. My journey response contains 'Subject: Smallholder beekeepers in rural Kashmir lose about 40 percent of their hives each winter to varroa mites and cold; I want an affordable hive (domain: enterprise).' and 'frame for: ... I want an affordable hive.' - no ellipsis or truncation mark - and the list is labelled 'the request's most frequent terms' (engine.py:505) though each listed pair occurs once. One correction to the stated mechanism: calling engine._subject() directly on the raw problem returns a 220-character cut ending '...saffron honey directly', so the ~140-character cut at 'hive' arises in how the genesis prompts wrap or split the problem (probably at the hyphen), not from a flat 150-character slice. The observed effect is exactly as reported. Tier 2 rather than 3: the frame is disclosed as a term count, but the unmarked cut presented as the Subject is not. Tier 2 rather than 1: the retained words are the founder's own, in order; nothing is invented, and 'most frequent' is loose rather than a fabricated figure. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Mark the cut ('... [request truncated at 150 of N characters]') or carry the full first paragraph; relabel the list 'the first terms of the request' unless a frequency is actually computed.

items.title: The 'integrated' Website, Web app and Phone app link to each other with paths that 404 in the platform's own preview, and the phone app is chipped 'offline' with no 'when hosted' qualifier — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R2)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R2), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §13 the repo 'integrates a Website, a Web app, and a Phone (mobile) app'; W446 scope: a real multi-page static site, a client-side app, an installable PWA 'offline-capable when hosted'; the platform generates, version-controls and serves them. OBSERVED: The three surfaces generate, version-control and serve: 3 pages + css, 4 web-app files, 7 PWA files with manifest, icon and service worker, each fetched 200 through its /page/{name} route. The website's nav carries 'Web app' -> ../webapp/index.html and 'Phone app' -> ../mobile/index.html, and the phone app carries links to ../web/index.html and ../webapp/index.html. Those relative paths are right inside a downloaded zip, but from the platform preview (/api/v1/vsb/{id}/website/page/index) they resolve to /api/v1/vsb/{id}/website/webapp/index.html etc., which return 404 - I requested four of them and all four were 404. The preview is the only place the founder can open the surfaces inside the platform, since it does not host them. Separately POST /mobile returns offline_capable: true and the Genesis page shows an emerald 'offline' chip; in the preview the service worker's cache list ('./', 'index.html') is not servable (mobile/page/index.html and mobile/page/ are both 404, failures swallowed by .catch), so the offline fallback has nothing to serve there. That part is reasoned from the generated sw.js and the routes, not observed in a browser. EVIDENCE: curl of website/page/index hrefs; 404s on {id}/website/webapp/index.html, {id}/website/mobile/index.html, {id}/mobile/web/index.html, {id}/webapp/web/index.html, {id}/mobile/page/index.html; mobile/sw.js ASSETS list; GenesisJourney.tsx:1235-1236. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No for the dead links; the README's general 'none is a built or running app' does not cover it.. WHY THIS TIER: The surfaces work and the README says none is a built or running app, so this is not a pretending surface. But the reader is shown working-looking 'Web app' / 'Phone app' links and an unqualified 'offline' chip, and nothing says the links only resolve in a downloaded copy or that offline needs hosting - a shortfall the surface does not state, tier 2. It is not tier 1 because 'offline_capable' is true of the artefact once hosted. REFUTER: Reproduced by curl. GET /vsb/{id}/website/page/index is 200 and its nav carries href='../webapp/index.html' and '../mobile/index.html'; the four resolved targets ({id}/website/webapp/index.html, {id}/website/mobile/index.html, {id}/mobile/web/index.html, {id}/webapp/web/index.html) all return 404. mobile/page/index is 200 but mobile/page/index.html is 404, and sw.js lists ASSETS ['./','index.html',...] with failures swallowed by .catch, so the offline fallback caches.match('index.html') has nothing in the preview (reasoned from the generated file, not observed in a browser). The POST /mobile note does say 'offline-capable when hosted ... not deployed/hosted' (vsb.py:1300-1302), but GenesisJourney.tsx:1234-1236 renders only pwa.kind plus bare 'installable' / 'offline' chips; I found no render of pwa.note on that page. Tier 2 rather than 3: the qualifier exists in the API body but not at the page chip, and nothing marks the cross-links as download-only. Tier 2 rather than 1: offline_capable is true of the artefact once hosted, and the links are correct inside the zip. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Rewrite cross-surface hrefs when serving through the preview routes (or serve the repo tree under one base path), accept 'index.html' in the page routes, and label the chip 'offline when hosted'.

items.title: The Chief's unprompted directive takes an instruction written for one scope and lands it on the Workstation apex plan, recorded as 'executed' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5/§17.4 Mode 2: the Chief is the founder's twin acting faithfully in presence and absence, 'built from the Owner's record'; §15.6 never fabricate. OBSERVED: twin_directive_unprompted() calls founder_model() with NO scope, so it reads instruction rows across every scope, takes the latest one verbatim and issues it through chief_instruct(scope='workstation'). Live on this server: my instruction 'Prioritise signing hospital trusts over opening a second kitchen' was written to scope r3audit at 20:32:37; at 20:38:25 a beat issued dir-3d2f3406 unprompted for scope 'workstation' and the Workstation plan now carries objective obj-172aab4b with that title, directive_id dir-3d2f3406, source 'chief_instruct_fallback'. The stored twin record says executed: True, cascaded_to_ceo: True and 'It ran through the gaas.v5 apex gate and was cascaded to the AI CEO, so it EXECUTES rather than being filed' - but on the floor the only thing that happened is the fallback appending the instruction itself as one objective row (the CEO plan was a frame with an empty subject). With auth on, the same unscoped read would lift another founder's VSB instruction into the apex plan as 'the Owner's own latest input'. The same unscoped root shows in GET /board/chief/model?scope=<vsb>: decisions are never scoped, so a new VSB's Chief reported 'chief carrying your record ... 1 decision(s) the Owner made' from an apex ratification unrelated to it. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/board.py:497 (m = founder_model()), :525 (_latest from instructions.recent[-1]), :536-537 (chief_instruct(... scope=scope ...) with scope='workstation' from heartbeat.py:670), :548 executed = bool(objectives_added), :554-556 basis text, :791-798 fallback objective. GET /api/v1/board/status recent_directives rows dir-c8512f16 (scope r3audit) and dir-3d2f3406 (unprompted, scope workstation, kind twin_directive_unprompted, executed True); GET /api/v1/business-plan objectives -> obj-172aab4b. I did not switch auto_align on; heartbeat/status now reads auto_align False with last_twin_directive 'nothing_new', so it was on at 20:38. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The record's instruction_source says it is the twin restating the Owner's latest input, but nothing says the input came from a different scope, and 'executed' is asserted.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader of the Workstation Business Plan page is shown the objective 'Prioritise signing hospital trusts over opening a second kitchen · ⌘ dir-3d2f3406' with the tooltip 'Landed by a Chief/Board directive', and the stored record states 'executed: true ... it EXECUTES rather than being filed'. Both are assertions of an outcome that did not occur as stated (the Owner never gave that instruction to this scope; nothing executed beyond a fallback row), so this is tier 1 rather than a tier-2 silent shortfall. REFUTER: Reproduced from code and the live store. twin_directive_unprompted() calls founder_model() with no scope (board.py:497), takes instructions.recent[-1] and issues it via chief_instruct(scope='workstation') (heartbeat.py passes 'workstation'). Live: dir-c8512f16 has business_plan_scope r3audit; dir-3d2f3406 (unprompted True) has business_plan_scope workstation with the same sentence, and the Workstation plan carries obj-172aab4b with that title, directive_id dir-3d2f3406, source chief_instruct_fallback. The twin record stores executed True / cascaded_to_ceo True and a basis saying it 'EXECUTES rather than being filed'. Tier 1 rather than 2: the apex plan page shows an objective with the tooltip 'Landed by a Chief/Board directive' that the Owner gave to a different scope, and the record asserts execution when only the fallback echo row landed - an assertion, not an omission. Caveats: the 'with auth on another founder's instruction' consequence is inference I did not execute, and I did not re-test the unscoped-decisions claim on GET /board/chief/model. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Pass the scope into founder_model(scope) inside twin_directive_unprompted and act only on instructions whose business_plan_scope equals it; scope _owner_decisions by vsb_id the same way; derive 'executed' from parsed (non-fallback) objectives and say 'filed as one fallback objective' when source is chief_instruct_fallback.

items.title: The Board Pack chip counts layers that hold content as 'empty' because the present-flag assignment fell out of its loop — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.3 Board Pack (on-demand): assembled fresh from live data, DCS-registered, each layer stating what it holds. OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/vsb/{id}/board-pack returned layers_present ['strategic'] while layers_state said constitutional: content and operational: content (the constitutional layer carried a mission and vision, the operational layer a stage and status). The Genesis page renders layers_present as the sky chip, then 'constitutional: content', 'operational: content' in emerald, then a chip computed as 4 - layers_present.length: '3 empty', whose tooltip lists constitutional and operational as empty. After a cadence refresh existed the second pack returned ['action_plan','operational','strategic'] - constitutional still absent, so '1 empty' beside 'constitutional: content'. Cause: the two setdefault('present', True)/('basis', ...) lines that belong to the `for _k in ('constitutional','operational')` loop now sit inside the later `if _qv638 and _cv584 ...` vision-note block, so they run only when a vision note fires and only for the loop's last value (operational); constitutional is never marked present. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/vsb.py:1592-1593 (loop body is now only setdefault('holds')), :1606-1613 (present/basis setdefault indented under the vision_note if), :1614 layers_present. apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/synthesis/GenesisJourney.tsx:1268-1297 (pack-layers-present, pack-layer-*, pack-layers-empty). Executed twice on vsb-156cad807d (v1: present ['strategic']; v2: constitutional 'present' key absent). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No - the page contradicts itself; a reader cannot tell which chip is right.. WHY THIS TIER: The page shows the figure '3 EMPTY' (then '1 EMPTY') on the same row as 'CONSTITUTIONAL: CONTENT' and 'OPERATIONAL: CONTENT'. A count of empty layers that includes layers the pack itself says hold content is a fabricated figure on a reached surface, not an omission - tier 1, not 2. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/vsb/vsb-156cad807d/board-pack returned layers_present ['action_plan','operational','strategic'] while layers_state.constitutional is {holds: 'content', basis: None}; the constitutional layer has no 'present' key. Code confirms the cause: the two setdefault('present'/'basis') lines sit inside the vision_note `if` (vsb.py:1606-1613) and use the leaked loop variable _k = 'operational', so constitutional is never marked. GenesisJourney.tsx:1291-1296 renders (4 - layers_present.length) + ' empty' with a tooltip listing 'constitutional: empty' beside the emerald 'constitutional: content' chip. I saw only the '1 empty' state (a refresh already existed); the '3 empty' state follows from the code when no vision note fires. Tier 1 rather than 2: '1 EMPTY' is a count the pack's own state contradicts - a wrong figure on a reached page, not a silent gap. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Move the two setdefault lines (present, basis) back inside the `for _k in ('constitutional','operational')` loop at vsb.py:1592, and add a guard that asserts layers_present == every layer whose holds == 'content'.

items.title: The AI CEO chat's floor answer reports the platform's own system prompt as the Subject and as 'the request's most frequent terms' — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5 AI CEO receives direction and answers for the organisation; §15.6 honesty over polish - a floor-served surface must disclose itself truthfully. OBSERVED: POST /api/v138/ceo/chat with 'What are our top three priorities this quarter and how is the plan progressing?' streamed: 'Subject: You are the AI CEO of this Workstation IDBO enterprise. You report to the Board, chaired by the Chief — the Owner's standing charter and las (domain: WITHHELD...)' and 'Structured frame over the terms most frequent in the request (a term count, not an analysis): workstation idbo · standing charter · idbo enterprise · owner standing · board chaired · not set'. None of those words were in the question; they are the handler's wrapper prompt. The same happened for scope=<vsb> (and it calls the VSB 'this Workstation IDBO enterprise'). The handler's own comment says the `Question:` label was added so the terms come from the user's question - measured, they do not. The same wrapper-as-request shape appears in POST /business-plan/generate's stored chief_draft ('draft nothing · not recorded · claims know') and in the Chief directive frame (charter terms), the latter covered by directive_reason. EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v138/ceo/chat twice (scope workstation, scope vsb-156cad807d); terminal frame served_by 'native'. agentic_core/api/v138/ceo.py:536-547 (prompt, 'Question:' label and comment). apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/CEOChat.tsx:285-292 renders m.content verbatim with the badge 'structured floor — not model analysis'. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly - the floor badge is shown, but nothing says the frame was computed over the platform's wrapper rather than the question.. WHY THIS TIER: The floor IS disclosed (amber 'structured floor — not model analysis'), so 'no model ran' is not the defect. The defect is the sentence the reader is shown: 'the terms most frequent in the request' followed by terms they never typed, and a 'Subject:' that is the platform's instruction to itself. That is an untrue statement about the user's own input, which is tier 1; an answer that merely said nothing about the question would have been tier 3. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution with a different question ('Which supplier contracts expire before December and what should we renegotiate?'). The stream returned 'Subject: You are the AI CEO of this Workstation IDBO enterprise...' and 'Structured frame over the terms most frequent in the request (a term count, not an analysis): workstation idbo, standing charter, idbo enterprise, owner standing, board chaired, not set'. None of my words appear; the terminal frame says served_by native. The handler's comment at ceo.py:543-545 claims the Question label makes the terms come from the user's question, which the output disproves. Tier 1 rather than 3: the floor is disclosed, but the sentence 'the terms most frequent in the request' followed by the platform's own wrapper is an untrue statement about the user's input. Not tier 2 because it is an assertion, not a silence. I tested scope workstation only, not the VSB scope. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Make the CEO stream path extract the subject and term list from the labelled `Question:` field only (as the non-stream path does for Topic), and when it cannot, emit the existing WITHHELD line instead of counting the wrapper; add a guard that asserts no listed term is absent from the user's message.

items.title: The living cadence reports an elapsed time one hour too long during daylight-saving time ('0.04 day(s) since the last refresh' one second after refreshing) — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.3: the Strategic layer refreshes quarterly + on market signal, the Action Plan weekly + on KPI trigger, with honest cadence state. OBSERVED: The cadence itself is real and reached: GET /api/v1/organism/cadence reports each layer's last refresh, due state and history; POST .../refresh refreshes when due, refuses when not, and fires on a caller-supplied signal; the heartbeat runs the step each beat (last_beat.ran true, beat 4, 'nothing was due'); refreshes are deterministic-floor derivations and say so; 'nothing in this platform observes markets or KPIs' is stated at the surface. The defect: _parse_stamp converts the stored UTC stamp with time.mktime(strptime(...)) - time.timezone, which is wrong by the DST offset. POST refresh at 20:35:37Z followed one second later by a second POST returned elapsed_seconds 3601.193 and reason 'not due: 0.04 day(s) since the last refresh'. The CadencePanel on the Business Plan page prints that reason verbatim. Layers will also come due one hour early for half the year. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/organism/cadence.py:85. Executed POST /api/v1/organism/cadence/refresh?layer=strategic&scope=r3audit twice (20:35:37Z then +1s -> elapsed 3601.193); GET /api/v1/organism/cadence for workstation showed elapsed 3655 ~55s after its 20:31:00Z refresh. apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/CadencePanel.tsx:27 renders l.due.reason. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown a figure - 'not due: 0.04 day(s) since the last refresh' - that is false by a constant hour. It is small, but it is a wrong number asserted on a reached surface rather than a missing one, so tier 1; the surrounding shortfalls (floor-derived content, no observed signals) are stated and would be tier 3 on their own. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/organism/cadence/refresh?layer=strategic&scope=r3refute&signal=... refreshed at 2026-10-09T20:43:36Z; an immediate second POST without a signal returned elapsed_seconds 3600.895 and 'not due: 0.04 day(s) since the last refresh'. Cause as stated: cadence.py:85 uses time.mktime(strptime(...)) - time.timezone, which ignores the DST offset. CadencePanel.tsx:26 prints due.reason verbatim on the Business Plan page. The rest of the cadence surface behaved honestly (refuses when not due, says no signal is observed). Tier 1 by the definition, though the smallest of the tier-1 rows: a figure shown to the reader is wrong by a constant hour. It is not tier 2 because a number is asserted, and not tier 3 because nothing states the offset. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Replace the parse with calendar.timegm(time.strptime(s, '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')) and add a test that drives a stamp one second old and asserts elapsed < 5 under a DST timezone.

items.title: The Swarm tab hides a Mode 3 review-gate refusal and silently runs the mission through the ungated delegate route instead — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.4 Mode 3: human review gates; every lifecycle mover (orchestrate, cascade, evolve, ship...) refuses with 409 while a gated stage is pending or rejected. OBSERVED: Backend holds: with 'build' pending on vsb-156cad807d, POST /swarm/cascade (scope=vsb), /repo/ship, /evolve, /business-plan/objective/{oid}/orchestrate and /board-pack all returned 409 naming the gate and how to clear it. But SwarmIntelligence.delegate() treats ANY non-ok cascade response as a cue to call POST /api/v1/swarm/delegate with only {task} (no scope, no gate) and prints that run's JSON in the green output box; the 409 body is never read or shown. I executed both calls in sequence: cascade 409, delegate 200 with a completed 2-agent run for the same mission. The run then appears under 'Recent Swarm Runs'. EVIDENCE: apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/organism/SwarmIntelligence.tsx:168-176. Executed POST /api/v1/swarm/cascade (409, mover 'cascade', gate 'build') then POST /api/v1/swarm/delegate (200, run 865469ba4d). GenesisJourney.tsx:1359 tells the user a gate 'blocks ... cascades ... with a 409 that names the gate'. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown a completed swarm run and never the sentence 'review gate blocks progress — a human review is pending (Mode 3); cascade refused'. Nothing on screen asserts the cascade succeeded (the output is visibly a delegate JSON), so it is not a tier-1 false statement; but the refusal - the whole point of the gate - is invisible at this surface, which is tier 2 rather than a disclosed tier-3 gap. Reasoned from source: I could not drive the browser. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution plus source reading. With a 'launch' gate pending on vsb-156cad807d, POST /api/v1/swarm/cascade (scope = the VSB) returned 409 naming the gate and the clearing call; POST /api/v1/swarm/delegate with only {task} returned 200 with run 0dde33c3b5 (CFO, CTO). SwarmIntelligence.tsx:168-176 takes any non-ok cascade response straight to that delegate call and prints its JSON; the 409 body is never read. Tier 2 rather than 1: no sentence on screen says the cascade ran or the gate passed - the output is visibly a delegate run - but the refusal is invisible and the mission runs ungated. Not tier 3 because nothing at this surface states it. The UI half is reasoned from source; I did not drive a browser. I cleared the gate afterwards (launch approved). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: On !response.ok read the body and render detail.error / clear_by as the result; drop the delegate fallback (or keep it only for a 404/405), never for a 409.

items.title: The Board page promises an instruction is 'faithfully interpreted' and 'delegated to the AI CEO', and the delegated plan and the objective chip carry no statement that neither read the instruction — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R3)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R3), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §5: the Chief interprets the founder's instruction and delivers it via Strategy; the Board delivers via action planning with timelines and resourced tasks; the AI CEO receives the action plan. OBSERVED: POST /board/chief/instruct on the floor returns a Chief directive framed over the platform's charter sentence (not the instruction) - this part IS disclosed: directive_reason says 'it did NOT read your instruction' and the page prints it in amber above the directive, with the Chief's role/record standing. The CEO half is not: ceo_action_plan is a frame over an EMPTY subject ('Native structured frame for 'Owner Intent' over: (domain: WITHHELD...) - (no salient terms extracted)') shown under the card title 'AI CEO Action Plan (delegated)' with no reason line, and the highlighted chip '1 objective → living plan' is the fallback that copies the instruction itself in as an objective with KPI '(KPI to be set by the Board)' - not something the CEO's plan produced. Static copy on the card reads 'Faithfully interpreted → board directive → delegated to the AI CEO' and the button reads 'Chief deliberating…'. The response's delegation_chain honestly reads Chief → AI CEO (the Board of Directors does not run on this path). EVIDENCE: Executed POST /api/v1/board/chief/instruct (dir-c8512f16: objectives_added 1, source chief_instruct_fallback; ai_provenance native x2). agentic_core/api/board.py:761-771, :791-798, :837-841 (reason exists for the Chief only). apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/BoardOfDirectors.tsx:289, :306, :337-341, :352, :358-361. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly - for the Chief directive yes, for the CEO action plan and the objective chip no.. WHY THIS TIER: The surface does state the floor (amber provenance badge, the Chief's directive_reason), so the Chief half is tier 3. But for the CEO plan the reader is shown 'AI CEO Action Plan (delegated)' and '1 OBJECTIVE → LIVING PLAN' with nothing saying the plan read no directive and the objective is their own sentence echoed back. That is a shortfall the surface does not state (tier 2); it stops short of tier 1 because one objective really was added and the plan text carries the floor marker. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /api/v1/board/chief/instruct (scope r3refute) returned directive_reason for the Chief only; ceo_action_plan is a frame over an empty subject ('Native structured frame for 'Owner Intent' over: (domain: WITHHELD...) - (no salient terms extracted)'); objectives_added 1 is obj-7ad4ddd9, my own sentence with KPI '(KPI to be set by the Board)' and source chief_instruct_fallback; delegation_chain ['Chief','AI CEO']. BoardOfDirectors.tsx:289 prints 'Faithfully interpreted → board directive → delegated to the AI CEO', :306 'Chief deliberating…', :337-341 the '1 objective → living plan' chip with no origin, and :358-361 the CEO plan with no reason line. Tier 2 is borderline with 3: the amber provenance badge covers both calls and the plan text labels itself a native frame, so the floor is stated. What is not stated is that the objective is the instruction echoed back and not a product of the CEO's plan, which is why it stays at 2. Not tier 1: one objective really was added and the count is true. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Return a ceo_plan_reason and an objectives_source ('fallback: your instruction recorded as one objective; the CEO plan produced none') and render both; change the static subtitle to describe what runs ('recorded → Chief directive → AI CEO plan; each says what composed it').

items.title: GET /api/v1/ai/quotas reports an external-first provider chain with "active: openai" while the native floor is the only resource that can serve — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6 / §15.1: in-house-first, external providers are optional accelerants and never dependencies; the surface must say honestly what serves. OBSERVED: The handler hardcodes ollama available=True, derives 'active' from whether an API key env var exists (ignoring AI_ALLOW_EXTERNAL and AI_DISABLE_LOCAL), and names the legacy external-first chain the vision calls the gap to close. Its docstring calls this the "real gateway provider chain". EVIDENCE: curl GET /api/v1/ai/quotas -> {"providers":[{anthropic, claude-opus-4-8, available:false},{openai, available:true},{ollama, available:true}],"chain":"claude → openai → ollama","active":"openai"}. Handler: agentic_core/api/integration_surface.py lines 49-63. Contrast: GET /api/v1/native-ai/status. grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src finds no consumer of ai/quotas. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. Nothing in the response says it is legacy or that external providers are disabled.. WHY THIS TIER: The response body states "chain": "claude → openai → ollama", "active": "openai", ollama "available": true and anthropic model "claude-opus-4-8". On the same backend /native-ai/status says external_allowed false, selection_order ["native"], ollama available false, openai available false, and the gateway's Claude model is claude-sonnet-4-6. It is an asserted outcome, not an omission, so it is tier 1 rather than 2. No page calls the route, so its reached form is the response body. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution and by reading the handler. The body asserts a chain and an active provider that contradict /native-ai/status on the same backend. Tier 1 rather than 2 because 'active: openai' and ollama 'available: true' are positive assertions, not blanks; not tier 3 because nothing in the body marks it legacy. Reach is the response body only: grep of apps/workstation-superapp/src finds no consumer of ai/quotas. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Serve this route from the native model registry (the same data as /native-ai/status), or retire it.

items.title: Resource Fabric tells the user a composition was "Modelled & simulated before commit" when nothing is simulated — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §7: users compose and reconfigure resources "with the platform modelling and simulating the configuration before commit". OBSERVED: The modelling half is real static analysis: pipeline names, capability union, usage-area incompatibilities, unset params, and a homeostasis capacity projection. The 'simulation' key holds a QMS gate run over a one-sentence template built from the resource names (served_by "template", not_assessable true, 0 of 16 bar criteria measured). No resource is executed or simulated. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/resources/compose/simulate with 7 resources returned simulation.quality.served_by "template", qms_gate_passed null, bar_measured.summary "0 measured · 0 attested · 2 screen-only · 14 not measured (of 16)". Code: agentic_core/api/resource_fabric.py _simulate_configuration (lines 1941-1965) builds plan_text and calls assure_delivery. UI (read from source, not driven): ResourceFabric.tsx lines 360, 471, 517. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly. The gate's abstention is shown; that the 'simulation' is a gate over a template sentence is not.. WHY THIS TIER: The page heading reads "Modelled & simulated before commit" and the API note reads "Modelled + simulated before commit (§7) — not saved." No run, dry-run or simulation of the pipeline happens. That asserts an outcome the platform did not produce, so tier 1 rather than 2. The adjacent chip ("gate could not assess — commit at your judgement") discloses that the gate abstained, not that no simulation exists. REFUTER: Reproduced. The modelling half is real static analysis; the 'simulation' is assure_delivery run over a one-sentence template built from resource names. Tier 1 rather than 2 because the page heading and the API note positively say 'simulated before commit' when no resource is run or dry-run. Not tier 3 because the adjacent chip discloses only that the gate abstained, not that there is no simulation. UI read from source, not driven. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Rename the heading, button and note to "Modelled before commit", or build a real dry run of each handler.

items.title: A composed Digital Twin & Simulator is recorded as having run /api/v1/twin/simulate and "its engine" when a single persona prompt ran — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §7 (W446 rule): resources are "never a prompt approximation of a real engine" and "every composed resource runs its REAL engine"; §17.2 calls the Musculoskeletal facilities and digital twin REAL and the modelling organ that ranking and twin pre-validation rely on. OBSERVED: The fabric handler for digital_twin calls orchestrator.complete with "You are a digital-twin simulator… Forward-simulate the scenario" and labels the result ran=/api/v1/twin/simulate. The real /twin/simulate route needs an existing model_id and is itself one prompt ("You are a simulation engineer…"). The Digital Twins page says its figure is a projection, "not a simulation". This handler also bypasses the gateway's per-call gate. The Forge's seven facilities are persona prompts too, but that page says so. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/resources/compositions/{cid}/run -> real_resource_runs[digital_twin] = {kind: facility_run, outcome_phrase: "ran its engine and produced this output", endpoint: /api/v1/twin/simulate, duration_ms: 1}, output "_Acting as: digital-twin simulator._ … Native structured frame for 'State Trajectory' over: (domain: WITHHELD…)". GET /api/v1/resources/compositions/runs stores the same endpoint and outcome. Code: resource_fabric.py lines 997-1010 and 169-173; digital_twin.py lines 143-194. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No on the fabric card and run row. Yes for floor provenance in the output text, and on the separate Digital Twins and Forge pages.. WHY THIS TIER: The run row and the durable run record state endpoint "/api/v1/twin/simulate", kind "facility_run", outcome_phrase "ran its engine and produced this output"; the fabric card says "Forward-simulates a system under a scenario". That route was not invoked and no simulator exists, so the record asserts something untrue: tier 1 rather than 2. In this environment the output text carries the floor banner, which limits how far a reader is misled; with a model serving, a written narrative would sit under the same label. REFUTER: Reproduced end to end: I composed a digital_twin composition, ran it, read the durable run row, then deleted the composition. The handler is a single orchestrator.complete persona prompt, yet the row and the stored record name the /twin/simulate route (never invoked; it needs a model_id) and say it 'ran its engine'. Tier 1 rather than 2 because the record asserts an outcome that did not happen, and the page renders both the endpoint and the 'ran an engine' count. The floor banner in the output text limits the harm in this environment but does not correct the label. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Label the row as a model-written scenario narrative with the true invocation (orchestrator.complete), and correct §7/§17.2 until a simulator exists.

items.title: A saved cascade silently drops each stage's requested model tier and its run reports requests_not_honoured: [] — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6/§7: cascades are user-reconfigurable, including which owned model tier serves each stage, with honest provenance of requested versus served. OBSERVED: SwarmStageSpec accepts 'model', but register_swarm rebuilds each stage as {role, instruction} only, so the choice is discarded at save for both /swarm/define and Genesis-registered cascades. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/resources/swarm/define with stages[0].model="local" -> stored stages [{role, instruction}]. POST /api/v1/resources/swarm/run {swarm_id} -> requests_not_honoured: []. POST /api/v1/resources/swarm/run with inline stages -> requests_not_honoured: [{step:1, requested:"local", served_by:"native"}]. Code: resource_fabric.py line 1558 versus lines 1585-1592. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: I saved a cascade with stage 1 model "local". The stored stage came back without the field and the run returned "requests_not_honoured": [] with no requested_model in the trace. The same stage run ad hoc returned requests_not_honoured [{step 1, requested local, served_by native}]. An empty list asserts nothing went unhonoured, which is untrue for the saved run, so tier 1 rather than an omission. Reach is API and stored record only: the designer page has no per-stage model control. REFUTER: Reproduced exactly. The request schema accepts 'model' and returns 200, register_swarm stores only role and instruction, and the saved run then returns an explicit empty requests_not_honoured while the same stages run inline list the unhonoured request. I considered tier 2, since the define response's missing field is an omission, but the run's explicitly named empty list is an assertion that nothing went unhonoured, which is untrue of what the caller saved; so tier 1. Reach is API and stored record only. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Carry 'model' through register_swarm (and the update path if it has the same rebuild), and add a per-stage model selector to the designer.

items.title: The ensemble route's governance checkpoint certifies an empty string as checked and compliant, under a method string naming a consensus that did not happen — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §6 owned orchestration with honest provenance; §11/§15.6 every completion carries a truthful governance checkpoint. OBSERVED: native_ensemble passes (synthesis or {}).output or "" to console_post_gate. In this environment the ensemble always has exactly one member (native), so every call takes this path. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/native-ai/ensemble -> models_run ["native"], synthesis null, method "parallel ensemble across owned models → consensus synthesis", governance_checkpoint.post_checked true. items.title: The organism cadence overstates time since last refresh by one hour under daylight-saving time — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R4), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.2/§17.3: circadian operation and a cadence that reports truthfully when each layer was refreshed and when it is due. OBSERVED: cadence.py parses the UTC stamp with time.mktime(...) - time.timezone, which ignores DST; the host is on BST (UTC+1). The orchestrator's own probation code documents this trap and uses calendar.timegm. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/organism/cadence (elapsed_seconds 3893.305, period_seconds 604800); `date -u` 20:36 versus local 21:36; agentic_core/organism/cadence.py line 85. A second mktime use is at agentic_core/api/organism_status.py line 80 (not exercised). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: GET /organism/cadence showed last_refresh_at 20:31:00Z with "elapsed_seconds": 3893.3 and "0.05 day(s) since the last refresh" when read at about 20:35:51Z; true elapsed was about 291 s. It is a wrong figure on a reached surface, so tier 1, but the practical effect is a refresh falling due one hour early against a weekly or quarterly period. REFUTER: Reproduced: the reported elapsed time is exactly 3600 s more than the true figure. It is a wrong figure on a surface a person reaches (CadencePanel.tsx calls the route), so tier 1 by definition rather than 2. It is the least consequential tier 1 here: against weekly and quarterly periods it makes a refresh due one hour early, and only while the host is on daylight-saving time. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Use calendar.timegm(time.strptime(...)) in both places.

items.title: The avatar labels a floor-served reply "grounded in your enterprise" although the reply used none of the enterprise's state — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §9: an enterprise-aware avatar; grounding is honesty-bound (never a fabricated description). OBSERVED: POST /api/v1/avatar/chat with vsb_id and the question "What is the status of my enterprise and what should I do next?" returned served_by native, grounded_in "vsb-156cad807d", and a body that is the floor's frame: a term list drawn partly from the entity's mission words, with no status, stage, economy or compliance line. The backend sets grounded_in whenever the grounding block was BUILT into the prompt, not when it was used. ConversationPanel renders the label whenever grounded_in is set, with no floor condition. Reasoned from source for the rendering; the API behaviour was executed. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/avatars/api.py:637-639 (`grounded_in=(request.vsb_id if grounding else None)`); apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/avatar/ConversationPanel.tsx data-testid="avatar-grounded-in"; live response grounded_in='vsb-156cad807d', served_by='native'. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The floor badge and the reply's own frame wording are shown, but the grounding label is affirmative and unqualified.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown "grounded in your enterprise vsb-156cad807d (your most recently updated one)" under a reply that is a term count and answers nothing about that enterprise. That is a field asserting an outcome the platform did not produce, not an omission, so it is tier 1 rather than 2. The same panel says "profile: not usable by the floor" for the identical situation with the saved profile, so the reader has no cue to discount the grounding label. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution: POST /api/v1/avatar/chat with vsb_id vsb-156cad807d returned served_by native, grounded_in 'vsb-156cad807d', and a body with no status, stage, economy or compliance line. agentic_core/avatars/api.py:639 sets grounded_in whenever the grounding block built; ConversationPanel.tsx:129-132 renders 'grounded in your enterprise {id} (your most recently updated one)' with no floor condition, while the profile label at :139-143 is floor-conditioned. Re-tiered 1 -> 2 because the assessor's title ('used none of the enterprise's state') is not what I observed: the floor's term list was drawn from the entity's records ('night-shift hospital', 'get halal-certified', 'hospital workers', 'workers leeds'), and the frame itself says the fields can hold 'the entity's own records' and that it is 'not an analysis of the subject'. So the label is narrowly true (the grounding block was built and its words did reach the reply) and the reply states its own nature; what is missing is the qualifier that the floor only counted words from the grounding and did not read the enterprise's status. That is a shortfall the label does not state (tier 2), not a field asserting an outcome that did not occur (tier 1). Not tier 3, because the label itself carries no qualification and the same panel does qualify the profile case. Rendering was reasoned from source. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: When served_by is native, either return grounded_in null with a basis, or render "your enterprise's record reached the prompt, but the floor does not read it" — the same treatment profile_state 'not_usable_by_floor' already gets.

items.title: Floor-served domain tools still print disclaimers saying the output is AI-generated, reasoned or AI-interpreted — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15 principle 6: honesty over polish, never fabricate, label simulation. §9: when the serving resource cannot honour the request, the answer says so. OBSERVED: Executed with the floor serving: /care/care-plan, /law/generate, /employment/salary-negotiation, /education/feedback, /religion/halal-review and /care/risk-assess all return a static disclaimer written for model output. /law/research and /law/analyse swap theirs for a floor-specific one, so the fix exists and was applied to two routes only. The NDA "document" from /law/generate is a four-heading frame that names no party, yet carries the solicitor-review disclaimer and is saved to My Work with it. For dementia_care, mental_health and safeguarding, score.available is false with note "no published arithmetic exists", while score.basis and the disclaimer both say it was computed from the published table. DomainTool renders result.disclaimer verbatim and appends it to every copy, download and saved record. EVIDENCE: Live responses (all served_by native). agentic_core/api/law.py:31-32, 207, 255 (floor swap) versus :309 (no swap); agentic_core/api/care.py:98, 164, 215; agentic_core/api/employment.py:234; apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/DomainTool.tsx withDisclosures and the `result.disclaimer` paragraph. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly. The floor note and badge are rendered above the text; the disclaimer below contradicts them.. WHY THIS TIER: Directly under an amber note saying "Composed by the native floor, not by a model", the reader is shown "This care plan is AI-generated as a planning aid only", "This document is AI-generated ... must be reviewed by a qualified solicitor before use", "Reasoned negotiation guidance, not live salary data", "the narrative is an AI interpretation aid only", and "The score is computed in-house from the published table" on tools that have no score. Each is an untrue sentence on the result card, so tier 1 rather than 2. Severity is held at medium because the true statement sits beside it. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution with served_by native on each: /care/care-plan returns 'This care plan is AI-generated as a planning aid only'; /law/generate (template nda) returns a floor frame that says 'The request carries no labelled subject' with the terms WITHHELD, under 'This document is AI-generated ... must be reviewed by a qualified solicitor'; /employment/salary-negotiation returns 'Reasoned negotiation guidance'; /law/research carries the floor-specific disclaimer, so the fix exists on that route and not the others. /care/risk-assess with tool dementia_care, mental_health and safeguarding each returned score.available false, note 'no published arithmetic exists for this tool', alongside score.basis 'computed in-house from the published table' and a disclaimer opening 'The score is computed in-house from the published table'. DomainTool.tsx:373 renders result.disclaimer verbatim. Tier 1 stands: these are affirmative untrue sentences on the result (a score said to be computed where the same record says none exists; floor output called AI-generated and reasoned), not omissions. It is not tier 2 or 3 because the true floor note beside them does not withdraw the false sentence - the reader is given two contradictory statements, and the disclaimer is the one that travels as the document's own legal/clinical caveat. I did not call /education/feedback or /religion/halal-review; the finding holds without them. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Apply law.py's `_FLOOR_X if provenance.get('floor_note') else ...` pattern to every domain route's disclaimer, and drop score.basis and the score sentence when score.available is false.

items.title: The floor lists the platform's own prompt wording as "the request's most frequent terms" — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §15 principle 6 (never fabricate). §3A: tools work on the user's own input. A third avatar turn asking "What is in this image?" listed "avatar conversation · conversation across · across every" (from the platform's own domain label) and "empiezo una · una empresa" (the previous turn) as the request's terms. The other frame variant does say "these are not necessarily your words", so the defect is in the 'Native structured frame' variant. EVIDENCE: Live responses from /api/v1/employment/interview-prep and /api/v1/avatar/chat (third turn of one session). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No for this variant. The floor note says terms are "taken from your input", which reinforces the wrong attribution.. WHY THIS TIER: The reader is shown "Native structured frame for 'Likely Questions' over: Action-Result scaffold) ... The list below is the request's most frequent terms" followed by "action-result scaffold". The user typed only "Nurse". The sentence asserts the terms are the request's, and they are the platform's wrapper, so it is an untrue statement rather than an unlabelled shortfall. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution: POST /api/v1/employment/interview-prep {target_role: Nurse} returned, in all five sections, "Native structured frame for '<heading>' over: Action-Result scaffold) (domain: employment). The list below is the request's most frequent terms" followed by '- action-result scaffold' and '- nurse'. I did not reproduce the three-turn avatar example or the empty-subject cases; the /law/generate call did show the separate, honest 'no labelled subject / WITHHELD' variant, so the empty-subject part may be narrower than stated. items.title: Choosing the Developing realm adds an "implementation" stage to a Genesis journey, attributed to the user's text — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R5)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.1: realm is one axis of the grid; taxonomy.py states realm changes depth and register, "not the structure". OBSERVED: Two POST /api/v1/genesis/journey calls with an identical problem ("Rural carers in Kashmir lack respite support and training"), domain care, product factory. With realm=developing, derived_stages contains implementation matched ['develop'], and an extra stage body is composed. With realm=learning, derived_stages is {}. The concept's first line is the realm note; the rest of the concept does not contain 'develop'. EVIDENCE: agentic_core/api/genesis.py:686-699 (`_derived_branches(f"{req.problem} {concept}")`); agentic_core/ai/native/orchestrator.py:217-245 (keyword 'develop'); the two live journey responses. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No. The basis attributes the match to the text.. WHY THIS TIER: The response states `derived_stages.implementation.basis: "derived from the text: it contains 'develop'"` and `derived_stages_basis: "selected from the problem and the concept"`. The only place 'develop' occurs is the platform's own preamble, "Composed for the Developing realm". The stated basis is therefore untrue, which is tier 1. Severity is low because the Genesis page does not render derived_stages, so the reached form is the response body and the stored journey. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution: two POST /api/v1/genesis/journey calls with the identical problem, domain care, product factory. realm=developing gave derived_stages.implementation matched ['develop'], basis "derived from the text: it contains 'develop'"; realm=learning gave {}. In the developing response the only occurrence of 'develop' in phase_1_conceptualisation is the platform's own preamble 'Composed for the Developing realm'. genesis.py:689 feeds problem + concept to derived_branches. Re-tiered 1 -> 2: the statements shown are literally true. The basis says the text contains 'develop' (it does - the concept does), and derived_stages_basis says the stages are 'selected from the problem and the concept by the same keyword rules', which is exactly the mechanism; neither sentence says the user wrote the word. The defect is that the realm choice silently changes the journey's structure through the platform's own preamble (contrary to taxonomy.py's 'not the structure'), and nothing tells the reader that the match came from the realm label - an unstated shortfall, tier 2. Not tier 1 because no shown sentence is false; not tier 3 because the response body and stored journey are the reached form and they do not disclose it. No frontend file references derived_stages (grep empty). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Strip the platform's realm preamble from the concept before keyword matching, or match on req.problem plus the concept body only.

items.title: The Religion hub's Certifications card says a record of completion "is issued instead", and nothing a learner can reach issues one — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R5)

A record of completion is issued instead, and it states that it is not a credential." The refusal half is a ratified boundary and correct. items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R5), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §3A offering 1: immediate, usable, in-house-AI-mediated tools in each of the six domains, of comparable scope. OBSERVED: All six domains execute and return 200. items.title: The organism's 'measured health' counts the immune term as measured even when it has observed nothing, and every health gate passes on it — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: profitability, satisfaction, founder-alignment and live compliance are 'continuously monitored'; §8 W482 rule: 'An engine computes or says it cannot … assessable: false with a reason, never an invented number'; §17.5 twin pre-validation before major change. OBSERVED: agentic_core/organism/biobus.py:363 sets immune_health 'measured': True unconditionally; _measured_only = immune alone when no circuit is tracked, so it is never None and mode_decidable is always true. Immune and self-healing are fed by the SAME call sites (ai/native/orchestrator.py _organism_report, ai/gateway.py), and with the floor serving, zero model calls are recorded — so 1.0 is the absence of observations. The same code treats that identical condition as 'defaulted to 1.0, not a measurement' for self-healing. Consumers: /organism/health-summary, /organism/status, CCA submit health_gate (verdict 'pass', decided_on composite_health_measured_only) and twin-prevalidate (verdict 'pass', source health_gate_default). The immune figure does become a real reading once compliance screens record fails (it later fell to 0.3 from 7 compliance_fail events), so the defect is specifically the no-observation state being certified as measured. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/organism/status at boot: composite_health_measured_only 1.0, immune events_in_window 0, self_healing overall_health null, mode_decidable true, health_summary 'measured health 100%'. POST /api/v1/cca/submit -> health_gate {measured_health 0.9, verdict 'pass'}. POST /api/v1/cca/{id}/twin-prevalidate -> verdict 'pass', method '…where too little is measured the gate returns not_assessable rather than a pass'. agentic_core/api/change_control.py:1388-1393 (not_assessable only when _m is None). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: Partly: the 40% weight and the defaulted/simulated terms are disclosed; that the 'measured' 40% itself rests on zero observations is not.. WHY THIS TIER: A reader is shown 'Organism nominal on what is measured — MAINTENANCE_FOCUS cycle, measured health 100%' and, on the Anatomy card, a large '100% measured only' with a chip 'immune_health 100% · w0.4 · measured'. On a fresh process no AI call had been carried (self-healing in the same payload says 'no circuit has carried a call yet — nothing measured, health unknown' and is labelled DEFAULTED), yet immune is hard-coded measured:true. That is an assertion of a measurement that was not taken, not an omission, so it is tier 1 rather than tier 2; and the twin gate's own sentence 'where too little is measured the gate returns not_assessable rather than a pass' is unreachable on the healthy path because of it. REFUTER: Mechanism reproduced in source and partly live; tier moved DOWN from 1 to 2. agentic_core/organism/biobus.py hard-codes immune_health measured:True, and _measured_only is immune-alone when no circuit is tracked, so it is never None on the normal path and the not_assessable branch at change_control.py:1389 is reachable only on the context-error fallback. agentic_core/organism/immune.py is a pure FAILURE counter over a 300s window (health = 1 - failures/10) with no count of observations, so a quiet process and a healthy one read identically. I could not reproduce the boot state itself (the window already held 7 failures: measured-only 0.3, DEGRADED), but I watched the same figure return to 0.8 / NOMINAL about two minutes later purely because failures aged out of the window. Why tier 2 and not 1: the reading is a real count, not an invented one - zero failures recorded IS what the instrument measured, and the surface shows its derivation ('health and threat are computed from N failure(s) in the window', the Anatomy immune card prints 'N errors in window', health_basis prints '40% measured'). Self-healing is a RATE over calls and is undefined at zero calls; immune is a count and is defined at zero, so the two are not the identical condition the assessor says. What the reader is NOT told is that the counter has no denominator and that failures silently expire after five minutes, so '100% measured' can mean 'nothing happened' - and every gate passes on it. That is an invisible shortfall (tier 2), not a disclosed one (tier 3). SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Have ImmuneSystem report an observation count (calls/screens seen in the window) and set immune 'measured' false, measured_only None, when it is zero — so the existing not_assessable branch becomes reachable and the summary says 'nothing measured yet'.
