items.title: The Economy page's default entity 'Workstation IDBO (apex)' is, by the API's own statement, an unregistered simulation — the page never says so, and its conjured WST funds registered entities — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §12: each VSB is an autonomous economic entity that self-manages its finances with double-entry books, Owner profit share and reinvestment; virtual money until the Owner directs real rails. OBSERVED: POST /economy/cycle on the default vsb_id returned registration 'UNREGISTERED' with the simulation basis, yet the same cycle (a) accrued 140 WST to the Owner and allowed a 40 WST payout, (b) 'funded' a venture position — '105.0 WST credited to the investee's intake this cycle' for registered entity vsb-1a0e91006d, whose later autonomous cycle distributed 226.8 WST — and (c) let 50 WST be transferred from its reserve fund to registered vsb-54c32fdef9, where it entered that entity's waterfall. So the statement that the entries 'belong to no entity that exists' is also not the whole truth: the simulated funds reach entities that do exist. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/economy/cycle {revenue:1000,costs:100} -> registration UNREGISTERED + venture_investment.positions[0].funding_state 'funded'; POST /api/v1/economy/transfer from workstation-idbo -> 200, receiver_pending_wst 50; next cycle on receiver: inter_vsb_received_wst 50. agentic_core/api/economy.py:310-317; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/enterprise/VSBEconomy.tsx:56,225-226,305 (no reference to registration/registration_basis anywhere in src). DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — disclosed in the API body only; the UI drops the field.. WHY THIS TIER: The API response says "'workstation-idbo' is not a registered living entity: this cycle is a SIMULATION run on request values, and the ledger entries and any Owner accrual it wrote belong to no entity that exists". The page (VSBEconomy.tsx) reads only d.cycle and d.governance, so that sentence is never rendered; the user sees an option labelled 'Workstation IDBO (apex)', an Owner balance of 140 WST and a board pack. Nothing shown is a false figure (the general 'virtual/simulated WST' banner is present), so it is not tier 1; the shortfall is real and invisible at the surface, so it is not tier 3. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. POST /economy/cycle on workstation-idbo returned registration 'UNREGISTERED' with the SIMULATION basis, and the same response carried owner_accrual 140 WST and a venture position for registered vsb-1a0e91006d with funding_state 'funded' ('21.08 WST credited to the investee's intake this cycle'). The transfer route accepts workstation-idbo as sender (overdraft refused only on balance: 'reserve fund holds 350.0 WST'). VSBEconomy.tsx defaults vsbId to 'workstation-idbo', labels it 'Workstation IDBO (apex)', and never reads registration or registration_basis (its only 'registration' strings concern the entity form). Tier 2 stands: every figure the page shows is labelled virtual/simulated WST, so no rendered figure is false (not tier 1); the specific fact that the default entity is unregistered and its funds reach real entities is stated only in the API body and dropped by the page (not tier 3). The API sentence 'belong to no entity that exists' is loose about the venture credit but is about the ledger entries and the accrual, so I do not raise it to tier 1. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Render registration_basis on the cycle card and beside the entity selector; and either register the apex as a living entity or refuse venture funding and outbound transfers from an unregistered id.

items.title: The Heartbeat page says the organism beats 'every ~60s' while the loop actually beats every 120s (up to 200s in rest phases) — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §8: circadian operation — the organism runs itself on a continuous heartbeat. OBSERVED: heartbeat.run() sleeps interval_seconds * (1 / phase_intensity); with intensity 0.5 that is 120s, with 0.3 it is 200s. /heartbeat/status publishes interval_seconds 60 with no effective-interval field, and the page presents it as the cadence. The 'Intensity 50%' tile is shown but nothing links it to the beat period. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/heartbeat/status recent[].at across six beats; agentic_core/organism/heartbeat.py:226,876-879; apps/workstation-superapp/src/pages/organism/HeartbeatMonitor.tsx:119. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: The page prints '{beats} beats · every ~{interval_seconds}s' = 'every ~60s'. Observed automatic beats were at 20:31:00, 20:33:01, 20:35:01, 20:37:01, 20:39:02, 20:41:02 — 120s apart. That is a stated figure that is untrue by a factor of two on a reached page, which is tier 1 by definition rather than an omission; the consequence is small, hence low severity. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. /heartbeat/status reports interval_seconds 60 and phase_intensity 0.5; automatic beats 10, 11, 12 were stamped 20:41:02, 20:43:02, 20:45:02 - 120s apart. heartbeat.py run() sleeps interval_seconds * (1/intensity). HeartbeatMonitor.tsx:119 prints '{beats} beats · every ~{interval_seconds}s' under 'Beating', i.e. 'every ~60s'. Tier 1 stands: it is a stated figure about the running system that is wrong by a factor of two on a reached page, not an omission (tier 2) and not disclosed anywhere (the Intensity tile is not linked to the period). Low severity - nobody is blocked by it. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Publish effective_interval_seconds (interval / intensity) from status and render that, or say 'base 60s, currently every ~120s (phase intensity 50%)'.

items.title: The living-cadence panel overstates time since the last refresh by exactly one hour during British Summer Time — MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M1 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.3/§17.5: the living business plan refreshes on cadence and is never more than five minutes stale; figures shown are measured. OBSERVED: cadence.py parses the stored UTC stamp with time.mktime(time.strptime(...)) - time.timezone. mktime applies local DST but time.timezone is the non-DST offset, so on a UK machine in BST every parsed stamp lands 3600s early and elapsed is overstated by an hour. Weekly and quarterly refreshes therefore fire one hour early for half the year. EVIDENCE: GET /api/v1/organism/cadence at 20:31:57Z -> layers.strategic.due {elapsed_seconds 3657.928, last_refresh_at '2026-10-09T20:31:00Z', reason 'not due: 0.04 day(s) since the last refresh…'}; agentic_core/organism/cadence.py:85; apps/workstation-superapp/src/components/CadencePanel.tsx renders due.reason. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No.. WHY THIS TIER: 57 seconds after a refresh stamped 2026-10-09T20:31:00Z the surface said 'not due: 0.04 day(s) since the last refresh' with elapsed_seconds 3657.9 — the whole displayed figure is the error (true value 0.00 days). A wrong computed figure rendered by CadencePanel is tier 1 rather than tier 2; the practical effect is only that elapsed-time triggers fire an hour early, hence low severity. REFUTER: Reproduced by execution. At 20:43:35Z, GET /organism/cadence returned last_refresh_at 2026-10-09T20:31:00Z with elapsed_seconds 4355.391 and reason 'not due: 0.05 day(s) since the last refresh'. True elapsed is 755s (0.01 day); the excess is exactly 3600s. cadence.py:85 uses time.mktime(...) - time.timezone, which ignores DST, on a machine in BST. CadencePanel.tsx:26 renders l.due?.reason verbatim. Tier 1 stands: a computed figure shown to the reader is wrong (not an omission), and nothing discloses it. Low severity: the practical effect is period triggers firing an hour early for half the year. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Parse with calendar.timegm(time.strptime(...)) (or datetime with tzinfo=UTC) and add a test that sets TZ to a DST zone.

items.title: The KPI gate stops a marketplace listing but not a ship or a repo download, while its own refusal says 'before listing or exporting' — MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6)
items.why: MILESTONE M2 ledger v14 (R6), measured 2026-10-09 against HEAD 375c5ffb on :8031, twelve agents. VISION CLAIM: §17.5 invariant 10: KPI gate before customer delivery (absolute). OBSERVED: kpi_release_gate is called from two sites, both in agentic_core/api/marketplace.py (listing create and from-entity). It is an honest presence test and it names what is missing — that half is delivered. Shipping the entity's repo, website, webapp and mobile surfaces and downloading the zip are ungated. EVIDENCE: POST /api/v1/marketplace/listings/from-entity/{vsb_id} -> 409 kpi_gate, 3 of 3 seeded objectives carry no KPI; POST /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/repo/ship -> 200 shipped:true on the same entity; GET /api/v1/vsb/{vsb_id}/repo/zip -> 200. grep kpi_release_gate: marketplace.py:381,464 only. DISCLOSED TO THE USER: No — the gate's wording implies exporting is covered.. WHY THIS TIER: The gate tells the founder 'Set a KPI on each before listing or exporting'. With no KPI set, POST /vsb/{id}/repo/ship returned shipped:true and GET /vsb/{id}/repo/zip returned 200. No surface says the gate covers the marketplace only, so the shortfall is invisible (not tier 3); the ship response's own figures are qualified ('written, not verified'), so nothing shown is false (not tier 1). REFUTER: Reproduced by execution on vsb-54c32fdef9. POST /marketplace/listings/from-entity -> 409 kpi_gate, '3 of 3 objective(s) carry no KPI ... Set a KPI on each before listing or exporting'. On the same entity POST /vsb/{id}/repo/ship -> 200 shipped:true across five surfaces, and GET /vsb/{id}/repo/zip -> 200 (29 KB). kpi_release_gate has exactly two call sites, both in marketplace.py (381, 464). Tier 2 stands: the listing half is delivered and honest; the export half is ungated and no surface says the gate is marketplace-only. Not tier 1 because 'before listing or exporting' is an instruction rather than a factual claim about the system, and the ship response qualifies itself ('written, not verified'); not tier 3 because the limit is stated nowhere. SMALLEST HONEST FIX: Either call kpi_release_gate on ship/zip, or state in the gate text and on the ship result that the KPI gate applies to marketplace release only.

items.title: Two registered spawner resources add a prompt stage and run no engine when composed
items.why: vsb_spawn and genesis_establish are in the fabric registry, selectable and described as spawners. The real-resource handler has no branch for either, so composing one adds a prompt stage and nothing is spawned. The Instrument Cell now reports them as prompt-stage only; the fabric's own list and its compose preview still present them as ordinary resources. Either give each a real handler, or say on the list and the preview what composing them does.

items.title: About sixty gateway call sites still do not say which text the person wrote
items.why: W640 flipped the floor's default to withholding. The domain tools, the journey, the cascade, the intelligence engines, the studio, the CEO chat and the composition runner now say; the rest (deliverables, products, change control, the digital twin, the VSB routes, the avatar and others) do not, so on the floor each tells its reader it was not told what they wrote. True, and less useful than it could be. The W640 floor guard prints the two counts; upgrade them in batches, reading each prompt to find the field the person typed.

items.title: Tests that save the single user's profile race each other across suite workers
items.why: Seven sites in the suite PUT or DELETE /api/v1/user/profile for the one unauthenticated user, and the four workers share one store. A test reading its 'no profile' state can run while another worker's profile exists; in W640's suite that turned the profile-verdict guard red with identical readings. The guard now removes the profile first, which narrows the window and does not close it. Give each such test its own user or its own store.

items.title: Shared floor notes say 'built from your request' on surfaces whose caller has not said what the person wrote
items.why: W640 made the floor attribute nothing to a person unless the caller names their words. For an upgraded caller the sentence is true; for the rest it is not. Either make each note conditional on the server's own statement, or upgrade the caller behind it.
